title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2. As a prerelease test, a team of 1,000 Fable 5.2 agents fully formalized Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 hours with minimal human intervention: they started from minimal prompts, organized their own coordination, and used no mathematical references beyond a list of intermediate theorem statements to score progress. The first formalization, by an unreleased research version of Claude, had taken 11 days with a purpose-built harness and human-researcher guidance. Fable 5.2 needed one-third of the action tokens and produced a proof seven times shorter, while Opus 5.5 with the same 1,000-agent setup completed 26% in 18 hours.
significance: A public model formalized Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 hours with minimal supervision, and its proof is far shorter than the human-guided first attempt — large agent teams can now run formalization at a scale and speed a single prover cannot.

title: Aaronson-Ambainis Conjecture proved! (By AI, of course)
summary: Scott Aaronson reports that the startup Physical Superintelligence has announced a proof of the Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture, which he and Andris Ambainis posed in 2009: every degree-d polynomial p from {0,1}^n to [0,1] in n Boolean variables, with constant variance, has some variable whose influence is at least 1/poly(d). The proof, obtained with a proprietary research harness on an internal Claude model and led by David Turturean and Jim Halverson, shows a variable of influence at least about 1/d^6. Aaronson says he believes it because there is a Lean certificate and human experts have already gone over it, and notes that it rules out one class of quantum speedup — yes-or-no problems relative to random oracles — not quantum supremacy in general.
significance: The conjecture implies there is no superpolynomial quantum query advantage over classical query complexity for decision problems on most Boolean inputs, which would answer a 1998 question of Fortnow and Rogers; its proof is another longstanding open problem settled by an AI system.

aiRole.description: Physical Superintelligence's proprietary research harness, run on an internal Claude model, produced a proof of the Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture showing a variable of influence at least about 1/d^6, backed by a Lean certificate.

humanContribution: David Turturean and Jim Halverson led the effort at Physical Superintelligence, human experts reviewed the proof, and Guy Blanc and colleagues wrote an exposition.

zh.title: Aaronson-Ambainis 猜想获证！（当然，是 AI 证的）
zh.summary: Scott Aaronson 报告称，初创公司 Physical Superintelligence 宣布证明了 Aaronson–Ambainis 猜想。该猜想由他与 Andris Ambainis 于 2009 年提出：任意定义在 n 个布尔变量上的次数为 d 的多项式 p:{0,1}^n→[0,1]，若方差为常数，则必有某个变量的影响至少为 1/poly(d)。这一证明由 David Turturean 与 Jim Halverson 主导，在一套专有研究框架上借助内部 Claude 模型得到，给出影响至少约为 1/d^6 的变量。Aaronson 表示，他相信证明成立，因为有 Lean 证书，且人类专家已经审阅过；并指出该结果排除的是一类量子加速——相对于随机 oracle 的是非判定问题——而非一般意义上的量子优越性。
zh.significance: 该猜想蕴含：对大多数布尔输入上的判定问题，量子查询复杂度相对经典查询复杂度不存在超多项式优势，这将回答 Fortnow 与 Rogers 于 1998 年提出的问题；其证明也成为一个被 AI 系统解决的长年未决问题。
zh.aiRoleDescription: Physical Superintelligence 的专有研究框架在内部 Claude 模型上运行，产出了 Aaronson–Ambainis 猜想的证明，给出影响至少约为 1/d^6 的变量，并有 Lean 证书作为支撑。
zh.humanContribution: David Turturean 与 Jim Halverson 在 Physical Superintelligence 主导了这项工作，人类专家审阅了证明，Guy Blanc 等人撰写了阐释文章。

title: Enhancing Mathematical Reasoning in Turkish Large Language Models with Search-Based Inference and Model Merging
summary: Turkish-Llama 8B-DPO is fine-tuned with LoRA on Turkish translations of MetaMath, NuminaMath and TigerLab, then combined with weight-space model merging and search-based inference. Data quality beats scale: Mix-30k is the best fine-tuned variant while large MetaMath underperforms; linear merging delivers the largest gains (GSM8K up to 0.63), Ties is modest and Breadcrumbs/Slerp degrade results. MCTS and Tree of Thoughts search improve mean LLM-judge scores for reasoning quality on a 0-100 scale. The stated limitations are machine translation, limited scale and search stochasticity.
significance: For a lower-resource language, a small well-curated translated corpus plus checkpoint merging can outperform more training data, and adding search at inference time improves reasoning quality beyond fine-tuning.

aiRole.description: The authors fine-tune Turkish-Llama 8B-DPO with LoRA, merge checkpoints and add MCTS and Tree of Thoughts search, reporting GSM8K scores up to 0.63 and higher mean LLM-judge reasoning-quality scores.

humanContribution: Humans selected and translated the training corpora, ran the LoRA fine-tuning and merging experiments, and evaluated the models with GSM8K and an LLM judge.

zh.title: 利用搜索式推理与模型合并提升土耳其语大模型的数学推理能力

title: Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI
summary: The authors build a quantum program library in Lean in which LLM agents synthesize novel programs against formal problem specifications and verify their correctness and cost, with agent teams collaborating through shared wikis and organized conferences. The automated discovery loop improves on prior baselines for parallel search by up to 1.4x, for quantum arithmetic by 290x, and for simulations relevant to fusion, photochemistry and drug metabolism by 11x, 8x and 2.5x.
significance: Because quantum algorithms can only be evaluated classically on restricted or small instances, a Lean library with machine-checked correctness and cost lets agents search program space beyond what today's computers can test.

aiRole.description: LLM agent teams synthesized and verified novel quantum programs inside a Lean library, improving baselines by up to 290x on quantum arithmetic and by 11x, 8x and 2.5x on fusion, photochemistry and drug-metabolism simulations.

humanContribution: Humans built the Lean quantum program library and its formal problem specifications, organized the agent teams with their wikis and conferences, and reviewed the resulting programs.

zh.title: 用 AI 发现经形式化验证的量子程序

zh.significance: 量子算法只能在受限或小规模实例上用经典计算机评估；有了经机器检验正确性与代价的 Lean 库，智能体便能搜索今天计算机无法测试的程序空间。

title: Test-Time Compute Scales Better with Parallel Agent Teams
summary: The paper compares ways to spend test-time compute when a verifier can score every attempt. Best-of-N sampling saturates quickly, and one large collaborating team scores higher but stops improving as it grows; parallel agent teams sample many small teams in parallel and keep the best team's result. With a 27B model and a budget of 100 agents, teams of ten beat parallel agents on 10 of 12 long-horizon tasks spanning GPU kernels, formal proofs and exploit development, beat one team of 100 on all four tasks where such a team was run, and at equal dollar cost beat a frontier model on half the tasks.
significance: A simple statistical model explains both failures — independent agents have a low sample mean, while a single large team gains no variance — so sampling many small teams balances the two and offers a better test-time scaling axis.

aiRole.description: Parallel agent teams of ten, run with a 27B model and a 100-agent budget, beat parallel independent agents on 10 of 12 long-horizon tasks including formal proofs, and at equal cost beat a frontier model on half the tasks.

humanContribution: Humans designed the parallel-team method and the statistical model of team size, and built the evaluation across GPU kernels, formal proofs and exploit-development tasks.

zh.title: 并行智能体团队能让测试时计算扩展得更好
zh.summary: 论文比较在验证器能给每次尝试打分时如何花费测试时计算。Best-of-N 采样很快饱和；单个大型协作团队得分更高，但规模变大后不再提升；并行智能体团队则并行采样许多小型团队并保留最佳团队的结果。在 270 亿参数模型、100 个智能体的预算下，十人小队在 12 项长周期任务（涵盖 GPU 内核、形式证明与漏洞利用开发）中于 10 项上胜过并行独立智能体，在运行过百人大团的全部 4 项任务上胜出，并在等额美元成本下于半数任务上超过前沿模型。
zh.significance: 一个简单的统计模型同时解释了两种失败：独立智能体样本均值偏低，单个大团队则无法获得方差收益；并行采样多个小团队在两者之间取得平衡，提供了更好的测试时扩展维度。
zh.aiRoleDescription: 在 270 亿参数模型与 100 个智能体的预算下，十人并行小队在 12 项长周期任务（含形式证明）中的 10 项胜过并行独立智能体，并在等额成本下于半数任务上超过前沿模型。
zh.humanContribution: 人类设计了并行团队方法及其团队规模的统计模型，并构建了涵盖 GPU 内核、形式证明与漏洞利用开发的评测。

title: Safety Is $Π_1$, Provability Is $Σ_1$: One Framework for the Hugging Face Breach and OpenAI's Mathematical Proofs
summary: The authors read two 2026 events — an agent-driven breach of Hugging Face and OpenAI's release of more than seven hundred AI-generated proof manuscripts — through a framework in which coding, proving and learning are one deductive mechanism distinguished by the premises they start from. Safety is a Π₁ statement, since it says no exploit exists and no finite list of passed tests can establish that, while provability is Σ₁, since one checked proof witnesses it. Using Turing's undecidability theorem they prove that attaching a statistical proposer to a deductive verifier does not change the undecidability result, however good the proposer is, and they discuss what does assure safety and where the residual risk goes.
significance: The logical form of the statement, not the quality of the proposer, decides what verification can certify: a single checked derivation settles a proof claim, while an absence claim has no finite witness.

zh.title: 安全性是 Π₁，可证性是 Σ₁：用一个框架同时解读 Hugging Face 入侵与 OpenAI 的数学证明
zh.summary: 作者用一个统一框架解读 2026 年的两件事——智能体入侵 Hugging Face，以及 OpenAI 发布七百多篇 AI 生成的证明手稿——该框架认为编码、证明与从数据中学习是同一种演绎机制，区别只在于所依据的前提。安全性是 Π₁ 陈述，因为它断言不存在漏洞利用，而任何有限的通过测试清单都无法确立这一点；可证性则是 Σ₁ 陈述，因为一份经检验的证明即可构成见证。借助图灵不可判定性定理，作者证明：把统计式提议者接到演绎验证器上，无论提议者多好，都不会改变不可判定性结论，并讨论了究竟什么才能保证安全、剩余风险落在何处。
zh.significance: 决定验证能担保什么的是陈述的逻辑形式，而不是提议者的水平：一份经检验的推导即可裁定可证性主张，而「不存在」类主张没有有限见证。

title: MIRA: Mitigating Pole Geometry Bias in Recurrent Language Models
summary: The paper shows that Transformer's recurrent successors — selective state-space models, RWKV and RetNet — can be characterized as infinite-impulse-response systems whose zero–pole geometry fixes the temporal modes they can represent, and that the algebraic structures adopted for parallelism often constrain poles to the real axis. Inspired by the lattice–ladder realization of general IIR systems, MIRA realizes a higher-order IIR block that can represent modes from both real and complex-conjugate poles. MirA-S, a 12-layer 0.14B-parameter model built entirely from MIRA blocks, pretrains to lower perplexity than strong recurrent baselines, generalizes beyond the training context length, and reaches higher throughput with a dedicated CUDA kernel.
significance: Treating recurrent architectures as IIR systems turns an architectural limitation into a pole-placement question, giving one mathematical language for comparing state-space, RWKV and RetNet-style models.

aiRole.description: MirA-S, a 12-layer 0.14B-parameter model built entirely from MIRA blocks, pretrained to lower perplexity than strong recurrent baselines, generalized beyond its training context length and ran at higher throughput with a dedicated CUDA kernel.

humanContribution: Humans derived the IIR characterization, designed the lattice–ladder MIRA block, pretrained MirA-S and wrote the CUDA kernel.

zh.title: MIRA：缓解循环语言模型中的极点几何偏差
zh.summary: 论文指出，Transformer 的循环后继架构——选择性状态空间模型、RWKV 与 RetNet——都可刻画为无限脉冲响应（IIR）系统，其零极点几何决定了可表示的时间模态；而为换取并行性所采用的参数化代数结构，往往把极点限制在实轴上。受一般 IIR 系统格型—梯形实现的启发，MIRA 用格型—梯形结构实现高阶 IIR 块，从而同时表示实极点与共轭复极点对应的模态。完全由 MIRA 块构成的 12 层、1.4 亿参数模型 MirA-S 在预训练中困惑度低于强循环基线，在超出训练长度的上下文上泛化更好，并借助专用 CUDA 内核获得更高吞吐。
zh.significance: 把循环架构视为 IIR 系统，可将架构上的限制转化为极点配置问题，为比较状态空间、RWKV 与 RetNet 类模型提供统一的数学语言。
zh.aiRoleDescription: 完全由 MIRA 块构成的 12 层、1.4 亿参数模型 MirA-S 预训练后困惑度低于强循环基线，在超出训练长度的上下文上泛化更好，并借助专用 CUDA 内核获得更高吞吐。
zh.humanContribution: 人类推导了 IIR 刻画，设计了格型—梯形 MIRA 块，预训练了 MirA-S 并编写了 CUDA 内核。

title: LeanDojo-v2: A Comprehensive Library for AI-Assisted Theorem Proving in Lean
summary: LeanDojo-v2 unifies repository data extraction, LLM fine-tuning, proof search, AI autocompletion and LLM-assisted theorem proving in one open library for Lean. title: All roads lead to Markov kernel networks: A representation theorem for discretization-stable learning
summary: The paper formalizes uniform discretization stability, a quantitative refinement of discretization invariance: a Hölder bound relates changes in an operator's output to the Wasserstein distance between the probability-measure representations of input functions and their discretizations. Its representation theorem shows that every uniformly discretization-stable operator can be written exactly as a stable Markov kernel network — a joint generalization of transformers, Fourier neural operators, Flowers and other learned operators — and that the read kernels can be realized as solutions of regularized variational problems recovering those architectures as special cases. Designing a new architecture then becomes a question of which parts of a Markov kernel network to parameterize.
significance: One representation theorem covers several successful learned operators and turns discretization stability into a design constraint expressed as a variational problem instead of a property checked after training.

zh.title: 殊途同归：面向离散化稳定学习的马尔可夫核网络表示定理
zh.summary: 论文形式化了「一致离散化稳定性」，这是离散化不变性的定量加强版：它以 Hölder 界把算子输出的变化与输入函数及其离散化作为概率测度表示之间的 Wasserstein 距离联系起来。其表示定理表明，任何一致离散化稳定的算子都可精确写成一个稳定马尔可夫核网络——它同时推广了 Transformer、傅里叶神经算子（FNO）、Flowers 等成功的可学习算子；论文还证明这些网络的读取核可作为正则化变分问题的解来实现，特定代价与正则项即可还原上述各类架构。由此，设计新架构就变成选择对马尔可夫核网络的哪些部分做参数化。
zh.significance: 一条表示定理覆盖了多种成功的可学习算子，并把离散化稳定性从训练后检验的性质，变成以变分问题表述的设计约束。

title: Random Symbolic Boosting: A Geometric Approach to Symbolic Regression
summary: Random Symbolic Boosting builds explicit additive symbolic models by boosting over populations of randomly generated syntax trees, treating tree semantics as vectors so no generational evolution is needed. For ordinary least squares the boosting process guarantees a monotone reduction of training error in both regression and classification, and an adaptive geometric early-stopping rule based on the angle between prediction and target vectors needs no per-task tuning. On a standard symbolic-regression benchmark the method sits at the Pareto-optimal point between accuracy and training time and ranks first on the real-world datasets, and it is competitive on a 200-problem tabular classification benchmark.
significance: Replacing generational evolution with boosting over random trees keeps symbolic models interpretable while removing most of the evolutionary search cost, which shows up as a better accuracy–time trade-off.

zh.title: 随机符号提升：符号回归的几何方法
zh.summary: 随机符号提升（RSB）通过对随机生成的语法树种群做提升（boosting）来构造显式的加性符号模型，并把语法树语义直接当作向量处理，从而无需代际演化。对普通最小二乘，该提升过程在回归与分类中都保证训练误差单调下降；一种基于预测向量与目标向量夹角的几何早停机制与问题尺度无关，也无需在不同任务间调参。在标准符号回归基准上，该方法处于预测精度与训练时间的 Pareto 最优点，并在真实数据集上排名第一；在包含 200 个问题的表格分类基准上也具有竞争力。
zh.significance: 以随机树上的提升替代代际演化，在保留符号模型可解释性的同时去掉了大部分演化搜索开销，体现为更优的精度—时间权衡。

title: The Gold Rush in AI4Math, II: What are signatures of AI-assisted Proofs?
summary: The authors build five cohorts of 8,281 papers — historical arXiv papers, recent papers that disclose substantive AI use, manuscripts released by OpenAI, and AI-generated and AI-reworded papers matched to the same research problems — and introduce ProofTrace, which represents each paper as a graph of immediate proof support (GIPS) and extracts interpretable features of mathematical organization. Principal-component projections show a gradient of AI involvement: reworded papers stay close to human papers, the two AI-generated cohorts depart in broadly shared directions, and disclosing papers sit in between and shift toward the generated cohorts over time. Recurring signatures of AI-generated proofs include fewer externally cited results, greater reliance on intermediate conclusions and altered graph connectivity, many of which persist under controls for field, length or graph size. ProofTrace distinguishes human-written from disclosing papers stably under AI rewording, where text-based detectors degrade sharply.
significance: If AI involvement leaves structural traces in how a proof is organized, provenance checks can use the proof graph rather than stylometry, which rewording defeats.

zh.title: AI4Math 淘金热 II：AI 辅助证明有哪些特征？
zh.summary: 作者构建了五个共 8,281 篇论文的队列——历史 arXiv 论文、近期披露实质性使用 AI 的论文、OpenAI 发布的手稿，以及针对同一研究问题匹配生成的 AI 论文与 AI 改写论文——并提出 ProofTrace：把每篇论文表示为「直接证明支撑图」（GIPS），提取可解释的数学组织特征。主成分投影显示出 AI 参与的梯度：AI 改写论文与人类论文接近，两个 AI 生成队列朝大致相同的方向偏离，披露使用 AI 的论文处于中间并随时间向生成队列移动。AI 生成证明反复出现的特征包括引用外部结果更少、更依赖中间结论以及图连通性改变；在控制领域、篇幅或图规模后，许多特征依然存在。在 AI 改写条件下，ProofTrace 仍能区分人类论文与披露使用 AI 的论文，而当前基于文本的检测器性能急剧下降。
zh.significance: 如果 AI 参与会在证明的组织方式上留下结构性痕迹，来源核查就可以依赖证明图而非文体计量，因为改写会让后者失效。

title: LeanContext: Disentangling Mathematical Resources from Local Formal Context in Lean Whole-Proof Generation
summary: LeanContext is a benchmark of 129,826 Lean whole-proof-generation problems that separates selected complete preceding mathematical declarations (Mathematical Context) from the remaining selected local source commands (Environment Context), with four aligned input views for crossed training and inference evaluation under the original Lean verification environments. Selected declarations outperform comparable alternatives by a larger margin when training includes Mathematical Context, for both diffusion- and autoregressive-based models, and auditing final inputs for omitted declarations improves Pass@32 by 1.40% for LLaDA and 1.70% for Llama on 2,000 targets.
significance: The split between mathematical resources and local formal context makes the value of retrieved declarations measurable, and the audit shows that silently dropped dependencies account for part of the gap.

zh.title: LeanContext：在 Lean 整体证明生成中分离数学资源与局部形式上下文
zh.summary: LeanContext 是一个包含 129,826 个 Lean 整体证明生成问题的基准，把选定的完整前置数学声明归为「数学上下文」（MC），把其余选定的本地源命令归为「环境上下文」（EC），并提供四种对齐的输入视图，用于在原始 Lean 验证环境下做交叉训练与推理评估。对扩散模型与自回归模型，当训练包含 MC 时，选定声明的优势比可比替代更大；对最终输入做审计以找出被遗漏的声明后，LLaDA 与 Llama 在 2,000 个目标上的 Pass@32 分别提升 1.40% 与 1.70%。
zh.significance: 把数学资源与局部形式上下文分开，使检索到的声明价值可以被度量；审计还表明，被静默丢弃的依赖解释了一部分差距。

title: Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench: The First Agentic and Verifiable Benchmark for Mathematical Modeling
summary: TB-MathModel covers 18 real CUMCM and MCM modeling problems from 2023–2025, each shipping its verbatim statement, official attachments and figures in a containerized terminal; the agent returns one JSON artifact scored on the numeric core of the final question. Two design choices define it: direction-aware, one-sided scoring that never penalises beating the anchor, and two-layer feasibility verification — a programmatic gate over six decidable invariant forms plus 624 Lean 4 obligations — that zeroes infeasible answers, with every task scored against a panel of human outstanding papers rather than one. Across seven multimodal entries with three seeds each, the strongest reach a multi-reference O-Eval of 64.58%, while a $2.54 open model holds 59.81% at 1/100 the cost.
significance: Scoring the numeric core against multiple outstanding papers with a feasibility gate makes modeling results machine-checkable, instead of trusting an LLM judge over whole reports.

zh.title: 终端式数学建模基准：首个面向数学建模的智能体化可验证基准
zh.summary: TB-MathModel 收录 2023–2025 年的 18 道真实 CUMCM 与 MCM 建模题，每题在容器化终端中提供原始题面、官方附件与图表；智能体返回单个 JSON 产物，按最终问题的数值核心评分。两个设计使其区别于既有基准：方向感知的单侧评分，不会因超过锚定值而扣分；以及两层可行性验证——对六类可判定不变式做程序化门槛检查，加上 624 条 Lean 4 义务——不可行答案直接判零；每题对照一组人类优秀论文而非单篇评分。在七个多模态模型（各三个随机种子）中，最强者的多参考 O-Eval 达到 64.58%，而成本 2.54 美元的开源模型以百分之一的成本取得 59.81%。
zh.significance: 以可行性门槛对多篇优秀论文的数值核心评分，使数学建模结果可被机器检验，而不再依赖 LLM 裁判对整篇报告打分。

title: TCSExam: Evaluating Frontier LLMs on the Full Range of TCS Research
summary: TCSExam is a framework and benchmark covering the full range of theoretical computer science research: theorem proving, solver engineering and constructions, alongside direct attempts to resolve open conjectures, with submissions checked by the Lean kernel or an executable task checker. TCSExam-Full has 100 expert-reviewed tasks and TCSExam-Lite 20 (five per track), reducing task attempts by 80% at the same per-attempt budget. Evaluating eight agents on Full and nine on Lite, the TCSExam Index has GPT-6 Astra leading Full at 71.9 and Opus 5.5 leading Lite at 72.3, the two rankings align strongly across eight shared agents (Spearman ρ=0.93), and the evaluations produced improved solver outputs and constructions plus independently verified special cases and bounds from open-conjecture attempts.
significance: A four-track benchmark with kernel- or checker-verified submissions measures progress on TCS research itself, including partial progress on open conjectures, and the Lite split preserves the Full ranking at a fifth of the attempts.

zh.title: TCSExam：在理论计算机科学研究的完整范围内评测前沿大模型

title: zkARc: Succinctly Verifiable Proofs for Neurosymbolic Natural Language Formalization and Verification
summary: zkARc wraps each stage of Automated Reasoning checks (ARc) — the planner's output, the policy's formalization, the action's formalization and both solver queries — in an independent, succinctly verifiable zero-knowledge proof, producing a receipt bound to the exact action received that reveals nothing beyond the declared public information and the verdict. The authors prove completeness, knowledge soundness and zero knowledge for the composed receipt under explicit assumptions. An implementation on Qwen2-0.5B enforces a spending policy end to end, approving two purchases and denying a third; a full receipt, which also proves model inference, takes about an hour to issue with CPU-only proving and verifies in under a minute, while the solver proof alone is 88 KiB and verifies in 0.3 seconds.
significance: Proof-carrying enforcement lets a third party check that a declared policy was applied without re-running the pipeline or trusting the operator, which ordinary middleware guardrails cannot provide.

aiRole.description: zkARc's neurosymbolic pipeline certifies the planner output, policy and action formalizations and solver queries with zero-knowledge proofs, enforcing a spending policy end to end on Qwen2-0.5B by approving two purchases and denying a third.

humanContribution: Humans designed the proof-carrying framework, stated and proved its completeness, knowledge soundness and zero-knowledge properties, and built the end-to-end implementation.

title: Formally verifying agent-written full-stack web apps with PDD Kit
summary: PDD Kit addresses AI-generated code that is too large to review line by line: it converts developer intent into a Verus specification, proves that the generated code meets it for every input, and falls back to tests where proofs are not practical. Developers then review intent rather than every line, which the Microsoft Research post presents as a way to keep agent-written full-stack web apps doing what the developer intended.
significance: Moving review from every line of code to a proved specification pairs agent code generation with machine-checked intent, addressing the scale of generated code rather than only its correctness.

title: Autonomous AI Agents Systematically Diverge From Human Preferences in Proof Formalization
summary: The authors present 'simulated collaboration', a method for asking how AI agents and humans differ in pursuing a proof-formalization task, applied to nine major human collaborations in Lean with 4.7M definitions across more than 6K commits. Over the course of proof construction, AI agents are far more strongly drawn than humans to explicitly marked gaps, show relative aversion to densely connected proof centers and to complex or surprising proof goals, and are relatively attracted to surprising proof bodies, which they tend to regularize toward baseline.
significance: The measured preference gaps locate where AI formalization departs from human practice, identifying blind spots and possible interventions for human–AI collaboration in mathematics.

title: Give Up to Get More: Priors, Not Policies, Govern Test-Time Compute Allocation
summary: The paper shows that the common difficulty-proportional rule for allocating repeated LLM attempts captures half or more of the oracle gain on benchmarks a model mostly solves, but at most 13% on hard workloads, even given true pass rates. Because the value of one more attempt peaks at intermediate difficulty, the optimal static allocation is an inverted U that gives little to inputs hopeless at the current budget. In a survey of 221 LLM allocation papers, at least 13 give the hardest inputs the most attempts. With a verifier and a prior from a related model's past runs on the same inputs, Thompson Sampling raises the solved share on the hardest workload from 14% to 27%; without such a prior no tested policy beats round-robin, and the gain vanishes between prior rank correlations of about 0.3 and 0.55.
significance: Information about which inputs are solvable, not the allocation policy, drives the gain, which redirects effort from policy design toward priors and verifier quality.

aiRole.description: Thompson Sampling with a prior from a related model's past runs raised the solved share on the hardest workload from 14% to 27%, while without such a prior no tested policy beat round-robin.

humanContribution: Humans surveyed 221 allocation papers, ran the experiments on public math, code and formal-proof samples, and turned the findings into a decision guide.

zh.title: 以退为进：决定测试时计算分配的是先验，而不是策略
zh.summary: 论文表明，常见的「难题多给尝试」规则在模型大多能解的基准上可取得 oracle 增益的一半以上，但在困难负载上最多只有 13%，即便已知真实通过率。由于多一次尝试的价值在中等难度处最高，最优的静态分配呈倒 U 形，对在当前预算下无望的输入几乎不投入。在 221 篇 LLM 分配论文的调查中，至少 13 篇把最多尝试给最难的输入。在具备验证器、且能用相关模型在同一批输入上的历史运行作为先验时，Thompson Sampling 把最难负载上的已解决比例从 14% 提升到 27%；没有这样的先验时，所测试的任何策略都不优于轮转，而增益在先验秩相关约 0.3 到 0.55 之间消失。

title: Formalizing inverse problems in the age of AI: possibilities, pitfalls, and an invitation
summary: The authors describe AutoIP, a Lean library in which classical linear regularization theory and the functional analysis it rests on have been autoformalized by AI agents, and organize it around the human task that machine-checked proofs leave open: confirming that each formal statement says what was intended. A reviewer compares formal statements with their natural-language counterparts and never needs to read a proof. The authors report that the risks lie in the statements rather than in the proofs, illustrating this with a textbook theorem whose hypothesis is more restrictive than asserted, and invite the inverse-problems community to extend the library.
significance: For an autoformalized library, statement review becomes the bottleneck and the place where errors survive; simple automated tests on statements can expose problems even in established literature.

aiRole.description: AI agents autoformalized classical linear regularization theory and its functional analysis as the Lean library AutoIP, and automated tests on the statements exposed a textbook theorem whose hypothesis was more restrictive than asserted.

humanContribution: Humans designed the library around statement review, compared formal statements with their natural-language counterparts, and wrote the automated statement tests.

title: ReSI-Math: Exploring Recoverable Capability Frontiers for Efficient Reasoning Improvement
summary: ReSI-Math is a framework that targets a "recoverable capability frontier": problems a policy fails to solve by direct decoding but can solve via trajectory-level search. It uses Self-Judge-guided evolutionary search to surface such recoverable failures and adaptively selects frontier problems for sequential RLVR, turning recovered capability into data-efficient supervision. On Qwen3-VL-8B, correct-incorrect trajectory crossover yielded 272 verifier-confirmed correct offspring from 621 attempts (43.8%); three sequential one-shot RLVR stages raised the MATH500 and WE-MATH average from 78.71 to 80.16, and under matched single-problem RLVR, frontier-guided Q1 reached 54.16 versus 53.31 for random selection.
significance: Separating genuine incapability from recoverable failure changes how supervision budget is allocated in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. The reported gains suggest that selecting problems near the recoverable frontier produces more sample-efficient mathematical reasoning improvement than random or untargeted problem selection.

aiRole.description: ReSI-Math, a framework using Self-Judge-guided evolutionary search and sequential RLVR, produced verifier-confirmed correct trajectories and benchmark gains on Qwen3-VL-8B (e.g., MATH500 and WE-MATH average improving from 78.71 to 80.16).

humanContribution: Humans built and designed the ReSI-Math framework, defined the search and RLVR training pipeline, and evaluated the resulting benchmarks.

zh.title: ReSI-Math：探索可恢复能力前沿以实现高效推理改进
zh.summary: ReSI-Math 是一个面向数学推理（mathematical reasoning）的框架，其目标是识别"可恢复能力前沿"，即策略在直接解码时无法解决、但通过轨迹级搜索可以解决的问题。该框架采用 Self-Judge-guided evolutionary search 挖掘此类可恢复的失败案例，并随策略演化自适应地挑选前沿问题进行序列式基于可验证奖励的强化学习（RLVR），把被恢复的能力转化为数据高效的监督信号。在 Qwen3-VL-8B 上，正误轨迹交叉在 621 次尝试中产生了 272 个经验证器确认正确的后代（43.8%）；三个序列式 one-shot RLVR 阶段使 MATH500 与 WE-MATH 的平均分从 78.71 提升到 80.16；在匹配的单题 RLVR 设置下，前沿引导的 Q1 达到 54.16，而随机选择仅为 53.31。

title: Formalizing PTX in Lean to Prove GPU Kernel Correctness
summary: The paper presents a mathematical formalization of PTX, designed to model and reason about patterns common in deep learning GPU kernels, including acquire-release semantics, tensor cores, proxies, asynchronous operations, multi-kernel pipelines, and data-dependent control flow. significance: GPU kernel correctness is difficult to establish by testing alone, especially for concurrency and pipeline patterns used in deep learning. title: Whiel: A Neurosymbolic Platform for Certified Relational Program Verification
summary: Whiel is a system for Lean-certified reasoning about imperative relational programs, encoding containment and equivalence problems for Datalog, its extensions with negation and the core fragment of graph query languages, plus optimized or incremental evaluation algorithms and first-order specifications of integrity constraints, schema mappings and views. title: Structured Priors: Towards an algebra of component priors for prior-data fitted networks
summary: This work replaces the hand-built synthetic generators used to train prior-data fitted networks with a structured prior: a small named set of component priors linked by five operators (mixture, convolution, amplitude scaling, local transform, projection) whose algebraic laws are formally proven within a measure-theoretic framework and implemented in the macl2l package. Experiments show the implemented generators reproduce the stated identities at permutation-test resolution, and that trained networks obey the distributive law. A mixed prior of small components matches or beats every individual component on seven of eight open regression benchmarks, and on two tables a structured prior reaches with one ninth of the data budget an error that a generic random-function prior does not reach at full budget. A theorem on model averaging shows that component networks that are Bayes predictors for their priors yield the Bayes predictor for the mixture, but a pre-registered test with trained component networks failed because the networks rarely identified the generating component.
significance: The approach turns the ad hoc mixture weights used in systems such as TabPFN, Mitra, and TabICLv2 into a compositional algebra with proven laws and tested behavior, making generator design more principled and inspectable. The benchmark gains suggest structured priors are competitive with much larger data budgets, while the failed pre-registered averaging test pinpoints component identification as a concrete obstacle for future work on the algebra of structured priors.

zh.title: 结构化先验：迈向先验数据拟合网络的组件先验代数
zh.summary: 本研究提出用结构化先验（structured prior）替代训练先验数据拟合网络（prior-data fitted networks）时手工构建的合成生成器：一个由少量具名组件先验构成的集合，通过五种算子相连接，即混合（mixture）、卷积（convolution）、振幅缩放（amplitude scaling）、局部变换（local transform）和投影（projection），其代数定律在测度论（measure-theoretic）框架下得到形式化证明，并在 macl2l 软件包中实现。实验表明，所实现的生成器在置换检验（permutation test）的分辨率范围内重现了这些恒等式，且训练后的网络服从分配律（distributive law）。由小组件构成的混合先验在八个开放回归基准（regression benchmarks）中的七个上与最优单个组件持平或更优；在其中两个数据表上，结构化先验仅用九分之一的数据预算就达到通用随机函数先验（random-function prior）用满预算仍未达到的误差。关于模型平均（model averaging）的定理表明，若各组件网络分别是其对应先验的贝叶斯预测器，则它们构成该混合先验的贝叶斯预测器；但用已训练组件网络进行的预注册检验未能成功，因为网络识别生成组件的频率过低。
zh.significance: 该方法把 TabPFN、Mitra、以及 TabICLv2 等系统中随意设定的混合权重，转变为一套具有已证定律与实测行为的组合代数，使生成器设计更加有原则、更可检查。基准结果表明结构化先验在小得多的数据预算下即具竞争力，而预注册的平均预测器检验失败则把组件识别明确为该结构化先验代数后续研究的具体障碍。
zh.aiRoleDescription: 该工作提出一种结构化先验，并形式化证明其代数定律；实验表明，训练后的 prior-data fitted networks 服从分配律，混合先验网络在八个回归基准中的七个上达到或超过单个组件网络。论文还给出模型平均定理，但其预注册检验在训练后的组件网络上未通过。

title: ProofPaths: An AI Agent Framework for Assessing Student Reasoning
summary: ProofPaths is an AI agent framework for assessing student reasoning that combines rubric-based grading with individualized, interactive interviews. Multiple grading agents score a submission against instructor guidance, exchange critiques, and revise their judgments; their scores determine which review supplies the grade and feedback. An interview agent asks students to justify steps in their submissions and uses their answers to guide follow-up questions, with each question linked to a retrieved submission excerpt so instructors can compare the explanation with the cited passage. The system tracks assessment progress and stores grading reviews and interview transcripts, while deterministic tests of the assessment controllers check source handling, score aggregation, and limits on correction attempts. Instructors can inspect all reviews and transcripts and override grades within the assignment workflow.
significance: The framework addresses the gap between producing a correct solution and demonstrating an understanding of its reasoning, while reducing the recurring staff effort of individualized interviews. Its multi-agent critique-and-revision process, evidence-linked interview questions, and tested assessment controllers give instructors auditable artifacts and direct control over grades.

title: What makes a theorem interesting? Operationalizing interestingness for open-ended exploration
summary: The paper studies what makes mathematical theorems interesting by observing which results mathematicians single out in formal libraries and in papers. Each form of selection is modeled as an evaluator weighting features of a result's statement, proof, and dependencies, with weights split into a shared and a subjective part. In formalized mathematics, ex-ante features predict these selections as well as a large language-model judge, and the two are complementary. Interestingness is largely shared: one weight set, carried mainly by structural features such as statement length, proof length, and the subfields a proof draws on, explains most of the signal and transfers partly across formal libraries. The remaining subjective variation depends more on practices and individual authors than on subfields. The judge's advantage lies in its knowledge of the canon, and neither the judge nor the features rely on memory of the papers. The approach, which infers what a community finds interesting from what it singles out, can be applied to other sciences.
significance: For agents that generate conjectures or research ideas and must decide which to keep, this work offers an empirically grounded alternative to hand-picked proxies or language-model judges. It shows that lightweight structural features match a large language-model judge and transfer across formal libraries, reveals a largely shared structure of human mathematical interest, and provides a method that generalizes to other sciences.

zh.title: 什么让定理有趣？为开放式探索将有趣性操作化
zh.summary: 本文通过观察数学家在形式库和论文中挑选哪些结果，研究数学定理（theorem）的有趣性。作者将每种挑选方式建模为一个评估器，对结果陈述、证明及依赖关系的特征赋予权重，并将权重分为共享部分和主观部分。在形式化数学（formalized mathematics）中，事前特征对这些挑选的预测能力与大型语言模型评审器相当，且两者互补。有趣性在很大程度上是共享的：一组主要由结构性特征（陈述长度、证明长度、证明所涉及的子领域）承载的权重解释了大部分信号，并能部分迁移到不同形式库。剩余的主观差异更多取决于研究实践和具体作者，而非子领域。评审器的优势在于其对经典文献的掌握，且评审器与特征都不依赖对论文的记忆。该方法从共同体所挑选的结果中推断其兴趣所在，可推广到其他科学领域。
zh.significance: 对于生成猜想（conjecture）或研究想法并需决定保留哪些结果的智能体，本文提供了有经验依据的判断方法，可替代手工挑选的代理指标或语言模型评审器。研究表明轻量的结构性特征可与大型语言模型评审器比美并能跨形式库迁移，揭示了人类数学兴趣的共享结构，并给出了可推广到其他科学领域的方法。

title: TLAPS-Bench: Formally Proving Correctness of Real-World System Specifications with TLA+ Proof System
summary: TLAPS-Bench is a benchmark and execution harness for building machine-checked proofs of real-world TLA+ system specifications with agentic AI. It supports iterative proof development atop the TLA+ Proof System (TLAPS), equipping agents with proof tools and libraries plus safeguards against reward hacking. The benchmark contains 265 proof targets, each encoding a property to prove, drawn from 95 TLA+ specifications of real-world systems. On a subset of 70 targets across 12 specifications, the highest-scoring model, GPT-6.1 Sol (max), proved 31 (44.3%). Using the harness, the team also proved previously unproved properties of important specifications spanning cache coherence, Byzantine consensus, and write-ahead logs.
significance: It makes machine-checked proof development over realistic system specifications testable at scale, targeting the hard subproblems of inductive invariant discovery, state-transition reasoning, and proof decomposition while guarding against reward hacking. The 44.3% result quantifies the remaining gap in end-to-end proof development, and the harness enables continued iterative proof work on unproved real-system properties.

title: Math Foundation Formalization Agent: A General-Purpose Approach to Formalizing Mathematical Foundations
summary: This paper presents MFF-Agent, a general-purpose agent that combines large language model reasoning with the formal verification capabilities of the Rocq proof assistant. It incorporates task classification, tool-assisted execution, verification feedback, and state-based task management to support the generation, refinement, and verification of formal proofs. Rather than targeting a single theory, the agent is evaluated through case studies on Morse–Kelley axiomatic set theory (MK), real numbers, propositional logic, and equivalences of the axiom of choice, distinguishing source-level completion, interactive verification, and reproducible compilation. The results demonstrate the feasibility of a unified operational framework for heterogeneous foundation-level tasks and clarify the gap between such a framework and a fully integrated mathematical foundation.
significance: The work supplies evidence that a single agent architecture can serve formalization tasks across multiple mathematical foundations, while also delineating what remains missing before such tooling becomes a fully integrated formalization pipeline.

humanContribution: Humans designed and built the agent, integrating task classification, tool-assisted execution, verification feedback and state-based task management, and examined its behavior through the case studies while distinguishing source-level completion, interactive verification and reproducible compilation.

title: Stop Handcrafting Your Engine! GenDB-V: Towards AI-Generated and Formally Verified Database Systems
summary: GenDB-V is a system that lets AI agents synthesize database engines specialized to given hardware and workloads while producing formal proofs of correctness. It introduces SQLSpec, a formalization of SQL semantics that deterministically constructs fixed, implementation-agnostic synthesis targets; it jointly synthesizes fast code and proofs via storage-execution co-optimization, performance-first exploration, and three-layer modular proofs bridging low-level execution to SQLSpec semantics; and it checks the synthesized code and proofs against the fixed targets in an isolated pipeline, establishing SQL correctness and program safety. On TPC-H and SEC-EDGAR, verified template implementations reach geometric-mean speedups of 22.0-61.3x over DuckDB and Umbra, a verified general-purpose engine gains 1.27-3.4x on TPC-H, and GenDB-V outperforms a testing-based LLM synthesis method whose implementations return incorrect answers for 16 of 28 templates.
significance: It addresses the repeated cost of rebuilding database engines as hardware and workloads change, and the persistence of wrong-answer bugs in mature engines, by pairing hardware- and workload-specialized performance with machine-checked correctness. The reported speedups and the incorrect answers exposed in the testing-based baseline suggest that AI-generated, formally verified engines are a serious alternative to handcrafted ones.

aiRole.description: GenDB-V uses AI agents to synthesize database engine implementations together with formal proofs of SQL correctness and program safety, achieving 22.0-61.3x geometric-mean speedups over DuckDB and Umbra on verified TPC-H template implementations and 1.27-3.4x on a verified general-purpose engine.

humanContribution: Humans designed the GenDB-V framework, formalized SQL semantics in SQLSpec, built the synthesis and isolated verification pipelines, and audited and tested the synthesized implementations.

title: Reap: Uncovering Monte Carlo proof search with a lightweight model
summary: Reap is an open framework for learning and analyzing formal proof search in Lean4. It implements policy-value-guided Monte Carlo tree search directly in Lean, sharing proof-state transitions, AND-OR search, and replay verification between inference and training rollouts, while structured action logs reveal how neural predictions interact with tactic execution. Using the framework, the authors train Reaper-1, a 1.7B-parameter policy-value model, through continued pre-training, supervised tactic learning, and iterative search-based reinforcement learning. With a separate premise selector, the system solves 79.9% of miniF2F-test at pass@32, the best result among open provers of comparable size and competitive with much larger models. The results suggest reinforcement learning helps the prover organize proofs around useful intermediate results, favoring substantial advances over repeated local adjustments, and producing longer tactic programs where fewer explicit search decisions each carry more work.
significance: Reap offers an open, inspectable pipeline for studying proof search, connecting training-time reinforcement learning to observable changes in search strategy. The observed shift toward fewer search decisions with heavier tactic execution clarifies the trade-off between search effort and tactic cost, giving researchers and tool builders concrete evidence of how learning reshapes the prover's problem-solving behavior.

zh.title: Reap：用轻量模型揭示蒙特卡洛证明搜索
zh.summary: Reap 是一个用于学习和分析 Lean4 中形式化证明搜索的开放框架。它直接在 Lean 中实现策略-价值引导（policy-value-guided）的蒙特卡洛树搜索（Monte Carlo Tree Search），在推理与训练的 rollout 之间共享证明状态转移、与-或搜索（AND-OR search）和回放验证，同时通过结构化动作日志揭示神经预测与策略执行的相互作用。研究者使用该框架训练了 1.7B 参数的策略-价值模型 Reaper-1，训练过程包括继续预训练、监督式策略学习和迭代的基于搜索的强化学习（reinforcement learning）。配合独立的前提选择器（premise selector），该系统在 pass@32 下解决 miniF2F-test 的 79.9%，在规模相当的开放证明器（prover）中表现最佳，并与更大的模型具有竞争力。结果表明，强化学习有助于证明器围绕有用的中间结果组织证明，倾向于取得实质性推进而非反复的局部微调，并生成更长的策略程序：显式的搜索决策更少，而每个决策中完成的工作更多。
zh.significance: Reap 提供了一条开放且可检视的流水线，用于研究证明搜索，把训练阶段的强化学习与搜索策略的可观察变化联系起来。观察到的从更多搜索决策转向更少决策、但每次决策承担更多策略执行的变化，澄清了搜索开销与策略执行成本之间的权衡，为研究者和工具开发者提供了学习如何改变证明器解题行为的具体证据。

title: LEANGUARD: Lean-Verified Guardrails for Tool-Using Agents
summary: LeanGuard is a runtime that checks every proposed tool call by a language-model agent against policies written in Lean4 before execution. Policies combine state predicates with scoped past-time temporal operators over execution history, evaluation is fail-closed, and the decision procedure is proved equivalent to a LeanLTL semantics. Denied calls can be repaired either by giving the agent the violated rule and a hint, or by proof-guided repair, where Lean metaprogramming searches for a nearby call preserving user intent and proves the policy admits it, without using the model. On Tau-Bench with five Qwen models (0.8B-27B), unguarded agents made at least 33 policy-violating calls while LeanGuard made none, with no significant change in task success under feedback. On DTap, direct prompt-injection success fell from 57.9% to 5.9%, and benign success in a telecom setting was unchanged. Feedback reduced repeated blocked calls and raised task success for four of five models over bare denial; on replayed denials, repair proved an admissible edit for 88 of 252 argument-value denials in a median of 2 ms.
significance: Tool-using agents face a gap between natural-language intent and enforceable action constraints; LeanGuard shows that machine-checked policies can close this gap at runtime with zero policy-violating executions in the reported benchmarks, while maintaining task performance and resisting prompt injection. The equivalence proof between the decision procedure and the LeanLTL semantics ties the guardrail to a verified formal foundation, and the proof-guided repair mode demonstrates an agentic use of Lean metaprogramming that produces policy-compliant edits with minimal latency, offering a practical route to verifiable agent safety.

zh.title: LeanGuard：面向工具使用型智能体的 Lean 验证护栏
zh.summary: LeanGuard 是一个运行时系统，在语言模型智能体的每个拟执行工具调用到达环境之前，依据用 Lean4 编写的策略对其进行检查。策略将状态谓词与执行历史上的限定范围过去时序算子（past-time temporal operators）相结合，求值采用失败即拒绝的方式，且该判定过程已被证明等价于一种 LeanLTL 语义。被拒绝的调用可通过两种方式修复：一种是反馈方式，即向智能体提供被违反的规则与提示；另一种是证明引导的修复，即由 Lean 元编程在不借助模型的情况下搜索一个保持用户意图的邻近调用，并证明策略允许该调用。在 Tau-Bench 上使用五个 Qwen 模型（0.8B-27B）进行评测时，无护栏的智能体执行了至少 33 次策略所禁止的调用，而 LeanGuard 一次也未执行，且在反馈方式下任务成功率无显著变化。在 DTap 上，直接提示注入（prompt-injection）的成功率从 57.9% 降至 5.9%；在无需写操作即可完成良性任务的电信场景中，良性任务成功率保持不变。相比仅拒绝，反馈方式减少了重复被拦截的调用，并在五个模型中的四个上提升了任务成功率。在重放的被拒调用中，对于 252 次由参数取值引起的拒绝，修复在其中 88 次上证明了一个可接受的编辑，中位耗时 2 毫秒。
zh.significance: 工具使用型智能体长期面临自然语言意图与可强制执行的行为约束之间的落差；LeanGuard 表明，经机器检查的策略可在运行时弥合这一落差，在所报告的基准测试中实现了零次违反策略的执行，同时保持了任务性能并抵御了提示注入。判定过程与 LeanLTL 语义的等价性证明将护栏建立在经过验证的形式化基础之上，而证明引导的修复模式展示了 Lean 元编程的一种智能体式应用，能够以极低延迟产出符合策略的编辑，为可验证的智能体安全性提供了切实可行的路径。

title: Action Verification through Conjecture and Refutation for Language Model Agents
summary: The paper introduces BlackSwan, a refutation-oriented "expect-suspect-test" procedure for verifying the actions of language model agents before execution. For each state-mutating action, BlackSwan predicts the intended effect, formulates specific and empirically testable hypotheses for how the action could be wrong, and tests them using existing observations or additional non-mutating actions, executing the action only if no hypothesis survives. On challenging AppWorld tasks, BlackSwan improves success rate over the strongest baseline by 14.9 and 25.2%p with and without the backbone model's thinking mode, respectively, and even without thinking mode or in-context demonstrations it outperforms stronger baselines equipped with them. The gains transfer beyond AppWorld, improving WebShop performance by 12.7%p.
significance: The work reframes action verification from asking what evidence supports an action to seeking evidence that refutes it, exposing a blind spot of confirmation-oriented checks through which wrong actions still pass. The results indicate that language model agents possess an underused capacity to recognize and self-correct misaligned actions, and that this capacity can be systematically elicited by active conjecture and refutation prior to execution.

zh.title: 通过猜想与反驳进行语言模型智能体的动作验证
zh.summary: 本文提出 BlackSwan，一种反驳导向的“期望-怀疑-检验”（expect-suspect-test）流程，用于在执行前验证语言模型智能体（language model agent）的动作。对于每一个会改变状态的动作，BlackSwan 预测其预期效果，就该动作可能出错的方式提出具体且可实证检验的猜想（conjecture），并利用已有观测或额外的非状态改变动作来检验这些猜想，只有在没有任何猜想通过检验时才执行该动作。在具有挑战性的 AppWorld 任务中，与最强基线相比，BlackSwan 在骨干模型开启和不开启 thinking mode 时分别将成功率提升 14.9 和 25.2 个百分点（%p）；即使不使用 thinking mode 和上下文示例（in-context demonstrations），其表现仍优于配备了这些能力的更强基线。该收益还可迁移到 AppWorld 之外，在 WebShop 上提升 12.7 个百分点（%p）。
zh.significance: 该工作把动作验证的思路从“寻找支持某个动作的证据”转向“寻找反驳该动作的证据”，揭示了确认式检查的盲区：错误动作往往能通过所有询问其是否正确的检查。结果表明，语言模型智能体具有识别并自我纠正错位动作的未被充分利用的能力，而通过执行前的主动猜想（conjecture）与反驳（refutation），可以系统地激发这一能力。
zh.aiRoleDescription: 论文提出了 BlackSwan，一种以反驳为导向的 expect-suspect-test 流程，其语言模型智能体会推测某个操作可能出错的方式并在执行前检验这些假设。在 AppWorld 上，该方法在开启与关闭骨干模型思考模式时分别比最强基线提升 14.9 和 25.2 个百分点，并在 WebShop 上提升 12.7 个百分点。

title: Modern Software Engineering with Verification Agents: A Spec-First Architecture for Autonomous Synthesis, Verification IRs, and Organizational Scale
summary: This paper proposes an end-to-end architecture for agent-authored, formally verified software engineering in which autonomous agents generate implementation code, formal specifications, and mechanical proofs together. The architecture inverts the usual workflow so that the formal specification becomes the primary human-reviewed artifact, while code and proof scripts are treated as disposable build outputs. Its logic-agnostic foundation combines a spec-first stack inversion, a CI-gated workflow without manual code review, and a minimal Verification Intermediate Representation (VIR) lowered through a thin verified translator. An extensional Computational Type Theory (CTT) specification layer with Higher-Order Abstract Syntax (HOAS) and linear resource typing is designed to reduce rewrite friction for synthesis agents, with a protocol frozen before the first reader to measure whether removing boundary coercions improves specification readability. For organizational scale, Personal Spec-Copilots and a Shared Synthesis Fleet detect cross-team Semantic Merge Conflicts and fuse modular contracts into zero-copy binaries. The approach is illustrated on a zero-copy authenticated message router, with existing baselines salt, SaltBench, x86lean, and MetaPRL distinguished from newly proposed components.
significance: The work reframes human review around specifications rather than generated code and proofs, potentially cutting verification and integration costs as autonomous coding agents handle larger software systems. The Verification Intermediate Representation offers a shared, minimal interface between varied logical foundations and synthesis tooling, while the frozen-protocol readability experiment supplies a falsifiable test of a central design claim. The multi-team architecture addresses a practical obstacle to deploying formal methods at organizational scale by turning contract fusion and semantic conflict detection into automated processes. The concrete router example and separation of established baselines from proposed components help indicate which elements are already supported by empirical experience.

zh.title: 以规范优先的现代软件工程与验证智能体：面向自主合成、验证中间表示与组织规模化的架构
zh.summary: 本文提出一种端到端的架构，用于由智能体撰写并经形式化验证的软件工程，使自主智能体同时生成实现代码、形式化规范（formal specification）与机械证明。该架构颠倒了常规工作流，将形式化规范作为供人审阅的主要工件，而把代码与证明脚本视为可丢弃的构建产物。其逻辑无关的基础部分结合了规范优先的栈反转、由持续集成（CI）自动检查把关且无需人工代码评审的工作流，以及通过薄层已验证翻译器降级生成的极简验证中间表示（Verification Intermediate Representation, VIR）。扩展式计算类型论（Computational Type Theory, CTT）规范层配合高阶抽象语法（Higher-Order Abstract Syntax, HOAS）与线性资源类型，旨在减少合成智能体的重写阻力；研究者还预先冻结实验协议，在第一位读者出现之前固定方案，以衡量去除边界强制转换是否提升规范可读性。为实现组织级协作扩展，架构引入个人规范副驾（Personal Spec-Copilots）与共享合成舰队（Shared Synthesis Fleet），用于检测跨团队语义合并冲突（Semantic Merge Conflicts），并把模块化契约融合为零拷贝二进制文件。论文以零拷贝认证消息路由器为例说明该架构，并明确区分既有经验基线 salt、SaltBench、x86lean 与 MetaPRL，以及新提出的组件。
zh.significance: 这项工作把人工评审的重心从生成的代码与证明转向规范，有望在自主编码智能体承担更大规模软件系统时降低验证与集成成本。验证中间表示（Verification Intermediate Representation）为不同逻辑基础与合成工具提供了共享的极简接口，而协议预先冻结的可读性实验则为架构的核心设计主张提供了可证伪的检验。多团队架构通过把契约融合与语义冲突检测自动化，回应了在组织规模上部署形式化方法的现实障碍。具体的路由器示例，以及对既有基线与新提出组件的区分，有助于说明哪些部分已有经验基础。

title: LARK: Lean-Assisted Reasoning for LLM-Generated GPU Kernels
summary: LARK is an agentic framework that formally verifies LLM-generated GPU kernels against their PyTorch reference implementations, proving equivalence in functional and memory behavior under exact arithmetic rather than relying on testing. It formalizes the GPU machine model and per-operation semantics in Lean 4 once per target language, then uses LLM agents in two steps: an agent decomposes whole-kernel semantics into segments validated by Lean 4, and further agents write Lean proofs that each segment matches its PyTorch counterpart, yielding whole-program equivalence. Combined with a simple ReAct agent on KernelCraft GPU tasks, LARK lets GLM 5.3 fully verify 10 of 12 Level-1 kernels and Opus 5.5 all 5 Level-2 kernels; across 10 production kernels sampled from open-source LLM serving frameworks, it verifies 9 and finds a new data race bug in the tenth.
significance: By shifting human effort from checking every generated line to verifying operator-level Lean semantics once ahead of generation, LARK establishes a trust boundary that makes large-scale, verifiable code generation practical. Its two-step proof strategy makes equivalence proving tractable for large kernels, and finding a previously unknown data race in production code shows formal verification delivers guarantees beyond what testing can provide.

aiRole.description: LARK is an agentic framework in which LLM agents decompose kernel semantics and write Lean 4 proofs establishing whole-program equivalence between generated GPU kernels and PyTorch references; combined with a ReAct agent it verified 10 of 12 Level-1 and all 5 Level-2 KernelCraft kernels, plus 9 of 10 production…

humanContribution: Humans built the framework, formalized the GPU machine model and per-operation semantics in Lean 4 once per target language, and verified operator-level Lean semantics ahead of kernel generation.

zh.title: LARK：面向LLM生成GPU内核的Lean辅助推理
zh.summary: LARK是一个智能体框架，可将LLM生成的GPU内核与其PyTorch参考实现进行形式化验证（formal verification），在精确算术下证明功能与内存行为的等价性（equivalence），而非依赖测试。该框架在Lean 4中针对每种目标语言一次性形式化GPU机器模型与各运算的语义，随后由LLM智能体分两步完成证明：一个智能体将整个内核的语义分解为若干片段，由Lean 4验证该分解的正确性；其余智能体编写Lean证明，使每个片段与其PyTorch对应部分匹配，合起来得到整程序等价性（whole-program equivalence）。在KernelCraft GPU任务上与简单的ReAct智能体结合时，LARK使GLM 5.3完整验证12个Level-1内核中的10个，Opus 5.5完整验证全部5个Level-2内核；在从开源LLM服务框架中随机抽取的10个生产级内核上，LARK验证了其中9个，并在第10个中发现一个此前未知的数据竞争（data race）缺陷。
zh.significance: LARK将人工投入从逐行检查生成代码转变为仅在生成前一次性验证算子级Lean语义，由此确立了信任边界，使大规模可验证代码生成成为现实。其两步证明策略使大型内核的等价性证明变得可行，而在生产代码中发现此前未知的数据竞争也表明，形式化验证能够提供测试无法给出的正确性保证。

title: Counterexample-driven autonomous research with application to excess radiated energy in a Z-pinch
summary: The paper introduces Simjecture, an open-source framework in which language-model agents pursue human-defined physical conjectures through counterexample-driven falsification and prospective hypothesis repair, using computational physics as an executable testbed while separating numerical-instrument qualification from scientific claim review. In an 82.6 h investigation of the long-standing Z-pinch problem of radiated energy exceeding imploding-shell kinetic energy, the study finds competing effects of energy conversion, retention, and release timing: stronger coherent helical deformation raises resistive conversion but lowers radiation and retains more energy, while a broader trailing-plasma profile delays the later radiation maximum and recovers much of the early bolometric deficit.
significance: The work refactors open-ended AI search for empirical science, where no model is final and claims must be tested against computation, and it produces concrete insight into the energy budget of high-energy-density plasma physics. The framework offers a recorded, auditable paradigm in which solvers and diagnostics can be adapted during an investigation.

aiRole.description: Language-model agents in the Simjecture framework ran an 82.6-hour counterexample-driven investigation that produced new findings on excess radiated energy in a Z-pinch, including competing effects of energy conversion, retention, and release timing and how helical deformation and trailing-plasma profiles affect them.

humanContribution: Humans built and open-sourced the Simjecture framework, defined the physical conjectures pursued by the agents, structured the falsification and repair workflow, and separated numerical instrument qualification from scientific claim review.

zh.title: 反例驱动的自主研究及其在Z箍缩（Z-pinch）过剩辐射能量问题中的应用
zh.summary: 论文提出开源框架 Simjecture，其中语言模型智能体围绕人类定义的物理猜想（conjecture）展开研究，采用反例驱动的证伪与前瞻性的假设修复，并以计算物理作为可执行的测试平台，同时将数值工具的资质认定与科学主张的评审分离。在一项长达 82.6 h 的研究中，团队针对Z箍缩中辐射能量超过内爆壳层动能这一长期存在的问题展开探究，发现能量转换、能量留存与释放时序之间存在相互竞争的效应：更强的相干螺旋形变提高电阻性转换，却降低辐射并使更多能量留存；更宽的尾随等离子体剖面则推迟后期辐射峰值，并弥补了早期辐射测量（测辐射热）的相当一部分亏损。
zh.significance: 该工作将开放式人工智能搜索改造为适用于经验科学的研究流程，其中不存在最终模型，主张必须经受计算检验，并为高能量密度等离子体物理（high-energy-density plasma physics）的能量收支问题提供了具体新见解。该框架给出一种有记录、可审计的新范式，允许在研究过程中调整求解器与诊断工具。
zh.aiRoleDescription: Simjecture 框架中的语言模型智能体开展了一项历时 82.6 小时、以反例驱动的探究，产出了关于 Z 箍缩中过剩辐射能量的新发现，包括能量转换、滞留与释放时序之间的竞争效应，以及螺旋形变和尾随等离子体剖面如何影响这些效应。
zh.humanContribution: 人类构建并开源了 Simjecture 框架，定义了智能体所探究的物理猜想，设计了证伪与假设修复的工作流程，并将数值仪器的鉴定与科学主张的评审分离开来。

title: ProofPatch: Reviewing Lean Statements and Keeping the Reviews Valid as Formalizations Evolve
summary: ProofPatch is a tool that helps reviewers check whether Lean statements say what was intended and keeps those judgments valid as formal developments change. Reviewers can pose targeted questions to the Lean kernel, such as whether a hypothesis is necessary or whether a counterexample exists, and each decision is stored with fingerprints of the elaborated statement and the definitions it depends on; any declaration can be pinned so that patches altering it are rejected, whether written by a person or by an LLM agent. Operating on elaborated terms rather than source text means notation and formatting changes leave decisions intact while a changed definition reaches every theorem using it. Across 229 pairs of consecutive Mathlib revisions, ProofPatch sends 118 of 12,898 synthetic decisions back for review, and every text-based alternative misses at least 38 of these or sends back at least 13 times as many. On 1,527 labeled statements, kernel evidence flags unfaithful statements with precision 0.88 to 0.96, and across 344 runs of an LLM agent no change to a pinned statement got through.
significance: As LLMs produce formal statements in bulk and agents edit developments continuously, the unchecked risk shifts from whether proofs are correct to whether formalizations express the intended mathematics. ProofPatch turns reviewer judgments into machine-checked, dependency-aware constraints that survive refactoring, measurably outperforming text-based tracking on real Mathlib revision pairs.

zh.title: ProofPatch：审核Lean语句并在形式化演进时保持审核结论有效
zh.summary: ProofPatch是一个帮助审核者检查Lean语句是否表达了预期含义、并在形式化开发持续演进时保持这些审核结论有效的工具。审核者可以向Lean内核提出针对性问题，例如某个假设是否必要，或是否存在反例；每个结论都会与经Lean精化（elaborated）的语句及其所依赖定义的指纹一同存储，并且任何声明都可被固定（pinned），从而阻止改变该声明的补丁通过，无论补丁由人编写还是由基于大语言模型（LLM）的代理编写。以精化后的项而非源文本为处理对象是核心设计选择：记号与格式的修改不会使审核结论失效，而定义的变更会波及每一个使用该定义的定理。在Mathlib连续版本的229组配对上，ProofPatch将12,898个合成审核结论中的118个送回复审，而每种基于文本的替代方法至少漏掉其中38个，或至少多送回13倍的结论。在1,527条已标注语句上，内核证据以0.88至0.96的精确率标记出不忠实于预期的语句；在344次LLM代理运行中，没有任何对被固定语句的改动得以通过。
zh.significance: 随着大语言模型批量生成形式语句、代理持续编辑形式化开发，风险重心从证明是否正确转移到形式化是否准确表达预期的数学含义。ProofPatch将审核者的判断转化为机器可检验、感知依赖关系的约束，并且这些约束在重构后依然有效，在真实的Mathlib版本配对上明显优于基于文本的追踪方法。

title: Geometric and algebraic inference in humans and neural networks
summary: This work formalizes two inference strategies used by humans and neural networks: geometric inference, which gradually reshapes representational geometry to mirror relational structure so later inference becomes cheap, and algebraic inference, which flexibly attends to and reasons over novel relations supplied in context at greater inference-time cost. The authors derive opposing signatures of the two strategies in transitive inference and predict that geometric inference dominates for familiar relations while algebraic inference supports de novo inferences, with experiments confirming these signatures in humans, networks trained from scratch, and large language models (LLMs). Causal interventions show the strategies rely on representational geometry and selective attention mechanisms respectively, reproducing the effects of analogous neurobiological disruptions.
significance: The framework reconciles competing accounts of cognitive flexibility by giving representational geometry and algebraic manipulation distinct, complementary roles, while unifying content effects in human and LLM reasoning with data-distribution effects in machine learning. It offers testable predictions about when each strategy should appear and mechanistic links between network components and human reasoning behavior.

zh.title: 人类与神经网络中的几何与代数推理
zh.summary: 这项研究将人类与神经网络使用的两类推理策略形式化：几何推理逐步重塑表征几何，使其反映底层关系结构，从而让后续推理代价低廉；代数推理则灵活地关注并处理上下文中给出的新颖关系，但在推理时需要额外计算。作者在传递推理（transitive inference）中推导出这两种策略相互对立的特征，并预测几何推理在关系熟悉时占主导，而代数推理支持在上下文中进行的从头推断；实验在人类、从零开始训练的网络以及大型语言模型（LLM）中均证实了这些特征。因果干预表明，两种策略分别依赖表征几何与选择性注意机制，并复现了人类中相应神经生物学损伤的效应。
zh.significance: 该框架通过赋予表征几何与代数操作各自独特且互补的作用，调和了关于认知灵活性的竞争性观点，并将人类与大型语言模型推理中的内容效应同机器学习中的数据分布效应统一起来。它提供了关于两种策略何时出现的可检验预测，并建立了网络组件与人类推理行为之间的机制性联系。

title: VerusWeave: A Benchmark for Proof Repair in Concurrent Verus Programs
summary: VerusWeave is the first benchmark dedicated to proof repair in concurrent Verus programs, derived from four open-source projects. It contains 75 focused tasks and 17 full-module variants covering features used to verify low-level concurrent code; each task removes selected proof annotations and asks agents to fill the gaps while keeping executable code and specifications intact. An evaluation harness validates repairs with Verus and a change checker, recording solutions, execution traces, and resource usage. Initial evaluation of four general-purpose coding-agent harnesses reached 75-85% success on focused tasks and 29-47% on full-module variants.
significance: Concurrency bugs can evade conventional testing, while Verus lets developers specify, implement, and prove the correctness of concurrent Rust code in one language. Existing Verus benchmarks offer limited coverage of tasks linking atomic operations to abstract protocols, and this benchmark targets that gap in proof repair. The large drop from focused tasks to full-module variants shows that autonomous module-wide repair remains difficult, and the benchmark offers a reusable foundation for evaluating automated proof construction for concurrent software.

aiRole.description: VerusWeave introduces the first benchmark for concurrent proof repair in Verus, with 75 focused tasks and 17 full-module variants derived from four open-source projects, and reports that four general-purpose coding-agent harnesses achieved 75-85% success on focused tasks and 29-47% on full-module variants.

humanContribution: Humans derived the tasks from four open-source projects, removed selected proof annotations to create repair gaps, and built the evaluation harness that validates repairs with Verus and a change checker while recording solutions, traces, and resource usage.

title: Automated Theorem Generation in First-Order Logic by Construction from Triangular Standard Contradictions
summary: The paper presents a constructive framework for automated theorem generation in first-order logic based on triangular standard contradictions. The method builds minimally unsatisfiable clause sets from selected first-order literals, then turns them into theorems by retaining some clauses as premises and negating one clause, or a conjunction of clauses, as the conclusion. Minimal unsatisfiability keeps the premises satisfiable, avoiding trivial inference by explosion, while the unsatisfiability of the full set guarantees entailment, so theorems are correct by construction with no per-instance proof procedure. Extending the earlier Δ1 generator, the authors introduce Δ2 through Δ8, giving a unified family of eight generation methods, and formulate a general Δ-class method covering the family. Δ1 through Δ4 are implemented and released, and combinatorial analysis indicates the capacity to systematically produce large numbers of distinct theorems.
significance: Most theorem-generation systems emit candidates that still require proof or formal verification, whereas this framework guarantees every generated theorem is valid at construction time. That removes a costly verification bottleneck and provides a principled foundation for automated theorem discovery and for building logically guaranteed knowledge bases.

zh.title: 通过三角标准矛盾从构造出发的一阶逻辑自动定理生成
zh.summary: 本文提出一种基于三角标准矛盾（triangular standard contradictions）的一阶逻辑（first-order logic）自动定理生成（automated theorem generation）构造性框架。该方法由选定的一阶文字构造最小不可满足子句集，随后保留部分子句作为前提，并将单个子句或若干子句的合取的否定作为结论，从而形成定理。最小不可满足性保证剩余前提可满足，避免由爆炸导致的平凡推理，而完整子句集的不可满足性保证所得蕴含成立，因此定理在构造上即为正确，无需对每个实例另设证明过程。在先前的 Δ1 生成器基础上，研究者引入 Δ2 至 Δ8，形成包含八种定理生成方法的统一家族，并给出涵盖该家族的一般 Δ 类方法。Δ1 至 Δ4 已实现并发布；组合分析显示该框架能够系统地生成大量互不相同的定理。
zh.significance: 多数定理生成系统输出的候选命题仍需后续证明或形式化验证，而该框架保证每条生成的定理在构造时即成立，从而消除了代价高昂的验证瓶颈，为自动定理发现（automated theorem discovery）以及构建具有逻辑保证的知识库提供了原则性基础。

title: DAPS: Dependency-Aware Premise Selection for LLM Theorem Proving
summary: DAPS targets premise selection for LLM-based theorem proving in Lean 4, where retrieval over-represents popular foundational lemmas and buries rare or newly contributed premises among hundreds of thousands of candidates. The authors systematically mine 53 Lean Blueprint projects, yielding 3,805 manually curated informal-plus-formal nodes containing research-level premises absent from Mathlib4, and extract typed, multi-level Mathlib4 dependencies. DAPS combines a structural neighborhood encoder, a group-level contrastive objective, and a Mathlib-then-Blueprint adaptation procedure, reaching mean Recall@32 of 89.25 on Mathlib4-Heldout (+11.41 over LeanHammer) and keeping the lead on two out-of-distribution benchmarks. Its selected premises also improve theorem proving on miniF2F and IMO-ProofBench.
significance: Rare, research-level and newly added lemmas are systematically under-retrieved, which limits LLM provers on competition problems and informal-language queries. Restoring dependency structure to both data and model yields measurable gains in retrieval that transfer out of distribution and translate into better end-to-end proving performance.

title: Researcher-in-the-Loop Evolutionary Discovery of Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Code Families
summary: The paper presents a researcher-in-the-loop pipeline combining LLM-guided program evolution, exact evaluation, mathematical generalization, certified nonexistence checks, and formal proof checking, applied to entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting codes (EAQECCs). Evolved programs yielded finite qubit constructions that researchers generalized into the family [[n,1,n-1;n-q-1]]_q for prime powers q≥3 with n≥2q+1 and for q=2 with odd n≥5, with Lean checking the underlying algebraic certificate. Together with entanglement lifting, this closes 54 gaps in archived EAQECC tables; the release includes 115 verified code records, ten nonexistence results with checked DRAT proofs, family implementations, and preserved search programs for seeded replay. In eight paired generation blocks, validation-selected iterative programs succeeded in 46.1% and 31.6% of held-out executions at unseen lengths n=13,15, versus 19.5% and 3.1% for independently generated programs.
significance: The work shows how computational discoveries from program evolution can be elevated into a proved, general code family backed by independently checkable evidence, addressing validity, generality, and reproducibility simultaneously. The combination of Lean-certified algebraic certificates, machine-checked nonexistence proofs, and reproducible search artifacts offers a model for trustworthy AI-assisted mathematical construction, while the held-out results quantify the benefit of validation-guided iterative program generation.

title: Ramanujan Challenge Results: AI-Assisted Evaluation Pipeline for Multi-Format Proofs
summary: This work analyzes submissions to the Ramanujan Challenge, a benchmark of research-level problems in number theory whose constant formulas are numerically checkable but may require deep proofs, including unpublished results and open conjectures. It measures the relative success of AI models, Computer Algebra Systems (CAS), and formal tools, and reports correct submissions that are conceptually distinct from the official solutions as well as a proof of one published open conjecture. To address the difficulty of judging complex proofs at scale, the authors introduce an AI-assisted evaluation pipeline covering natural language proofs, CAS code, and Lean formalizations, which cuts false-positive verdicts on natural language proofs from 23% to 6% and raises judgment accuracy on supporting code from 46% to 58%.
significance: Reliable evaluation of research-level proofs is a growing bottleneck as AI systems tackle problems beyond textbook and olympiad settings. The reported pipeline demonstrably reduces over-acceptance of flawed proofs and improves assessment of accompanying code, offering a reusable methodology for scalable benchmarking of mathematical reasoning in both mathematics and AI for science.

title: Algebraic World Model: From Exploration to Proofs
summary: The Algebraic World Model (AWM) is a framework that turns interaction with unfamiliar environments into explicit mathematical models supporting formal reasoning. AWM explores an environment, builds and revises executable Python hypotheses against observations, organizes them into typed objects and shared rules, simplifies them via category-theory-guided transformations, and formalizes the resulting model in Lean 4 to prove reachability and impossibility. On two impossible game levels it produced closed, kernel-checked Lean proofs excluding every legal winning sequence in all six runs, versus none in twelve baseline runs for Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. Four of AWM's six initial bounds were correct (one for Opus 5.5, none for GPT-6 Astra), rising to six of six after feedback about a cheaper win. Across all 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games, the resulting models let Lean replay winning trajectories for all 183 levels and generalize to unseen transitions and changed mechanics; with Claude Opus 5, AWM clears all levels with a score of 99.9, using certified winning trajectories with 43% of the human baseline's actions.
significance: AWM shows that machine-checked proofs can be obtained not only from predefined definitions but from environments whose rules are discovered empirically, including formal impossibility certificates that rule out winning sequences beyond explored trajectories. Its interpretable, testable models could give theorem proving systems a path to rigorous reasoning about unknown systems, with measured advantages over tool-equipped frontier models in both proof construction and bound accuracy.

aiRole.description: AWM constructs closed, kernel-checked Lean 4 proofs that certain game goals are unreachable, and produces interpretable mathematical models whose rules let Lean replay winning trajectories across 25 ARC-AGI-3 games and generalize beyond observed play.

humanContribution: Humans designed and built the AWM framework and provided feedback, such as noting that a cheaper win exists, which led AWM to revise its rules and construct new proofs.

zh.title: 代数世界模型：从探索到证明
zh.summary: 代数世界模型（Algebraic World Model，AWM）是一个将与陌生环境的交互转化为显式数学模型并支持形式化推理（formal reasoning）的框架。AWM 探索环境，依据观测构建并修订可执行的 Python 假设，将其组织为带类型的对象与共享规则，借助由范畴论（category theory）引导的变换简化结构，并把所得模型在 Lean 4 中形式化，以证明可达性与不可能性。在两个不可能的游戏关卡上，AWM 在全部六次运行中构造出封闭且经内核检查的 Lean 证明，排除所有合法获胜序列，而 Claude Opus 5.5 与 GPT-6 Astra 在十二次基线运行中没有产出任何此类证明。AWM 的六个初始界中有四个正确（Opus 5.5 一个，GPT-6 Astra 无），在仅收到存在更省动作的获胜方式的反馈后，AWM 修订规则并构造新证明，达到六个全对。在全部 25 个公开 ARC-AGI-3 游戏中，这些模型使 Lean 能重放全部 183 个关卡的获胜轨迹，并推广到未观测的转移与机制变化；配合 Claude Opus 5，AWM 以 99.9 的分数通关全部关卡，其经认证的获胜轨迹仅使用人类基线 43% 的动作。
zh.significance: AWM 表明，机器检查证明不仅可以来自预定义的定义，也可以来自规则需经经验发现的环境，其中还包括排除探索轨迹之外获胜序列的形式化不可能性证书。其可解释、可逐步检验的模型为定理证明（theorem proving）系统对未知系统进行严格推理提供了可行路径，并在证明构造与界值准确性上相对配备工具的前沿模型取得了可量化的提升。
zh.aiRoleDescription: AWM 构造了经内核检查的 Lean 4 封闭证明，说明某些游戏目标不可达，并生成可解释的数学模型，其规则使 Lean 能在 25 个 ARC-AGI-3 游戏中重放获胜轨迹并超越已观测的玩法进行泛化。
zh.humanContribution: 人类设计并构建了 AWM 框架，并提供了诸如存在更廉价获胜方式的反馈，促使 AWM 修订规则并构造新的证明。

title: Scaling Mathematical Proof Supervision from Structured Textbooks
summary: TOME-Math (Textbook-Oriented Mathematical Evidence) is a large-scale corpus built from 2,118 university-level mathematics textbooks, yielding about 380K structured proof-supervision records that preserve chapter order, proposition-proof links, dependency references, and source provenance. Using these structural signals, the authors explore curriculum learning across several mathematical subjects and characterize scaling with supervision volume and source breadth. Fine-tuning at full scale improves the unweighted mean score over held-out evaluations and established public benchmarks by 16.7 percentage points over the base model and outperforms all three public instruction-data baselines in aggregate. The corpus is to be released.
significance: The work turns textbook structure rather than flattened problem-solution pairs into machine supervision, giving a scalable source of mathematical training data while keeping evidential and curricular organization intact. Its scaling analysis offers empirical evidence that data organization itself affects mathematical reasoning, and the planned corpus release enables further study of structured mathematical supervision.

title: Beyond Selected Breakthroughs: Evaluating Language Models on Randomly Sampled Mathematical Conjectures
summary: This work introduces OpenConjecture, a dataset of conjectures from mathematics papers posted on arXiv since February 2026, and uses it to evaluate frontier GPT models on a random sample of 200 conjectures. Over three passes with a reproducible protocol and no problem-specific mathematical guidance, the models produced candidate solutions for about 60% of conjectures, with counterexamples roughly 1.3 times more frequent than proofs. Rather than expert-verifying these candidates, the authors analyze solution types, novelty, relations to and citations of existing literature, and whether proposed resolutions exploit errors or underspecification in the conjecture. The models sometimes answer outside the authors' intent, such as offering the trivial group as a counterexample, and several proofs follow closely from known results, though some resolutions show at least moderate novelty.
significance: Evaluations focused on celebrated breakthroughs overstate how well language models handle open mathematics and hide the compute cost involved. Sampling conjectures systematically reveals where models succeed, how their outputs draw on prior work, and how often they sidestep the intended problem, supporting richer benchmarks that assess fidelity to the statement and attribution alongside correctness.

title: Hammering with Vampire in Lean
summary: The paper presents Vampire-Hammer, a hammer for the Lean interactive theorem prover that discharges goals with the Vampire automated theorem prover and reconstructs proofs certified by the Lean kernel. Vampire-Hammer uses the Lean-auto framework to process goals and premises before sending them to Vampire, relying on standard TPTP problem formats and annotated TSTP proofs to support reconstruction. With a 10-second budget over 196,083 eligible Mathlib theorems, Vampire-Hammer solves 21,158 problems that other evaluated tools do not solve within the same budget.
significance: Connecting a strong general-purpose automated theorem prover to Lean with kernel-checked proof reconstruction gives formal mathematics practitioners stronger goal automation without sacrificing trust. The evaluation shows that Vampire-Hammer contributes substantial unique coverage of Mathlib theorems beyond existing tools, making it a valuable complement in interactive proving workflows.

title: H$^2$R: Hierarchical Hint-Based Reward for Mathematical Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
summary: This work introduces Hierarchical Hint-based Reward, a reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) framework that uses the sub-question structure of math problems as logically grounded intermediate milestones, reducing the reasoning horizon toward the final answer. The authors also present HiMath, a benchmark of hierarchically structured math problems. Hierarchical hints improve performance across diverse LLMs even without task-specific training, and integrating them into RL training raises Qwen2.5-Math-7B accuracy on HiMath from 30.4% to 39.1%, reaching up to 45.6% with Oracle Hierarchical Hints.
significance: Complex multi-step mathematical reasoning suffers from sparse, answer-only supervision in RLVR. The reported gains suggest that reliable intermediate checkpoints in reward design help sustain long-horizon mathematical reasoning, and the HiMath benchmark provides a structured testbed for evaluating such methods across models.

title: Countable Nondeterminism in Weighted Programming with an Application to Mechanized Foundations for Probabilistic Program Verification
summary: This work extends weighted programming, introduced by Batz et al., which describes mathematical models and optimization problems as imperative programs parametrized over semirings, with two features: countable nondeterminism and user-defined additive rewards. The programs are then parametrized over modules rather than semirings. Because continuity properties commonly assumed in program semantics can fail under countable nondeterminism, wp-style reasoning for such programs may be unsound over arbitrary modules. The authors introduce an operational ground truth based on weighted decision processes (WDPs), transition systems generalizing Markov decision processes by drawing transition weights and state rewards from a module, and give conditions under which a wp-style transformer is sound with respect to it. They then show that many concrete instances satisfy these conditions and support sound weakest precondition reasoning, illustrated by case studies covering expected resource consumption of probabilistic programs and optimal scores of combinatorial games. The extended framework and main soundness results are mechanized in Lean, yielding, to the authors' knowledge, the first mechanized proof of a fixed point characterization of minimal expected rewards in Markov decision processes with countable nondeterminism.
significance: The work addresses a known soundness gap in weakest precondition calculi for programs with unbounded choice and rewards, supplying checkable semantic conditions rather than assuming continuity. Mechanizing the framework and its soundness theorems in Lean turns a delicate semantic argument into a machine-checked artifact, and the instantiated probabilistic result gives formally verified foundations for reasoning about expected rewards in Markov decision processes with countable nondeterminism, with extensions to resource analysis and game optimization.

zh.title: 带权重编程中的可数非确定性及其在概率程序验证机械化基础中的应用
zh.summary: 本文扩展了由 Batz 等人提出的带权重编程（weighted programming）框架：该框架把数学模型或优化问题描述为参数化于半环（semirings）的命令式程序，并用最弱前置条件演算（wp-calculi）等程序验证技术加以分析。本文为其加入两项特性，即可数非确定性（countable nondeterminism）与用户自定义的加性奖励，此时程序参数化于模块（modules）而非半环。由于程序语义中常用的连续性性质在可数非确定性下可能失效，在任意模块上对这类程序做最弱前置条件推理可能是不可靠的。作者以加权决策过程（WDPs）定义操作语义上的基准：这类转移系统把转移权重与状态奖励取自某个模块，是马尔可夫决策过程（Markov decision processes）的推广。基于该基准，作者给出使最弱前置条件风格变换器（wp-style transformer）保持可靠性的条件，并证明一系列具体实例满足这些条件，从而支持可靠的最弱前置条件推理；案例研究涉及概率程序的期望资源消耗与组合博弈的最优得分。扩展后的框架及主要可靠性定理已在交互式定理证明器 Lean 中完成机械化，据作者所知，由此得到首个关于含可数非确定性的马尔可夫决策过程中最小期望奖励之不动点刻画（fixed point characterization）的机械化证明。
zh.significance: 该工作针对含无界选择与奖励的程序在最弱前置条件演算中已知的可靠性缺口，给出可检验的语义条件，而非默认连续性成立。将框架及其可靠性定理在 Lean 中机械化，使原本精细的语义论证成为机器检验的形式化工件；而针对概率程序的实例化结果，为含可数非确定性的马尔可夫决策过程中期望奖励的推理提供了形式化基础，并可推广到资源分析与博弈优化。
