title: Scratchy: Visual-Scratchpad Multimodal Reasoning for Cryptographic Proof Generation in EasyCrypt
summary: This paper presents Scratchy, a visual-scratchpad approach for generating EasyCrypt proofs from natural-language security descriptions, formal context, and target propositions. Proof objects are normalized into a typed proof-relation graph, which a structure-preserving visual compiler converts into a formula-rich visual proof state that guides a multimodal model in producing the proof. The authors also introduce Scratchy-eval, a 114-task dataset derived from reliable official EasyCrypt files, comprising 64 security-form proof generations and 50 multiple-choice knowledge tests. Evaluations covering semantic grounding, relational invariants, and game reductions show that LLMs such as GPT-5.6-Sol and Claude-Opus-5 gain a clear advantage from Scratchy's structured visual proof states.
significance: Cryptographic proof generation requires coordinating probability, adversarial games, invariants, assumptions, and bounds, whose dependencies are typically implicit and scattered across programs, making them hard for LLMs to recover. Scratchy makes this proof structure explicit through a visual proof-state representation, and the reported gains for GPT-5.6-Sol and Claude-Opus-5 suggest that explicit structure and multimodal proof states are a promising direction for computer-aided cryptography, supported by the new Scratchy-eval benchmark.

aiRole.description: Scratchy normalizes proof objects into a typed proof-relation graph and compiles it into visual proof states that guide multimodal models in generating EasyCrypt proofs; evaluations on the Scratchy-eval benchmark show that GPT-5.6-Sol and Claude-Opus-5 gain a clear advantage from these structured visual proof states.

humanContribution: Humans built the Scratchy pipeline including graph normalization and the structure-preserving visual compiler, and curated the 114-task Scratchy-eval dataset from official EasyCrypt files before evaluating the models.

The central principle is epistemic separation: learned geometry may rank and organize evidence but cannot promote a hypothesis to certified ground truth. title: ModularPhaseNet: Finite-Cyclic Phase Geometry for Computable Semantic Hierarchy, Direction, and Context Consistency in Standard Transformers
summary: ModularPhaseNet replaces the continuous complex phase geometry of QuantumPhaseNet with a classical, integer-computable construction. Standard Transformer hidden states remain real-valued, while an auxiliary phase channel is quantized into a cyclic subgroup G = <g> of order q dividing p-1 inside the multiplicative group of F_p: a continuous phase e^{i phi} is encoded as z = g^a mod p, phase composition becomes group multiplication, relative phase becomes group division, conceptual hierarchy is induced by a filtration of cyclic quotients, semantic direction by oriented relative group elements, and contextual consistency by gauge-invariant cycle holonomy. Three components — a finite-phase encoder, a quotient-filtration hierarchy module, and a group-valued connection module — feed real-valued bias terms into self-attention. Training uses distributions in the real group algebra or straight-through Gumbel-Softmax; inference uses exact modular exponentiation and lookup tables, with no quantum hardware, complex-valued matrix multiplication, or discrete logarithms. The paper proves quantization-distortion bounds, nesting of quotient-induced partitions, gauge invariance, a discrete integrability result for flat connections, and boundedness of the attention output. It reports theory plus a pre-registered evaluation plan; the experiments of Section 14 have not been run and no empirical result is claimed.
significance: The construction turns phase-based relational structure into exact integer arithmetic that is cheap to compute and free of complex or quantum resources, while supplying proved guarantees for its discretization and invariants. The pre-registered plan targets hierarchy recovery, discourse alignment, contradiction detection, and calibrated hallucination-risk prediction under controlled compute, offering a reproducible test of whether exact discrete invariants help standard Transformers; since the experiments remain outstanding, the central empirical hypothesis is currently unverified.

title: Do LLMs Exhibit Coherent Knowledge Structures in Mathematical Reasoning? A Perspective from Knowledge Space Theory
summary: The paper introduces a framework grounded in Knowledge Space Theory (KST) to evaluate the knowledge structure of LLMs in mathematical reasoning, using KST as a normative benchmark for principled knowledge dependencies. Comparing eight open- and closed-source LLMs with real human learners, the study finds that LLMs frequently violate prerequisite knowledge dependencies, fail to use related knowledge provided in context to improve performance on dependent questions, and lack consistent shared structures, with low overlap among their knowledge distributions. These deficiencies remain largely invisible to accuracy-based and LLM-as-judge evaluations.
significance: The results provide behavioral evidence that current LLM knowledge is not organized in a human-like structure, challenging assumptions behind existing performance-based evaluations and informing how mathematical reasoning abilities should be assessed and developed.

aiRole.description: A KST-grounded framework evaluated eight open- and closed-source LLMs on mathematical reasoning, finding that they violate human knowledge dependencies and do not share a consistent knowledge structure. These structural deficiencies were largely invisible to accuracy-based and LLM-as-judge evaluations.

title: AxQM: A Textbook-Scale Benchmark for Formal Proof Synthesis in a Library of Finite-Dimensional Quantum Mechanics
summary: AxQM is a benchmark of 1,019 kernel-checkable proof-synthesis tasks built on 479 items from Nielsen and Chuang's textbook Quantum Computation and Quantum Information, all stated in a custom Lean library of finite-dimensional quantum mechanics. It is derived from a near-complete formalization of the textbook's formal portions, so every task is guaranteed a solution, which the authors keep private. Grading is deterministic: the Lean kernel checks that the proof compiles, contains no sorry anywhere in its dependency closure, and introduces no new axioms. By task count it is the largest proof-synthesis benchmark in physics, exceeding the previous largest by a factor of four.
significance: Theoretical physics arguments rely on idealizations that are rarely spelled out fully, so unnoticed logical gaps can cascade across interdependent results. AxQM brings machine-checked rigor to physics and provides a large, reliably solvable and objectively graded testbed for evaluating autoformalization systems at textbook scale.

title: Capsule Lens: Locating and Tracking Concept Geometry in Model Representations
summary: Capsule Lens is a framework for characterizing where a concept sits in model representation space by fitting each concept's region with a capsule, a simple geometric form with interpretable parameters estimated in closed form and validated on held-out samples. The authors apply it to static representations across several models, where span and norm curves expose geometric traits, and to dynamic representations in three case studies: CLIP pretraining, RL post-training on visual question answering, and RL post-training on mathematical reasoning. These reveal qualitatively different dynamics, from broad network-wide restructuring during CLIP pretraining to localized, concept-specific changes under RL post-training, alongside both literature-consistent findings and novel observations.
significance: Existing methods largely project representations into more interpretable spaces rather than describing how concepts occupy them, and proposed hypotheses often lack rigorous validation and neglect temporal change. Capsule Lens offers a validated, trackable account of concept geometry in both static and dynamic settings, supporting mechanistic interpretability and the trustworthy deployment of capable models.

title: Extending concurrent separation logic to the hardware level to verify the xv6 OS kernel on RISC-V with AI agents
summary: MachCSL is a framework for verifying system software on top of low-level RISC-V semantics, based on the Sail RISC-V semantics. It adapts Iris-based concurrent separation logic to sub-instruction-level hardware reasoning, covering page-table translation, TLB, privilege levels, configuration registers, instruction fetch/decode/execute, traps and interrupts, DMA, shared memory, and power failures. As a case study, the authors verify the xv6 OS kernel (6,657 lines of C and assembly), a traditional Unix-style system with processes, file system, file descriptors, preemptive scheduling, multi-core support, and fine-grained locking. The effort uncovered 11 bugs in xv6, one bug in the Sail RISC-V semantics, and one bug in Sail's Lean extraction, taking 102 days including framework development. On top of the verified kernel, a theorem on console-level behavior is proved: typing echo hello world at the UART console can produce only the output hello world if no crashes or errors occur, covering the kernel and the init, sh, echo, cat, grep, sync, and seccomp binaries.
significance: The work shows that OS kernel verification can be pushed down to concrete hardware behavior, including traps, DMA, and power failures, rather than stopping at an abstract machine model. The case study demonstrates that LLM-based agents can handle the tedious sub-instruction reasoning this requires, while the theorem gives an end-to-end behavioral guarantee spanning the kernel and user binaries. The bugs found in xv6, in the Sail RISC-V semantics, and in Lean extraction indicate that such low-level verification also exposes defects in toolchains and hardware models themselves.

zh.summary: MachCSL是一个基于Sail RISC-V语义（Sail RISC-V semantics）、在底层RISC-V语义之上验证系统软件的框架。它将基于Iris的并发分离逻辑（concurrent separation logic）扩展到子指令级别的硬件推理，涵盖页表翻译、TLB、特权级、配置寄存器、指令取指/译码/执行、陷阱与中断、DMA、共享内存和断电等情况。作为案例研究，作者验证了xv6操作系统内核（6,657行C与汇编代码），该系统提供传统Unix风格的进程、文件系统、文件描述符与抢占式调度，并含多核支持与细粒度锁等大量内部并发。此次工作发现xv6实现中的11个bug、Sail RISC-V语义中的1个bug，以及Sail的Lean提取中的1个bug，验证过程历时102天（含MachCSL框架开发）。在已验证内核之上，研究者证明了一个关于控制台行为的定理：若无崩溃或其他错误，在UART控制台输入echo hello world时，系统能产生的唯一输出为hello world。该定理覆盖内核以及初始文件系统镜像中的init、sh、echo、cat、grep、sync、seccomp程序。
zh.significance: 这项工作表明操作系统内核验证可以下推到具体硬件行为层面，包括陷阱、DMA与断电，而不止于抽象机器模型。案例研究表明，基于LLM的智能体能够承担这种验证所需的繁琐子指令级推理；定理则给出贯穿内核与用户程序的端到端行为保证。在xv6、Sail RISC-V语义及Lean提取中发现的bug说明，这类底层验证也能揭示工具链与硬件模型自身的缺陷。
zh.aiRoleDescription: MachCSL 将基于 Iris 的并发分离逻辑适配到 Sail RISC-V 底层硬件语义，并借助 LLM 智能体验证 xv6 操作系统内核，发现 xv6 中 11 个缺陷、Sail RISC-V 语义中 1 个缺陷以及 Sail 的 Lean 提取中 1 个缺陷，并证明了覆盖内核与初始用户态二进制程序的控制台层行为定理。
zh.humanContribution: 人类构建了 MachCSL 框架，将并发分离逻辑适配到指令级以下的硬件推理，并主导和检查整个验证工作，包括框架开发在内共耗时 102 天。

title: LeanGRPO: Eliminating Redundant Recomputation in Diffusion RL
summary: LeanGRPO removes mathematically redundant timestep recomputation in on-policy diffusion reinforcement learning, where rollout and update use the same backend. It restructures the data-parallel layout and offers two recompute-free schedules for trajectory-logprob diffusion RL: LeanGRPO-Retain keeps gradient tracking during rollout and reuses the resulting computation graphs and saved activations directly for the update backward pass, while LeanGRPO-Reweight backpropagates each selected step immediately with a provisional advantage, delays gradient synchronization, and corrects the provisional gradients with the true advantage once the trajectory completes. The two schedules target different model scales and input sizes. Across FlowGRPO and DanceGRPO with FLUX.1-dev and Wan, the method yields up to 1.83x end-to-end speedup while preserving the original optimization objective.
significance: Diffusion RL is a standard post-training route for image and video generative models, and eliminating redundant recomputation directly reduces training cost without altering the optimization objective. The split into retain-and-reuse and provisional-gradient schedules gives practitioners memory- and compute-aware options across model scales, and the reported up to 1.83x end-to-end speedup shows the gains carry through full training runs on established FlowGRPO and DanceGRPO pipelines with FLUX.1-dev and Wan.

zh.title: LeanGRPO：消除扩散强化学习中的冗余重计算
zh.summary: LeanGRPO 消除了同策略（on-policy）扩散强化学习中在数学上冗余的时间步重计算，其中采样（rollout）与策略更新使用同一后端。该方法重构了数据并行布局，并为轨迹对数概率扩散强化学习（trajectory-logprob diffusion RL）提供两种免重计算训练调度：LeanGRPO-Retain 在采样期间保留梯度跟踪，并将由此得到的计算图和保存的激活值直接复用于更新阶段的反向传播；LeanGRPO-Reweight 同样在采样期间开启梯度，对每个选定时间步使用临时优势立即反向传播，延迟梯度同步，并在轨迹完成后用真实优势修正临时梯度。两种调度面向不同模型规模和输入尺寸。在 FlowGRPO 和 DanceGRPO 结合 FLUX.1-dev 与 Wan 的实验中，该方法在保持原有优化目标不变的前提下实现了最高 1.83 倍的端到端加速。
zh.significance: 扩散强化学习（diffusion RL）是图像和视频生成模型进行后训练的主流路线，消除冗余重计算可在不改变优化目标的前提下直接降低训练成本。保留复用与临时梯度修正两种调度的划分，使实践者能够依据模型规模在显存和算力之间做出选择；在成熟的 FlowGRPO 和 DanceGRPO 流水线上结合 FLUX.1-dev 与 Wan 测得的最高 1.83 倍端到端加速表明，该收益可贯通完整训练流程。

title: LeanStream: A Speculate-and-Refine Streaming Framework for Efficient on-Device LLM Inference
summary: LeanStream is a streaming speculate-and-refine framework for on-device LLM inference on mobile and embedded devices, where model weights exceed available DRAM. Existing activation-sparsity and weight-offload designs must choose between up-to-date context for accurate sparse execution decisions and early prediction for computation-I/O overlap, leading to serialized execution or redundant weight fetches, extra computation, and cache overhead. LeanStream progressively refines computation, loading, and cache-retention priorities using partial GPU results, achieving fine-grained overlap between GPU execution and storage I/O. Implemented on mobile and embedded platforms, it reduces memory usage by 4.8x to 7.5x at the best throughput of prior systems while improving token generation throughput by 1.6x to 2.1x.
significance: Moving large-model inference onto resource-constrained mobile and embedded hardware is central to private, responsive LLM deployment, and the storage-I/O bottleneck is the main obstacle. LeanStream's speculate-and-refine strategy offers a practical way to overlap GPU work with weight loading without the redundant fetches and cache costs of earlier approaches, making on-device inference substantially more memory-efficient and faster.

zh.title: LeanStream：面向高效端侧大语言模型推理的推测与精化流式框架
zh.summary: LeanStream 是一种面向端侧大语言模型（LLM）推理的流式推测与精化框架，适用于模型权重远超可用 DRAM 的移动与嵌入式设备。现有基于激活稀疏性与权重卸载的方案必须在两难之间取舍：精确的稀疏执行决策需要最新上下文，而高效的计算与 I/O 重叠需要提前预测，因而导致执行串行化，或产生冗余权重读取、额外计算和大量缓存开销。LeanStream 利用部分 GPU 结果逐步精化计算、加载与缓存保留的优先级，实现 GPU 执行与存储 I/O 的细粒度重叠。研究团队在移动与嵌入式平台上实现了该系统，在此前工作达到的最佳吞吐量下将内存占用降低 4.8 倍至 7.5 倍，并进一步将 token 生成吞吐量提升 1.6 倍至 2.1 倍。
zh.significance: 在资源受限的移动与嵌入式硬件上运行大模型推理，是实现注重隐私、低延迟的大语言模型部署的关键，而存储 I/O 瓶颈是主要障碍。LeanStream 的推测与精化策略提供了一种实用途径，可在避免先前方案中冗余权重读取与缓存开销的同时，将 GPU 计算与权重加载重叠，从而显著提升端侧推理的内存效率与速度。

title: Knowing, and Saying It Only When Asked: LLM Endognostics and the Schizognosis of Minerva-7B
summary: This paper introduces LLM endognostics, a white-box internal auditing framework that extracts and causally manipulates latent knowledge in the residual stream, applied to Minerva-7B-Instruct-v1.0. Behavioral evaluation fails to distinguish the members of 63.7% of 124 minimal prompt pairs (95% CI [55.0%, 71.6%]), yet a Jacobian-lens projection reveals a statistically significant Contrastive Endognostic Margin, showing robust internal risk differentiation. In a second protocol crossing 25 facts with five linguistic framings, the model conforms to presupposed falsehoods in 72% of cases while representing the true entity in its latent layers; ablating the planted falsehood direction restores the correct answer in 11 of 25 suppressed cases (McNemar p = 0.0010, blind human annotation kappa = 0.68). A linear probe reaches 77% accuracy at layer 10, but its orthogonal ablation yields 0% recovery, establishing that linear decodability is decoupled from causal control over verbalization.
significance: The results show that behavioral evaluation and internal reading can systematically disagree for aligned language models, so auditing should combine internal probing with causal interventions rather than rely on outputs alone. The 77% probe accuracy paired with 0% recovery also warns that successful decoding is not evidence that a representation controls what the model says.

zh.title: 知道，且只在被问及时说出：大语言模型内诊（LLM Endognostics）与 Minerva-7B 的精神分裂认知（Schizognosis）
zh.summary: 本文提出大语言模型内诊（LLM endognostics），一个白盒内部审计框架，用于提取并因果操控残差流（residual stream）中的潜在知识，并将其应用于 Minerva-7B-Instruct-v1.0。在 124 组最小化提示对上，行为评估无法区分其中 63.7% 的配对（95% CI [55.0%, 71.6%]）中的两个成员；然而，通过 Jacobian 透镜（Jacobian lens）投影可发现统计显著的对比内诊边际（Contrastive Endognostic Margin），表明模型内部具有稳健的风险区分能力。在第二套协议中，将 25 个事实与五种语言框架交叉测试，模型在 72% 的情形下顺从被预设的虚假前提，尽管其潜在层中仍表征着真实实体；对植入的虚假方向进行外科式消融后，25 个被压制案例中有 11 个恢复正确答案（McNemar p = 0.0010，盲评人工标注一致率 kappa = 0.68）。线性探针（linear probe）在第 10 层达到 77% 准确率，但对其做正交消融后恢复率为 0%，由此确立线性可解码性与言语化（verbalization）的因果控制相互脱钩。
zh.significance: 这些结果表明，对齐语言模型的行为评估与内部读取可能系统性不一致，因此审计应把内部探测与因果干预结合起来，而不应只依赖模型输出。探针 77% 的准确率伴随 0% 的恢复率也警示：成功解码并不意味着该表征实际控制模型的表述内容。
zh.aiRoleDescription: 研究人员报告 Minerva-7B-Instruct-v1.0 在 63.7% 的最小提示对上行为一致，但其内部仍对风险做出区分；切除所植入虚假信息的方向后，25 个被抑制案例中有 11 个恢复了正确答案，从而证明线性可解码性与对言语输出的因果控制相分离。
zh.humanContribution: 人类设计并构建了 endognostics 审计框架，制作了 124 个提示对与 25 乘 5 的事实框架协议，并通过盲法人工标注对结果进行验证。

title: Scaled Idempotence in Transformer Attention: Paired OV Geometry and Shared-Value Algebras
summary: We identify a recurrent algebraic regularity in Transformer attention: a sparse subset of effective OV operators $T=OV^\top$ nearly closes under composition, $T^2\approxαT$. Across six pretrained endpoints spanning 2.8B--235B parameters, 3.98--8.00% of heads reach squared closure alignment $\mathcal{P}\geq0.9$, while no matched within-layer O/V mismatch does. An exact principal-coordinate factorization, $T=Q_OKQ_V^\top$ and $T^2=Q_O(KDK)Q_V^\top$, separates within-support transport from read--write return geometry. Across all 7,304 heads in nine MHA/GQA models, scrambling only the orientation of $K$ while preserving singular values, norms, factor spans, and principal angles reduces median closure from 0.336 to $1.04\times10^{-4}$; trained orientation wins for 98.64% of heads and in every layer. Constructive searches show that high closure is feasible in every surveyed layer, but usually not attained. Retrospective trajectories in three independently trained lineages further separate broadly available capacity from the orientations attained by final strong heads. Under exact value sharing, headwise closure extends to a right-action algebra, $T_iT_j=α_jT_i$. Seven-model experiments verify the approximate law and reveal distinct oblique projections with a shared value-defined kernel. These results characterize scaled idempotence as a sparse trained orientation within broadly available geometric capacity and show how value sharing extends a headwise relation into a local operator algebra.

zh.title: Transformer 注意力中的缩放幂等性（Scaled Idempotence）：配对 OV 几何与共享值代数（Shared-Value Algebras）
zh.summary: 我们在 Transformer 注意力中识别出一种反复出现的代数规律：一小组有效 OV 算子 $T=OV^\top$ 近似在合成下封闭，$T^2\approxαT$。在参数量覆盖 2.8B–235B 的六个预训练端点中，3.98–8.00% 的注意力头达到平方闭合对齐 $\mathcal{P}\geq0.9$，而任何配对的同层 O/V 错配均未达到。精确的主坐标分解（principal-coordinate factorization）$T=Q_OKQ_V^\top$ 与 $T^2=Q_O(KDK)Q_V^\top$，将支持集内传输与读—写返回几何分离开来。在九个 MHA/GQA 模型的全部 7,304 个头中，仅打乱 $K$ 的取向而保持奇异值、范数、因子子空间与主角不变，就使中位闭合度从 0.336 降至 $1.04\times10^{-4}$；训练所得取向在 98.64% 的头中胜出，并在每一层均如此。构造性搜索表明，高闭合度在所调查的每一层都可实现，但通常并未达到。对三个独立训练谱系的回溯轨迹进一步区分了广泛可用的几何能力与最终强头实际获得的取向。在精确值共享（value sharing）下，逐头闭合推广为右作用代数（right-action algebra），$T_iT_j=\alpha_jT_i$。七模型实验验证了这一近似定律，并揭示出具有共享值定义核的不同斜投影（oblique projection）。这些结果将缩放幂等性刻画为广泛可用几何能力中的一种稀疏、由训练决定的取向，并展示了值共享如何把逐头关系扩展为局部算子代数（local operator algebra）。
zh.significance: 这些发现把注意力 OV 电路中的经验现象提炼为精确的代数结构，使研究人员能够量化哪些注意力头在何种意义上近似幂等，以及这种结构是被训练塑造的、而非由几何容量自动保证的。把"能力"与"训练所得取向"区分开来，为可解释性分析、模型比较与训练动态研究提供了可操作的指标；而值共享所导出的局部算子代数，则说明看似独立的注意力头如何组织成协调的读写机制，为理解多头协同、模型结构与潜在的结构化设计或剪枝策略奠定基础。

title: Neural Symbollic Regression Using Deep Learning and Sparse Modelling
summary: This work introduces a Neural Symbolic Regression (NSR) framework that uses neural networks as functional preconditioners for symbolic discovery. A decoupled pipeline first learns a smooth, noise-robust approximation of the target function in an interaction-aware nonlinear feature space, after which LASSO extracts sparse, interpretable closed-form expressions. Hyperparameter optimization integrated with Ray Tune and ASHA scheduling improves predictive accuracy and symbolic fidelity. Experiments on the Nguyen benchmark suite show consistent gains over SINDy and non-tuned neural baselines in RMSE, noise robustness, and out-of-distribution generalization, while ablation studies confirm the importance of feature interactions, neural depth, and tuning strategies.
significance: The framework addresses scalability and noise sensitivity in Genetic Programming and the fixed feature library dependency of SINDy, offering a scalable and interpretable route to sparse equation discovery. By linking neural approximation with symbolic extraction, it advances automated, human-readable model discovery for scientific machine learning.

title: StudyBench: Can Self-Evolution Squeeze Textbooks for Olympiad Capability?
summary: StudyBench is a controlled physics benchmark that measures how efficiently a self-evolution method converts raw training material into transferable problem-solving capability. Its Application Set of difficult textbook problems tests absorption, while its Transfer Set of olympiad-level problems tests transfer. Across three base models, gains on the Application Set rarely carry over to the Transfer Set; a guidance ablation reveals a Guidance Gap relative to supplying the same material as in-context guidance, and every method reaches a Compute Plateau well before exhausting its compute budget.
significance: The benchmark turns self-evolution progress into a measurable target by isolating learning efficiency from raw material, and the results suggest the remaining gap stems from method rather than data or compute, giving future research a clear focus. Code is available at https://github.com/thunlp/StudyBench.

zh.title: StudyBench：自我进化能压缩教材以获得奥赛能力吗？
zh.summary: StudyBench 是一个受控的物理基准，直接衡量自我进化方法将原始训练材料转化为可迁移解题能力的效率。其中 Application Set 由较难的教材习题组成，考察吸收能力，Transfer Set 由奥赛水平的题目组成，考察迁移能力。在三个基础模型上评测代表性自我进化方法后，研究发现 Application Set 上的提升很少迁移到更难的 Transfer Set；引导消融实验揭示了引导差距（Guidance Gap），即最强方法也仅弥合了同一材料以上下文引导形式提供时所能解锁能力的一小部分。此外，所有方法都触及计算高原（Compute Plateau），远在计算预算耗尽之前就趋于饱和。
zh.significance: 该基准把自我进化从开放式追求变为可测量的目标，为衡量从原始材料中学习的效率提供了直接而受控的度量。结果表明剩余差距源于方法而非数据或计算量，为后续研究指明了明确方向。代码发布于 https://github.com/thunlp/StudyBench。

title: GeoPAR: Large-Scale Multi-Agent Combinatorial Optimization with Geometry-Guided Parallel Autoregressive Learning
summary: GeoPAR is a geometry-guided parallel autoregressive reinforcement learning framework for large-scale multi-agent combinatorial optimization. It combines a projection-window sparse geometry mechanism that builds lightweight local candidate neighborhoods via multi-directional projections, sparse edge-biased attention that embeds these geometric relations into node representations, and cache-guided conflict-aware assignment that reuses the geometric cache during decoding to prevent duplicate selection of exclusive tasks. Experiments on heterogeneous vehicle routing and open multi-depot pickup-and-delivery problems show improved large-scale zero-shot generalization, fewer rollout steps, and efficient inference.
significance: Parallel autoregressive neural solvers lose accuracy on large-scale instances when local geometry is poorly modeled and conflicts are resolved only after actions are generated. GeoPAR addresses both weaknesses by injecting geometric structure early and enforcing conflict-aware assignment during decoding, offering a scalable route to stronger generalization and faster inference on large multi-agent combinatorial problems.

aiRole.description: GeoPAR, a geometry-guided parallel autoregressive reinforcement learning framework built by the authors, improves large-scale zero-shot generalization on heterogeneous vehicle routing and open multi-depot pickup-and-delivery problems while reducing rollout steps and keeping inference efficient.

humanContribution: Humans designed and built the GeoPAR framework and its three components, trained the reinforcement learning solvers, curated the problem instances, and ran the experiments evaluating performance and inference efficiency.

zh.title: GeoPAR：几何引导的并行自回归学习用于大规模多智能体组合优化
zh.summary: GeoPAR 是一个面向大规模多智能体组合优化（multi-agent combinatorial optimization）的几何引导并行自回归强化学习（reinforcement learning）框架。该方法结合三项核心组件：通过多方向投影构建轻量局部候选邻域的投影窗口稀疏几何机制，将这些几何关系注入节点表示的稀疏边偏置注意力（sparse edge-biased attention），以及在解码过程中复用几何缓存以抑制对独占任务重复选择的缓引导向冲突感知分配。在异构车辆路径问题（heterogeneous vehicle routing）和开放式多车场取送货问题（open multi-depot pickup-and-delivery）上的实验表明，GeoPAR 改善了大规模零样本泛化（zero-shot generalization），显著减少了推演步数，并保持了高效推理。
zh.significance: 并行自回归神经求解器在大规模实例上表现下降，主要源于对局部几何结构建模不足，以及冲突仅在动作生成后才被处理。GeoPAR 通过提前注入几何结构并在解码阶段实施冲突感知分配，同时针对这两项弱点加以改进，为大规模多智能体组合优化问题提供了兼顾更强泛化能力与更快推理速度的可扩展路径。
zh.aiRoleDescription: GeoPAR 是作者构建的几何引导并行自回归强化学习框架，在异构车辆路径问题和开放式多车场取送货问题上提升了大规模零样本泛化能力，同时减少了 rollout 步数并保持高效推理。
zh.humanContribution: 人类设计并构建了 GeoPAR 框架及其三个组件，训练强化学习求解器，整理问题实例，并运行评估性能与推理效率的实验。

title: Dr. Andrew Rechnitzer Appointed Head of the Department of Mathematics
summary: UBC Mathematics has appointed Dr. Andrew Rechnitzer as Head of the Department for a five-year term effective July 2026. Rechnitzer, who joined UBC in 2007, works in combinatorics and statistical mechanics, with a focus on lattice models, random walks, and exact enumeration, often developing new tools and algorithms for problems involving polymers and phase transitions. Rechnitzer earned a PhD from the University of Melbourne in 2001 and has held postdoctoral positions at York University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Melbourne. Rechnitzer also co-authored the open-source CLP Calculus textbook series and developed the open-source grading platform PLOM, and has stated that the department will examine the proper role of AI in teaching and research as the technology evolves.
significance: The appointment places a researcher with expertise in combinatorics, statistical mechanics, and algorithmic enumeration in strategic leadership of one of the world's leading mathematics departments, shaping its research and educational direction, including its approach to AI in teaching and research.

title: Dr. Christoph Ortner Appointed Director of the Institute of Applied Mathematics (IAM)
summary: UBC Mathematics announces that Dr. Christoph Ortner has been appointed Director of the Institute of Applied Mathematics (IAM) for a five-year term starting July 1, 2026. Ortner has been an IAM member since joining UBC in 2020, after serving as a professor at the University of Warwick's Mathematics Institute (2011-2020) and as an RCUK Academic Fellow at the University of Oxford (2007-2011). The research centers on the mathematical foundations of molecular and multiscale modelling, combining mathematical analysis with algorithm design and scientific applications, and includes recent work on geometric deep learning methods for molecular simulation carried out with collaborators in physics, chemistry, and materials science. As Director, Ortner aims to strengthen IAM's role as a hub linking mathematics with the physical sciences and to clarify the place of mathematics as artificial intelligence reshapes scientific research.
significance: The appointment signals continuity in IAM leadership and a stated agenda to position mathematics at the interface of artificial intelligence and scientific research, with an emphasis on mathematically grounded multiscale and molecular modelling and on cross-disciplinary work with the physical sciences.

zh.title: Christoph Ortner博士获任应用数学研究所（Institute of Applied Mathematics, IAM）所长

zh.significance: 该任命体现了IAM领导层的延续性，并提出明确的工作方向：在人工智能与科学研究的交汇处为数学定位，重点推进具有数学基础的多尺度与分子建模，以及与物理科学界的跨学科合作。

title: Twelve UBC Mathematics Faculty Members Awarded NSERC Discovery Grants
summary: UBC Mathematics announced on July 10, 2026 that twelve of its faculty members received 2026 NSERC Discovery Grants, which support long-term research in the natural sciences and engineering. The awardees and their project topics are Omer Angel on applications of discrete probability, Rodolfo Brandão on mathematical modelling of liquid sheets and filaments, Eric Cytrynbaum on mechanochemical models of developmental organization from cytoskeleton to tissue, Leah Edelstein-Keshet on modeling and simulating cell motility and cell-cell interactions from single cells to collective behaviour, Ailana Fraser on minimal submanifolds in Riemannian geometry, Kasia Jankiewicz on covers and fiberings of cell complexes, Deanna Needell on foundational machine learning, Chadi Saad-Roy on theoretical models of pathogen adaptation to new and changing host environments, Nicolle Gonzalez on combinatorics and representation theory in link homology, Pablo Shmerkin on interactions between fractal geometry, harmonic analysis and ergodic theory, Lior Silberman on projects in pure and applied mathematics, and Christoph Ortner on scientific machine learning for particle systems.
significance: The announcement documents sustained Canadian federal funding for a broad range of mathematics at UBC, spanning probability, geometry, dynamics, combinatorics and representation theory, mathematical biology, and machine learning, including projects in areas such as Riemannian geometry (minimal submanifolds), harmonic analysis, and ergodic theory.

zh.summary: 英属哥伦比亚大学数学系于2026年7月10日宣布，该系十二位教师获得2026年NSERC探索基金（NSERC Discovery Grant）。该基金旨在支持自然科学与工程领域中最有潜力推动学科发展的长期研究目标。获奖者及其课题为：Omer Angel研究离散概率（discrete probability）的应用；Rodolfo Brandão研究液膜与液丝的数学建模；Eric Cytrynbaum研究从细胞骨架到组织的发育组织力学化学模型；Leah Edelstein-Keshet研究细胞运动性与细胞间相互作用的建模与模拟，涵盖从单细胞到集体行为；Ailana Fraser研究黎曼几何（Riemannian geometry）中的极小子流形；Kasia Jankiewicz研究胞腔复形的覆叠与纤维化；Deanna Needell研究基础机器学习；Chadi Saad-Roy研究病原体适应新的及变化中的宿主环境的理论模型；Nicolle Gonzalez研究链同调（link homology）中的组合学与表示论；Pablo Shmerkin研究分形几何、调和分析与遍历理论（ergodic theory）之间更深入的相互作用；Lior Silberman从事纯粹数学与应用数学的项目；Christoph Ortner研究面向粒子系统的科学机器学习。

title: Yuhan Chu Awarded the 2026 Lorraine Schwartz Award
summary: Yuhan Chu has been awarded the 2026 Lorraine Schwartz Prize in recognition of exceptional work in mathematics and probability. Yuhan Chu graduated in May 2026 with a B.Sc., Honours in Mathematics. The prize was established in 1966 by friends and colleagues of Dr. Lorraine Schwartz, Assistant Professor in the Department of Mathematics from 1960 to 1965, and is awarded annually to an undergraduate or graduate student for distinctions in statistics and probability, on the recommendation of the Departments of Mathematics and Statistics. Announcement dated June 3, 2026.
significance: The award recognizes outstanding undergraduate achievement in mathematics and probability and highlights the departments' ongoing support for students working in statistics and probability.

title: Mathematicians call for action on AI to protect the future of the discipline
summary: Researchers from fifteen universities have issued the Leiden Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and Mathematics, urging mathematicians, research organisations and governments to act now to safeguard the core values of mathematics as AI reshapes the discipline. It highlights urgent concerns about reliability, attribution, access, and academic responsibility.
significance: The declaration shows a coordinated community effort to address how AI is changing mathematical practice and to establish shared expectations for trustworthy, fairly attributed and accessible use of AI in the discipline.

title: Maryam Mirzakhani New Frontiers Prize
summary: Anna Skorobogatova, a Clay Research Fellow, has been awarded a 2026 Maryam Mirzakhani New Frontiers Prize in recognition of notable contributions to geometric measure theory, a field that applies techniques from analysis to geometric problems such as finding surfaces of minimal area. zh.significance: 该奖项凸显了几何测度论在分析学与几何学交汇处取得的进展，并表彰了这项合作研究工作，该工作解决了该领域中一个长期悬而未决的问题。

title: Professor Uzy Smilansky, the unlikeliest archaeologist
summary: A profile of Professor Uzy Smilansky, who visited the Isaac Newton Institute for the Geometric Spectral Theory programme shortly after his 85th birthday, on his fourth visit to the Institute. The piece recounts his path from the physics of chaotic systems and mathematics into archaeology, and highlights his talent for connecting ideas across disciplines to produce breakthroughs.
significance: The profile offers insight into how methods from chaotic dynamics and geometric spectral theory can migrate into other fields, illustrating the value of long-term interdisciplinary engagement within the Institute's research programmes.

title: MIT scientists build the world’s largest collection of Olympiad-level math problems, and open it to everyone
summary: MIT scientists have assembled the world's largest collection of Olympiad-level mathematics problems, a new dataset containing more than 30,000 competition problems drawn from 47 countries. The collection is opened to everyone, serving as a harder evaluation set for AI researchers and as a training resource for students worldwide.
significance: A large, openly available corpus of high-difficulty competition problems gives the AI community a more demanding benchmark than standard mathematical problem sets, potentially revealing weaknesses in current reasoning systems. At the same time, free access offers students across the globe an unusually rich training ground that was previously scattered across national competitions.

zh.significance: 一个大规模且公开可得的高难度竞赛题目语料库，为人工智能（AI）社区提供了比标准数学题集更严苛的基准，有助于揭示当前推理系统的不足。与此同时，免费开放使全球各地的学生获得了一份异常丰富的训练资源，而这些题目此前分散于各国竞赛之中。

title: Believe in the strength of your ideas
summary: The Isaac Newton Institute hosted Dr. Reetha Thomas, a Ramanujan Fellow and postdoctoral researcher at the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore, during summer 2025. Coming from a background in the invariant analysis of nonlinear fractional partial differential equations, she now works on integrating Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) into climate and epidemiological modelling. The article covers her residency within an INI programme, the impact of the Ramanujan Fellowship, and her collaborative research on spatio-temporal climate data.
significance: The article highlights how Physics-Informed Neural Networks are being applied to pressing spatio-temporal problems in climate and epidemiology, and how sustained fellowship support and institute residencies foster cross-institutional collaboration in AI-assisted mathematical modelling.

zh.significance: 本文展示了Physics-Informed Neural Networks（PINNs）如何被用于气候与流行病学中紧迫的时空问题，也说明了持续的学者基金支持与研究所驻访如何促进AI辅助数学建模领域的跨机构合作。

title: Do Multi-Agents Solve Better Than Single? Evaluating Agentic Frameworks for Diagram-Grounded Geometry Problem Solving and Reasoning
summary: The paper systematically compares single-agent and multi-agent pipelines on four visual math benchmarks: Geometry3K, MathVerse, OlympiadBench, and We-Math. For open-source models, multi-agent design consistently improves performance: Qwen-2.5-VL (7B) gains +6.8 points and Qwen-2.5-VL (32B) gains +3.3 on Geometry3K, with further gains on OlympiadBench and We-Math. For the closed-source Gemini-2.0-Flash, single-agent mode generally performs better on the classic benchmarks, while multi-agent yields only modest improvements on the newer We-Math dataset. The authors conclude that agentic decomposition clearly benefits open-source models and can assist strong proprietary systems on newer, less familiar benchmarks, but is not universally optimal. Code, data, and reasoning files are available at the linked repository.
significance: Diagram-grounded geometry problem solving is a key benchmark for multimodal large language models, and whether multi-agent design is worth its added complexity has remained unclear. By testing multiple pipelines across four benchmarks and contrasting open-source with proprietary models, the study provides concrete evidence of when multi-agent decomposition helps and when a single agent suffices, informing both architecture choices and evaluation practice for MLLM-based geometry reasoning.

aiRole.description: The paper reports benchmark scores earned by AI systems: single-agent and multi-agent pipelines evaluated on Geometry3K, MathVerse, OlympiadBench, and We-Math, with multi-agent improving open-source models such as Qwen-2.5-VL (7B, +6.8 on Geometry3K) while Gemini-2.0-Flash often preferred single-agent mode.

humanContribution: Humans built and compared the single-agent and multi-agent agentic pipelines, curated the four visual math benchmarks and reasoning files, and evaluated the models' performance across the datasets.

zh.title: 多智能体是否更优？面向图形几何问题求解与推理（reasoning）的智能体框架评测
zh.summary: 本文在 Geometry3K、MathVerse、OlympiadBench 和 We-Math 四个视觉数学基准上系统比较了单智能体与多智能体流程。对开源模型而言，多智能体设计一致带来性能提升：Qwen-2.5-VL (7B) 在 Geometry3K 上提升 +6.8 分，Qwen-2.5-VL (32B) 提升 +3.3 分，且两个 Qwen-2.5-VL 变体在 OlympiadBench 和 We-Math 上还有进一步增益。对闭源的 Gemini-2.0-Flash 而言，单智能体模式在经典基准上总体表现更好，多智能体仅在较新的 We-Math 数据集上带来温和提升。作者得出结论：智能体化分解（agentic decomposition）对开源模型有明显收益，也能在较新、较陌生的基准上辅助强闭源系统，但并非普遍最优。代码、数据与推理文件已在链接仓库中公开。
zh.significance: 基于图形的几何问题求解是多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）的关键基准，而多智能体设计相较单智能体是否真正更优此前并不明确。该研究通过在四个基准上测试多种流程，并对比开源模型与闭源模型，给出了多智能体分解何时有益、何时单智能体已足够的具体证据，可为多模态大语言模型几何推理系统的架构选择与评测实践提供参考。
zh.aiRoleDescription: 论文报告了 AI 系统取得的基准成绩：在 Geometry3K、MathVerse、OlympiadBench 和 We-Math 上评测单智能体与多智能体流程，多智能体提升了 Qwen-2.5-VL（7B 在 Geometry3K 上 +6.8）等开源模型的表现，而 Gemini-2.0-Flash 往往在单智能体模式下更好。
zh.humanContribution: 人类构建并比较了单智能体与多智能体的 agentic 流程，整理了四个视觉数学基准与推理文件，并评测了各模型在这些数据集上的表现。

title: Achieving Olympiad-Level Geometry Large Language Model Agent via Complexity Boosting Reinforcement Learning
summary: The paper presents InternGeometry, a large language model (LLM) agent for geometry problem solving built on InternThinker-32B. The agent iteratively proposes propositions and auxiliary constructions, verifies them with a symbolic engine, and reflects on the engine's feedback, using a dynamic memory mechanism that allows over two hundred symbolic engine interactions per problem. Training employs Complexity-Boosting Reinforcement Learning (CBRL), which progressively increases the complexity of synthesized problems across stages. With 13K training examples, about 0.004% of the data used by AlphaGeometry 2, InternGeometry solves 44 of 50 International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO) geometry problems from 2000 to 2024, exceeding the average gold medalist score of 40.9. The agent also proposes novel auxiliary constructions not found in human solutions.
significance: Geometry solving has been dominated by expert systems such as AlphaGeometry 2 that depend on large-scale data synthesis and search. This work shows that an LLM agent with symbolic verification, reflective feedback, and complexity-scheduled reinforcement learning can reach medalist-level geometry performance with dramatically less training data, while generating auxiliary constructions beyond human reference solutions.

title: RLMEval: Evaluating Research-Level Neural Theorem Proving
summary: RLMEval is a new evaluation suite for research-level neural theorem proving and proof autoformalization, built from real-world Lean Blueprint formalization projects. Its 613 theorems drawn from 6 Lean projects show that gains on curated benchmarks transfer poorly to realistic research mathematics: the best evaluated model passes only 10.3% of theorems. The suite aims to guide progress in automated reasoning for formal mathematics.
significance: Existing benchmarks overstate current capabilities, hiding the difficulty LLMs face on genuine research-level formalization work. RLMEval supplies a harder, realistic testbed that can better measure and motivate advances in neural theorem proving and proof autoformalization.

zh.title: RLMEval：研究级神经定理证明评测

title: GeoSketch: A Neural-Symbolic Approach to Geometric Multimodal Reasoning with Auxiliary Line Construction and Affine Transformation
summary: GeoSketch is a neural-symbolic framework that treats geometric problem solving as a closed perception-reasoning-action loop rather than static diagram interpretation. A Perception module converts diagrams into structured logic forms, a Symbolic Reasoning module applies geometric theorems to select the next deductive step, and a Sketch Action module executes auxiliary line construction and affine transformations to update the diagram. The agent is trained with supervised fine-tuning on 2,000 symbolic-curated trajectories followed by reinforcement learning with dense symbolic rewards. The accompanying GeoSketch Benchmark contains 390 geometry problems requiring auxiliary construction or affine transformation; experiments on strong MLLM baselines show gains in stepwise reasoning accuracy and problem-solving success over static perception methods.
significance: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have struggled with geometry because they treat diagrams as fixed images, while human-style reasoning depends on actively modifying the figure and verifying each step. GeoSketch combines executable visual actions, hierarchical decision-making, and symbolic verification into one trainable agent, and supplies a dedicated benchmark of construction- and transformation-dependent problems, giving the field a concrete path from static multimodal interpretation to dynamic, verifiable visuospatial reasoning.

aiRole.description: GeoSketch, a neural-symbolic framework for geometric reasoning with auxiliary line construction and affine transformations, significantly improves stepwise reasoning accuracy and problem-solving success over static perception methods on its GeoSketch Benchmark of 390 geometry problems.

humanContribution: Humans built the Perception, Symbolic Reasoning, and Sketch Action modules, curated 2,000 symbolic trajectories for supervised fine-tuning, and designed the reinforcement learning pipeline and the GeoSketch Benchmark used for evaluation.

title: LeanGeo: Formalizing Competitional Geometry problems in Lean
summary: This work introduces LeanGeo, a unified formal system for formalizing and solving competition-level geometry problems inside the Lean 4 theorem prover. LeanGeo provides a comprehensive library of high-level geometric theorems grounded in Lean's foundational logic, supporting rigorous proof verification and seamless integration with Mathlib. The authors also present LeanGeo-Bench, a formal geometry benchmark drawn from the International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO) and other advanced sources, and evaluate state-of-the-art Large Language Models on it, exposing both their capabilities and their limitations in automated geometric reasoning. The theorem library and benchmark are released as open source.
significance: Geometry problem solving has been hard to combine with other mathematical fields because existing systems lack a unified formal framework and because diagram-based intuition resists verification. By grounding competition geometry in Lean 4 with an extensive theorem library and Mathlib compatibility, LeanGeo enables machine-checked geometry proofs that interoperate with the wider formal mathematics ecosystem. LeanGeo-Bench additionally offers a standardized testbed that measures and reveals current gaps in Large Language Model geometric reasoning, directing future work in automated theorem proving.

title: A Minimalist Proof Language for Neural Theorem Proving over Isabelle/HOL
summary: This work designs Minilang, a minimalist proof language with 10 clearly separated operations, intended to capture reasoning patterns shared by informal proofs and mechanized proofs and to ease neural theorem proving (NTP) over Isabelle/HOL. The authors build a rule-based translator from Isar to Minilang that converts roughly 340K existing proofs with about 85% success. Fine-tuning two LLMs on the translated corpus, Minilang improves pass@1 on the PISA benchmark by up to 20/29 percentage points over Isar-based LLMs with or without Sledgehammer. The resulting pass@1 reaches 69.1%, surpassing Baldur's pass@64 of 65.7%, and pass@8 reaches 79.2%, exceeding Magnushammer's state-of-the-art 71.0% on PISA.
significance: Prover-specific syntax and tactics impose a burden on LLM-based NTP that has no counterpart in informal mathematical reasoning. By minimizing this gap at the language-design level, Minilang shows that a proof language with only 10 semantically distinct operations can substantially raise LLM proof success on Isabelle/HOL, outperforming established baselines and state-of-the-art systems on PISA.

aiRole.description: LLMs finetuned on a Minilang-translated corpus of Isabelle/HOL proofs achieved a pass@1 rate of 69.1% and pass@8 rate of 79.2% on the PISA benchmark, outperforming Isar-based baselines and prior results from Baldur and Magnushammer.

humanContribution: Humans designed the Minilang proof language and its 10 operations, built a rule-based translator from Isar to Minilang, curated and translated roughly 340K existing proofs, and finetuned and evaluated the two LLMs.

zh.title: 面向 Isabelle/HOL 神经定理证明的极简证明语言
zh.summary: 本研究设计了 Minilang，一种仅含 10 个语义清晰区分操作的极简证明语言，旨在捕捉非形式化证明与机械化证明共有的推理模式，以降低在 Isabelle/HOL 上开展神经定理证明（Neural Theorem Proving, NTP）的难度。作者构建了从 Isar 到 Minilang 的规则化翻译器，将约 34 万条现有证明转换为 Minilang，成功率约 85%。研究者在翻译语料上微调两个 LLM：与基于 Isar 的 LLM（含或不含 Sledgehammer）相比，Minilang 使 PISA 基准上的 pass@1 最多提高 20/29 个百分点。最终 pass@1 达到 69.1%，超过 Baldur 的 pass@64（65.7%）；pass@8 达到 79.2%，超过 Magnushammer 在 PISA 上取得的当前最优结果（71.0%）。

zh.aiRoleDescription: 使用由 Minilang 翻译的 Isabelle/HOL 证明语料微调的两个 LLM 在 PISA 基准上取得 69.1% 的 pass@1 和 79.2% 的 pass@8，超过 Isar 基线以及 Baldur 与 Magnushammer 的既有结果。

title: Generalized Tree Edit Distance (GTED): A Faithful Evaluation Metric for Statement Autoformalization
summary: GTED (Generalized Tree Edit Distance) is a new evaluation framework for statement autoformalization that standardizes formal statements, converts them into operator trees, and measures semantic similarity with a generalized tree edit distance. On the miniF2F and ProofNet benchmarks it ranks among the top metrics, attaining the highest accuracy and Kappa on miniF2F and joint-highest accuracy on ProofNet, while remaining computationally lightweight.
significance: Robust evaluation of statement autoformalization has been hampered by metrics that are semantically shallow, expensive, or limited by automated theorem proving progress. GTED offers a faithful, low-cost alternative, and its strong benchmark results give the community a practical tool for comparing autoformalization systems.

zh.title: 广义树编辑距离（Generalized Tree Edit Distance, GTED）：语句自动形式化的忠实评估指标
zh.summary: GTED（广义树编辑距离，Generalized Tree Edit Distance）是面向语句自动形式化（statement autoformalization）的新型评估框架，其先对形式化语句进行标准化并转换为算子树，再借助同名的广义树编辑距离度量语义相似度。在 miniF2F 与 ProofNet 基准上，该方法跻身表现最佳的指标之列，在 miniF2F 上取得最高的准确率与 Kappa 值，在 ProofNet 上取得并列最高的准确率，同时保持较低的计算开销。
zh.significance: 语句自动形式化的稳健评估一直受限于现有指标缺乏语义理解、计算成本高，以及受自动定理证明（automated theorem proving）进展制约。GTED 提供了一种忠实且轻量的替代方案，其在基准上的优异表现为研究者与社区比较自动形式化系统提供了实用工具。

title: AI Mathematician: Towards Fully Automated Frontier Mathematical Research
summary: This work introduces AI Mathematician (AIM), a framework that harnesses Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) to support frontier mathematical research rather than competition-level problems. The authors identify two challenges of research-level work: intrinsic problem complexity and the requirement of procedural rigor. AIM addresses these through an exploration mechanism that fosters longer solution paths and a pessimistic reasonable verification method designed to ensure reliability. Experiments across several real-world mathematical topics report that the early version of AIM autonomously constructs substantial portions of proofs and uncovers non-trivial insights, suggesting LRM-based agent systems could accelerate mathematical research.
significance: The work shifts LLM-driven theorem proving from competition benchmarks toward open research-level mathematics, targeting the rigor and depth gaps that have limited automation so far. Its combination of extended exploration and pessimistic verification offers a concrete agent design for producing reliable partial proofs and novel insights, and its reported results on real topics point to LRM-based agents as practical accelerators for frontier mathematical discovery.

aiRole.description: The AI Mathematician (AIM) framework, harnessing Large Reasoning Models, autonomously constructs substantial portions of proofs and uncovers non-trivial insights on research-level mathematical tasks across several real-world topics.

humanContribution: Humans designed and built the AIM framework, including its exploration mechanism and pessimistic reasonable verification method, and ran the extensive experiments evaluating it on real-world mathematical topics.

title: HybridProver: Augmenting Theorem Proving with LLM-Driven Proof Synthesis and Refinement
summary: HybridProver is a unified framework that combines whole-proof synthesis and stepwise tactic-based generation in Isabelle/HOL through proof sketches as an intermediate representation, allowing partially correct proof structures to be reused while merging high-level planning with fine-grained reasoning. The authors post-train two 7B-scale LLMs on optimized Isabelle datasets and report a 73.8% success rate on the miniF2F Isabelle benchmark, improving on the previous state of the art of 61.9%. Ablation studies examine how dataset quality, training configurations, and sampling strategies affect proof generation.
significance: The work shows that lightweight 7B models, coupled with a hybrid proof generation strategy, can outperform prior results on a standard Isabelle benchmark without depending on very large LLMs, potentially lowering the cost of AI-assisted formal verification and reducing the manual effort that limits adoption of formal methods. The ablation analysis also offers practical guidance on data and training choices for LLM-driven theorem proving.

aiRole.description: HybridProver's post-trained 7B-scale LLMs generated Isabelle/HOL proofs on the miniF2F benchmark, achieving a 73.8% success rate and surpassing the previous state of the art of 61.9%.

humanContribution: Humans designed the HybridProver framework, built and optimized the Isabelle datasets, and post-trained the two 7B-scale LLMs; they also ran ablation studies on data quality, training configurations and sampling strategies.

zh.title: HybridProver：以大语言模型驱动的证明合成与优化增强定理证明

title: Ineq-Comp: Benchmarking Human-Intuitive Compositional Reasoning in Automated Theorem Proving on Inequalities
summary: The paper introduces Ineq-Comp, a benchmark of elementary inequality problems built by systematic transformations such as variable duplication, algebraic rewriting, and multi-step composition, designed to test whether LLM-based formal proof assistants in Lean can recognize and combine known inequalities such as AM/GM. Most evaluated provers, including Goedel, STP, and Kimina-7B, struggle with these problems despite their ease for humans. DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B is relatively robust but still drops 20% at pass@32, and DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B retains a gap between compositional variants and seed problems, so model scaling alone does not remove the weakness. Performance remains poor even when formal proofs of the constituent parts are given in context, which the authors read as evidence that the deficit lies in compositional reasoning itself.
significance: Compositional use of standard tools is a core part of how humans solve inequality problems, so current provers failing on human-easy variants reveals a generalization gap that larger models do not close. The benchmark offers a controlled diagnostic, separating surface difficulty from compositional structure, and its open data and evaluation code give the community a reproducible way to measure progress in automated theorem proving on inequalities.

aiRole.description: The authors introduce Ineq-Comp, a benchmark of compositional inequality problems in Lean, and report pass@32 scores showing that AI provers such as Goedel, STP, Kimina-7B and DeepSeek-Prover-V2 struggle on compositional variants, with performance remaining poor even when formal proofs of constituent parts are…

humanContribution: Humans built the benchmark from elementary inequalities through systematic transformations, including variable duplication, algebraic rewriting and multi-step composition, and evaluated the provers' Lean proof attempts. The data and evaluation code were released by the authors.

title: A Combinatorial Identities Benchmark for Theorem Proving via Automated Theorem Generation
summary: LeanComb is a manually constructed Lean benchmark for combinatorial identities, presented as the first formalized theorem proving benchmark for this subject. The team develops ATG4CI, which combines candidate tactics suggested by a self-improving LLM with Reinforcement Learning Tree Search for tactic prediction, yielding LeanComb-Enhanced with 260K combinatorial identity theorems, each with a complete Lean proof. Models trained on this dataset generate more effective tactics and achieve higher automated theorem proving success rates.
significance: The scarcity of high-quality training data limits LLM-based formal theorem proving in complex domains, and combinatorics is especially challenging for automated methods. This work provides a large verified corpus of formalized combinatorial identities together with a generation pipeline that improves tactic quality and proof success, offering concrete training and evaluation resources for theorem proving in Lean.

title: Scaling Natural-Language Graph-Based Test Time Compute for Automated Theorem Proving
summary: This work introduces KG-Prover, a framework that augments general-purpose large language models with knowledge graphs mined from reputable mathematical texts to help identify key concepts and construct and formalize proofs in natural language. The authors study the scaling of graph-based test-time compute and report gains over baselines: general-purpose LLMs improve by up to 21% on miniF2F-test when combined with KG-Prover, with consistent improvements of 2-11% across ProofNet, miniF2F-test, and MUSTARD, and KG-Prover with o4-mini reaches 50% on miniF2F-test. The approach requires no additional finetuning.
significance: Automated theorem proving demands multi-step logical reasoning, concept identification, and correct proof formalization in natural language, and this work shows that external knowledge graphs can deliver sizable, consistent gains across multiple benchmarks without finetuning. The reported scaling trends suggest that graph-based test-time compute is a practical and promising direction for strengthening natural-language proof reasoning with general-purpose LLMs.

aiRole.description: KG-Prover, a framework combining knowledge graphs mined from mathematical texts with general-purpose LLMs, improves automated theorem proving benchmarks, raising scores by up to 21% on miniF2F-test and reaching 50% pass rate on miniF2F-test with o4-mini.

humanContribution: Humans built the KG-Prover framework, mined and curated the knowledge graphs from reputable mathematical texts, and ran evaluations on the ProofNet, miniF2F-test and MUSTARD datasets.

summary: This work presents a systematic pipeline for improving large language models on the Bangla AI mathematical challenge benchmark, covering evaluation of diverse LLM configurations, fine-tuning on targeted datasets, and integration of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to raise reasoning accuracy in a multilingual setting. significance: Math Olympiad problems demand multi-step reasoning that remains difficult for LLMs, especially in low-resource languages such as Bangla. Evidence that tailored prompting, data augmentation, retrieval augmentation, and iterative reasoning yield gains suggests practical routes for building stronger non-English mathematical reasoning systems.

title: HunyuanProver: A Scalable Data Synthesis Framework and Guided Tree Search for Automated Theorem Proving
summary: HunyuanProver is a language model finetuned from Hunyuan 7B for interactive automatic theorem proving with LEAN4. To address data sparsity, the authors design a scalable framework that iteratively synthesizes training data at low cost, together with guided tree search algorithms intended to enable system 2 thinking in the prover. The system reports state-of-the-art results on major benchmarks, with a 68.4% pass rate on miniF2F-test versus the previous best of 65.9%, and it proves four IMO statements in miniF2F-test: imo_1960_p2, imo_1962_p2, imo_1964_p2, and imo_1983_p6. The team plans to open-source a dataset of 30k synthesized instances, each containing the natural-language question, the autoformalized statement, and the proof produced by HunyuanProver.
significance: A scalable, low-cost data synthesis pipeline directly targets the training data bottleneck in automated theorem proving, and the reported benchmark gains suggest the approach is competitive with existing methods. The combination of guided tree search and stronger benchmark performance, including results on several historical IMO problems, advances LEAN4-based proving systems, while release of the 30k instance dataset would give the community reusable training data spanning autoformalization and machine-generated proofs.

zh.title: HunyuanProver：自动化定理证明的可扩展数据合成框架与引导式树搜索
zh.summary: HunyuanProver 是一个基于 Hunyuan 7B 微调的语言模型，用于 LEAN4 上的交互式自动定理证明（Automated Theorem Proving）。为缓解数据稀疏问题，作者设计了一个可扩展框架，以低成本迭代合成训练数据，并设计了引导式树搜索算法，使证明器具备"系统2思维"。该系统在主要基准测试中报告了当前最优（SOTA）性能，在 miniF2F-test 上通过率达到 68.4%，此前最优结果为 65.9%，并在 miniF2F-test 中证明了四个 IMO 命题：imo_1960_p2、imo_1962_p2、imo_1964_p2 和 imo_1983_p6。为惠及社区，研究团队将开源一个包含 3 万条合成实例的数据集，每条实例包含自然语言原始问题、经自动形式化转换后的陈述，以及由 HunyuanProver 给出的证明。

title: A Lean Dataset for International Math Olympiad: Small Steps towards Writing Math Proofs for Hard Problems
summary: The authors write complete original Lean formal proofs for the IMO problems in the miniF2F test set that previously lacked them, plus 3 extra problems from IMO 2022 and 2023, adding 5,880 lines of Lean proof to the public domain. They further decompose these proofs into 1,329 lemmas spanning more than 40k lines of Lean code, forming a dataset of intermediate proof steps, and evaluate SOTA LLMs on it while analyzing their success and failure modes. Code and data are released at https://github.com/roozbeh-yz/IMO-Steps.
significance: The work closes a gap in publicly available formal proofs for hard competition problems and supplies an evaluation benchmark of approachable intermediate lemmas rather than only end-to-end proof tasks. This makes it possible to diagnose where proof-writing models fail and to track incremental progress toward systems that can automatically prove IMO problems and harder ones.

title: FormalAlign: Automated Alignment Evaluation for Autoformalization
summary: FormalAlign is introduced as the first automated framework for evaluating alignment between natural and formal languages in autoformalization. It jointly trains on the autoformalization sequence generation task and on representational alignment between input and output, using a dual loss that couples the two mutually reinforcing tasks. Across four benchmarks augmented with proposed misalignment strategies, FormalAlign surpasses GPT-4, with an Alignment-Selection Score of 99.21% versus 88.91% on Forml-Basic (11.58% higher) and 66.39% versus 64.34% on MiniF2F-Valid (3.19% higher). Dataset and code are publicly released.
significance: Manual verification of semantic agreement between informal proofs and their formalizations is a major bottleneck for scaling autoformalization. By automating this alignment check with quality competitive with or exceeding GPT-4, FormalAlign could substantially cut verification effort and support higher-throughput, more reliable proof formalization.

title: ImProver: Agent-Based Automated Proof Optimization
summary: The paper introduces automated proof optimization: rewriting a formal proof so that it remains correct while optimizing an arbitrary user-defined criterion such as length, readability, style, or modularity. The authors present ImProver, a large-language-model agent that rewrites Lean proofs toward such metrics. Because naive LLM approaches perform poorly on this task, ImProver adds several components: a novel Chain-of-States technique that injects symbolic Lean context into the agent's reasoning, error correction, and retrieval. Evaluation on real-world undergraduate, competition, and research-level mathematics theorems shows ImProver can produce proofs that are substantially shorter, more modular, and more readable.
significance: Optimized formal proofs are valuable for downstream uses such as training and evaluating proof models, where human-written proofs may not be well suited. This work defines a new problem class, automated proof optimization, and supplies a first working agent-based method, Chain-of-States, that makes symbolic prover context usable by language-model agents. Demonstrated gains in proof length, modularity, and readability suggest a practical path toward automatically curating and improving formal proof corpora.

title: Diagram Formalization Enhanced Multi-Modal Geometry Problem Solver
summary: The paper presents DFE-GPS (Diagram Formalization Enhanced Geometry Problem Solver), a framework that combines visual features, geometric formal language, and natural language representations to help multimodal large language models (MLLMs) interpret geometric diagrams. Because vision encoders trained on natural scenes handle such diagrams poorly, the authors propose a synthetic data method producing SynthGeo228K, a large-scale geometry dataset annotated with both formal and natural language captions, used to fine-tune the vision encoder for geometric structures. The framework reportedly improves MLLM performance on geometric diagrams and extends their use to open-ended tasks on the formalgeo7k dataset.
significance: Effective representation of geometric relationships is a persistent bottleneck, with multimodal models often no better than text-only LLMs on diagram-based problems. A large synthetic dataset paired with formal and natural language annotations offers a scalable way to teach vision encoders geometric structure, while the formal language component may improve reliability and interpretability of diagram reasoning. The extension to open-ended tasks on formalgeo7k suggests broader applicability beyond multiple-choice-style geometry solving.

title: Fuse, Reason and Verify: Geometry Problem Solving with Parsed Clauses from Diagram
summary: This paper presents PGPSNet-v2, a neural-symbolic solver for plane geometry problem solving (PGPS) built around three stages: modal fusion, reasoning, and knowledge verification. Textual clauses parsed from diagrams capture fine-grained structural and semantic content and are fused with the written problem through structural-semantic pre-training. An interpretable solution program is generated autoregressively by a self-limited decoder, and a multi-level theorem verifier discards solutions inconsistent with geometric principles, reducing neural hallucination. The authors also introduce PGPS9K, a large-scale dataset annotated with textual clauses, solution programs, and knowledge tuples. Experiments on Geometry3K and PGPS9K show PGPSNet outperforming existing symbolic and neural solvers while retaining explainability and reliability, with each component ablated and shown effective.
significance: Reliable geometry solving needs more than answer accuracy: it needs interpretable reasoning steps and checks against established theorems. By combining diagram parsing into clauses with an explicit solution program and a theorem-based verifier, PGPSNet-v2 targets hallucination in neural solvers while remaining inspectable. The PGPS9K dataset adds fine-grained annotations that can support training and analysis of multimodal reasoning and knowledge application, and the reported gains over symbolic and neural baselines suggest the pipeline advances both performance and trustworthiness in geometry problem solving.

aiRole.description: The authors' PGPSNet-v2 neural-symbolic solver generates solution programs for plane geometry problems and outperforms existing symbolic and neural solvers on Geometry3K and PGPS9K, with its fusion, reasoning and verification components shown effective.

humanContribution: Humans designed and built PGPSNet-v2, curated the annotated PGPS9K dataset, and ran the experiments that justified the solver components and measured its GPS performance.

zh.title: 融合、推理与验证：基于图解析子句的几何问题求解
zh.summary: 本文提出用于平面几何问题求解（plane geometry problem solving, PGPS）的神经-符号求解器PGPSNet-v2，包含多模态融合、推理过程和知识验证三个阶段。由图解析得到的文本子句刻画几何图的细粒度结构与语义内容，并通过结构-语义预训练与题目文本高效融合。推理阶段采用可解释的解法程序描述几何推理过程，由自限性解码器（self-limited decoder）自回归生成该程序；为减少解法错误，作者提出多层次定理验证器，剔除不符合几何原理的解法，从而缓解神经模型的幻觉。作者还构建了大规模几何问题数据集PGPS9K，包含文本子句、解法程序和涉及知识三元组的细粒度标注。在Geometry3K和PGPS9K上的大量实验表明，PGPSNet的求解性能优于现有符号求解器与神经求解器，同时保持良好的可解释性与可靠性，融合、推理、验证各组件均被验证有效。
zh.significance: 可靠的几何求解不仅需要正确答案，还需要可解释的推理步骤以及与已知定理的核对。PGPSNet-v2将图解析子句、显式解法程序与基于定理的验证器相结合，在保持结果可审查的同时抑制神经求解器的幻觉。PGPS9K提供的细粒度标注可用于多模态推理与知识应用的训练与分析，而相对符号方法与神经方法的性能提升表明该流程在几何问题求解（GPS）中同时推进了性能与可信度。

title: Reliable Evaluation and Benchmarks for Statement Autoformalization
summary: This work addresses the shortage of reliable metrics, datasets, and standards for statement autoformalization into formal languages such as Lean 4. It introduces BEq+, an automated metric strongly correlated with human judgment, and ProofNetVerif, a dataset of 3,752 annotated examples for assessing metric quality. Two benchmarks are also developed: ProofNet#, a corrected version of ProofNet, and RLM25, containing 619 research-level mathematics pairs from six formalization projects. Experiments show up to 45.1% accuracy on undergraduate mathematics, while research-level content remains difficult without proper context.
significance: Robust evaluation is essential for tracking genuine progress in statement autoformalization. The proposed metric, metric-assessment dataset, and corrected and research-level benchmarks provide a common evaluation foundation, while the experiments clarify both the current capabilities of autoformalization systems and their limitations on research mathematics.

aiRole.description: The work introduces BEq+ (an automated evaluation metric), the ProofNetVerif dataset, and the ProofNet# and RLM25 benchmarks, and reports that current autoformalization techniques reach up to 45.1% accuracy on undergraduate mathematics while struggling with research-level content without proper context.

humanContribution: Humans designed the metrics, curated and annotated the datasets, built and corrected the benchmarks, and carried out the systematic evaluation of autoformalization techniques.

zh.title: 可靠的陈述自动形式化评估与基准

title: An Evaluation Benchmark for Autoformalization in Lean4
summary: This paper introduces an evaluation benchmark for autoformalization in Lean4, a mathematical programming language, and applies it to test state-of-the-art large language models including GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Gemini Pro. The analysis shows that these models still have limitations in autoformalization, especially in more complex areas of mathematics, motivating further model development.
significance: A rigorous Lean4-based benchmark gives the field a standardized way to measure autoformalization progress and reveals where current models fall short, helping direct future improvements toward reliable machine-assisted formalization of mathematics.

aiRole.description: The paper introduces an evaluation benchmark for autoformalization in Lean4 and reports performance of GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Gemini Pro on it, finding that these LLMs still show limitations in autoformalization, especially in more complex areas of mathematics.

humanContribution: Humans designed and constructed the Lean4 benchmark, selected the LLMs to evaluate, and analyzed their autoformalization capabilities.

title: Verification and Refinement of Natural Language Explanations through LLM-Symbolic Theorem Proving
summary: This paper presents Explanation-Refiner, a neuro-symbolic framework that combines Large Language Models (LLMs) with Theorem Provers (TPs) to generate and formalise explanatory sentences and suggest inference strategies for Natural Language Inference (NLI). The TP checks the logical validity of the explanations and supplies feedback for iterative refinement. The authors show how the framework can jointly assess the explanatory reasoning, autoformalisation, and error correction capabilities of state-of-the-art LLMs while automatically improving explanation quality across domains and levels of complexity.
significance: Validating natural language explanations for NLI usually relies on crowd-sourced datasets that are slow to build and prone to logical errors. By anchoring LLM-generated explanations in formal verification, the work offers a scalable route to machine-checked evaluation and automated refinement of multi-step reasoning, with relevance to explanation quality in mathematical and logical domains.

title: Wu's Method can Boost Symbolic AI to Rival Silver Medalists and AlphaGeometry to Outperform Gold Medalists at IMO Geometry
summary: This note revisits the IMO-AG-30 Challenge introduced with AlphaGeometry and reports that Wu's method is far stronger than the previously reported baseline. Wu's method alone solves 15 of 30 problems, including some solved by no other method. Combining Wu's method with classic synthetic techniques — deductive databases and angle, ratio, and distance chasing — solves 21 of 30 problems on a CPU-only laptop with a 5-minute limit per problem, four fewer than AlphaGeometry and the first fully symbolic baseline rivaling an IMO silver medalist. Wu's method also solves 2 of the 5 problems AlphaGeometry missed, so combining AlphaGeometry with Wu's method reaches 27 of 30, a new state of the art that outperforms an IMO gold medalist.
significance: The results overturn the impression that Wu's method is a weak baseline for olympiad geometry and show that a fully symbolic pipeline, requiring no large-scale synthetic training, approaches neuro-symbolic performance. Complementarity between symbolic and neural methods yields the best reported IMO-AG-30 result, suggesting that hybrid theorem-proving systems can surpass human medal-level performance on olympiad geometry.

aiRole.description: The note reports benchmark results on the IMO-AG-30 Challenge: Wu's method alone solves 15 of 30 problems, a fully symbolic combination solves 21, and combining AlphaGeometry with Wu's method sets a new state of the art at 27 of 30, outperforming an IMO gold medalist.

humanContribution: Humans designed and implemented the Wu's method and classic synthetic proving components, and built and trained the AlphaGeometry neuro-symbolic model with 100 million synthetic samples; they also curate and define the IMO-AG-30 benchmark used for evaluation.

zh.significance: 这些结果推翻了Wu's method在奥林匹克几何中只是弱基线的印象，并表明完全符号化的推理流程无需大规模合成训练即可接近神经符号（neuro-symbolic）方法的性能。符号方法与神经方法的互补性带来了IMO-AG-30上目前最好的结果，说明混合式定理证明系统在奥林匹克几何上可以达到并超过人类奖牌水平。

title: Don't Trust: Verify -- Grounding LLM Quantitative Reasoning with Autoformalization
summary: The paper proposes grounding large language model quantitative reasoning by prompting models to autoformalize informal math statements and their solutions into Isabelle code, which is then checked automatically for internal consistency. Solutions whose formalized versions are inconsistent with themselves or with the formalized problem statement are rejected. Evaluations on GSM8K, MATH, and MultiArith show the method consistently beats vanilla majority voting, previously the best correctness-identification heuristic, by more than 12% on GSM8K, with gains across all datasets and model sizes. Code is released at the given GitHub repository.
significance: LLMs such as Minerva and GPT still produce unjustified logical and computational errors, so reliably identifying correct answers is a central bottleneck. Autoformalization-based verification offers a cheap, automatic filter that outperforms majority voting and scales across model sizes, moving mathematical reasoning toward verifiable rather than merely plausible solutions.

title: Enhancing Formal Theorem Proving: A Comprehensive Dataset for Training AI Models on Coq Code
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive dataset for training Large Language Models (LLMs) on Coq code, built from over 10,000 Coq source files and covering a wide range of propositions, proofs, and definitions, enriched with metadata such as source references and licensing information. The goal is to help LLMs generate syntactically correct and semantically meaningful Coq constructs. Initial experiments show improved accuracy in Coq code generation after training on the data, with one fine-tuned LLM producing 141 valid proofs for a basic lemma, illustrating the dataset's capacity to support diverse and valid proof strategies. The paper describes the dataset's composition, its construction methodology, and implications for machine learning in formal verification. The dataset is publicly available on Hugging Face.
significance: Coq's specialized syntax and semantics remain a challenge for general-purpose LLMs, limiting progress in automated theorem proving. A large, well-documented corpus with licensing and provenance metadata gives the community reusable training material for mathematically rigorous code generation, and the reported 141 valid proofs for a single lemma suggest such data can elicit a breadth of proof strategies rather than one memorized answer. The public release lowers the barrier to further research on AI-assisted formal verification.

aiRole.description: The authors released a dataset of Coq propositions, proofs, and definitions and reported that models trained on it achieved higher accuracy in Coq code generation, including one fine-tuned LLM that generated 141 valid proofs for a basic lemma.

humanContribution: Humans curated the dataset from over 10,000 Coq source files with metadata and licensing information, and built and fine-tuned the LLMs evaluated in the experiments.

title: Apriori Knowledge in an Era of Computational Opacity: The Role of AI in Mathematical Discovery
summary: This philosophical paper endorses Burge's view that Appel and Haken could acquire apriori knowledge of the Four Color Theorem from their computer program because that program automated ordinary human mathematical reasoning. The authors argue that the computational opacity of modern LLMs and DNNs blocks comparable apriori knowledge, but that attaching a proof-checker which automates human forms of proof-checking restores access to such knowledge, even though the underlying machines remain opaque and the proofs they produce may not be human-surveyable.
significance: The paper clarifies when AI-assisted proofs can yield genuine mathematical knowledge rather than mere testimony, highlighting proof-checking and formal verification as the mechanism that makes opaque systems epistemically usable. This bears directly on how the community should treat AI-generated proofs whose reasoning is not human-inspectable.

zh.title: 计算不透明时代中的先验知识：人工智能在数学发现中的作用
zh.summary: 这篇哲学论文赞同 Burge 的观点：Appel 和 Haken 能够从其计算机程序中获得关于四色定理（Four Color Theorem）的先验知识（apriori knowledge），因为该程序只是自动化了人类常规的数学推理形式。作者论证说，现代 LLMs 与 DNNs 的计算不透明性阻碍了以类似方式获得这种先验知识；但如果在这类机器上附接一个自动化人类证明检查形式的证明检查器，那么即便原初机器对我们完全不透明、且其输出的证明本身可能并非人类可通览的，我们仍可从中获得先验的数学知识。
zh.significance: 本文厘清了 AI 辅助证明在何种条件下能够产生真正的数学知识，而非仅仅是证词，并指出证明检查与形式化验证是使不透明系统在认识论上可用的关键机制。这直接关系到学界应如何对待那些推理过程无法由人类检视的 AI 生成证明。

title: Enhancing Neural Theorem Proving through Data Augmentation and Dynamic Sampling Method
summary: The paper introduces DS-Prover, a dynamic sampling method for neural theorem proving that adjusts the number of tactics used to expand the current goal according to the remaining proving time relative to the total allocated budget, rebalancing exploration and exploitation as time runs down. It also augments the training data by decomposing simplification and rewrite tactics with multiple premises into single-premise tactics, giving the model more examples and improving its prediction of tactics with premises. Experiments use the Mathlib dataset for Lean and are evaluated on MiniF2F and ProofNet, with significant gains reported: Pass@1 of 14.2% on ProofNet, described as state of the art, and 29.8% on MiniF2F, slightly above the best-reported Lean result of 29.6%.
significance: Efficient proof search under a time budget is a central bottleneck in LLM-based interactive theorem proving, and DS-Prover offers a simple time-aware control signal for tactic expansion that can be layered on existing provers. The premise-decomposition augmentation targets a concrete weakness in tactic prediction, and the gains on both ProofNet and MiniF2F show the approach transfers across benchmarks rather than overfitting to one evaluation set.

zh.title: 通过数据增强与动态采样方法增强神经定理证明
zh.summary: 本文提出面向定理证明的动态采样方法 DS-Prover，该方法根据剩余时间占证明总时间预算的比例，动态决定扩展当前目标所应用的策略（tactic）数量，从而随时间推移调整探索与利用之间的平衡。作者还通过将含多个前提的化简策略与重写策略分解为单前提策略来增强训练数据，使模型获得更多学习样本，从而更准确地预测带前提的实验。实验使用 Lean 定理证明器的 Mathlib 数据集，并在 MiniF2F 与 ProofNet 两个标准数据集上评测：ProofNet 上 Pass@1 达到 14.2%，被报告为当前最优；MiniF2F 上达到 29.8%，略高于此前基于 Lean 的最佳 Pass@1 29.6%。
zh.significance: 在时间预算约束下进行高效证明搜索，是基于大语言模型（LLM）的交互式定理证明中的核心瓶颈，DS-Prover 为策略扩展提供了一个简单且感知时间的控制信号，可叠加到现有证明器之上。面向前提的分解式数据增强针对策略预测中的具体薄弱环节，而在 ProofNet 与 MiniF2F 上的性能提升表明该方法可跨基准迁移，而非过拟合于单一评测集。
zh.aiRoleDescription: 作者的神经定理证明系统 DS-Prover 结合 LLM 策略生成与 Lean 检查，并采用动态采样与数据增强，在 ProofNet 上取得 14.2% 的 Pass@1，在 MiniF2F 上取得 29.8%，略高于此前使用 Lean 的最佳报告结果 29.6%。
zh.humanContribution: 人类构建并训练了该系统，设计了动态采样方法与策略分解数据增强，并从 Mathlib 数据集中整理训练数据，在 MiniF2F 和 ProofNet 上进行评估。
