title: Automated Planning Techniques for Elementary Proofs in Abstract Algebra
summary: This paper applies automated planning to automated theorem proving, implementing basic implications, equalities, and rules in both deterministic and non-deterministic domains to model commutative rings and deduce elementary results about them. The initial implementation's success suggests that established automated planning techniques transfer to the newer field of automated theorem proving, which in turn offers automated planning a new challenging domain.
significance: The work connects automated planning and automated theorem proving, showing that planning can construct elementary proofs in abstract algebra and offering new proof construction tooling for formal mathematics while providing automated planning research with a demanding new test domain.

aiRole.description: An automated planning system was used to construct elementary proofs and deduce elementary results about commutative rings, modeled in both deterministic and non-deterministic domains. The reported results suggest that automated planning techniques apply to elementary proofs in abstract algebra.

humanContribution: Humans implemented the basic implications, equalities, and rules that model commutative rings and set up the deterministic and non-deterministic planning domains.

zh.title: 面向抽象代数初等证明的自动规划技术
zh.summary: 本文将自动规划（automated planning）应用于自动定理证明（automated theorem proving），在确定性与非确定性域中实现基本蕴含、等式和规则，以对交换环（commutative rings）建模并推导其初等结论。初步实现的成功表明，成熟的自动规划技术适用于相对新兴的自动定理证明领域，而自动定理证明反过来也为自动规划提供了新的挑战性应用域。
zh.significance: 该工作连接了自动规划与自动定理证明，表明规划技术可在抽象代数（abstract algebra）中构造初等证明，既为形式数学的证明构造提供了新的工具路径，也为自动规划研究提供了富有挑战性的新应用领域。
zh.aiRoleDescription: 一个自动规划系统用于构造初等证明，并在确定性与非确定性域中推导有关交换环的基本结果。报告结果表明，自动规划技术适用于抽象代数中的初等证明。
zh.humanContribution: 研究人员实现了用于建模交换环的基本蕴含、等式和规则，并搭建了确定性与非确定性的规划域。

title: Multilingual Mathematical Autoformalization
summary: This work introduces MMA, a large, flexible, multilingual and multi-domain dataset of informal-formal mathematical statement pairs, built by having a language model translate in the reverse direction from formal statements to informal ones to overcome the scarcity of parallel data. Language models fine-tuned on MMA produce statements acceptable with minimal corrections on the miniF2F and ProofNet benchmarks at a rate of 16–18%, up from 0% for the base model. The experiments further show that fine-tuning on multilingual formal data yields more capable autoformalization models even when they are applied to monolingual tasks.
significance: MMA addresses the data bottleneck that has limited autoformalization research, offering a scalable alternative to manually curated corpora and few-shot prompting. The reported gains on miniF2F and ProofNet, together with the transfer benefit of multilingual formal data to monolingual settings, suggest that dataset construction via reverse translation is a practical route to stronger autoformalization systems.

title: LLMSTEP: LLM proofstep suggestions in Lean
summary: LLMSTEP is a tool for integrating a language model into the Lean proof assistant. Implemented as a Lean 4 tactic, it sends the user's proof state to a server hosting a language model, whose generated suggestions are checked in Lean and displayed in the development environment. The work provides a baseline language model plus code for fine-tuning and evaluation, along with server implementations running on CPU, a CUDA GPU, or a Google Colab notebook.
significance: The tool brings language model proofstep suggestions directly into the Lean workflow, with suggestions verified inside Lean before being shown to the user. The released baseline, training and evaluation code, and flexible server deployments lower the barrier to developing and using fast, effective suggestions for mathematical reasoning.

zh.title: LLMSTEP：Lean 中的 LLM 证明步骤建议
zh.summary: 本文提出 LLMSTEP，一个将语言模型（language model）集成到 Lean 证明助手（Lean proof assistant）中的工具。LLMSTEP 是一个 Lean 4 tactic，可将用户的证明状态发送到托管语言模型的服务器，模型生成的建议会在 Lean 中检验，并显示在用户的开发环境中。作者提供了一个基线语言模型，以及用于微调和评估的代码，还提供了可在 CPU、CUDA GPU 或 Google Colab 笔记本上运行的服务器实现。
zh.significance: 该工具将 LLM 证明步骤建议直接嵌入 Lean 工作流，建议先经 Lean 检验再呈现给用户。公开的基线模型、训练与评估代码以及多样化的服务器部署方式，降低了开发和使用快速、有效数学推理建议的门槛。

title: FormalGeo: An Extensible Formalized Framework for Olympiad Geometric Problem Solving
summary: FormalGeo presents the first stage of a three-year effort: a consistent formal plane geometry system guided by the geometry formalization theory (GFT). The framework contains 88 geometric predicates and 196 theorems for representing, validating, and solving IMO-level geometry problems, and it integrates with modern AI models to produce deductive proofs that are readable, traceable, and verifiable. The authors also provide FGPS (formal geometry problem solver), written in Python, usable both as an interactive verification assistant and as an automatic solver, together with the formalgeo7k dataset of 6,981 problems (133,818 after augmentation) and the formalgeo-imo dataset of 18 IMO-level problems (2,627 after augmentation and growing). All annotated problems include formal language descriptions and solutions, and a backward depth-first search method reaches a 2.42% problem-solving failure rate, with deep learning techniques suggested to lower it further.
significance: A formal, verifiable substrate for IMO-level geometry lets AI reasoning be checked step by step instead of accepted on trust, addressing a key barrier to using language models in rigorous mathematical problem solving. The framework's extensible predicate-theorem library, the FGPS implementation, and the annotated training and challenge datasets give the community reusable infrastructure and benchmarks for studying how formal systems, search, and deep learning can be combined on olympiad geometry.

zh.title: FormalGeo：一个用于奥林匹克几何问题求解的可扩展形式化框架
zh.summary: FormalGeo 是过去三年一系列工作的首篇论文，提出了几何形式化理论（geometry formalization theory, GFT），并据此构建了一套一致的形式化平面几何（plane geometry）系统。该框架包含 88 个几何谓词和 196 条定理（theorems），可用于表示、验证并求解 IMO 水平的几何问题，并能与现代 AI 模型无缝集成，生成可读、可追溯、可验证的演绎推理证明。研究者还用 Python 实现了 FGPS（formal geometry problem solver），既可作为验证解题过程的交互式助手，也可作为自动求解器；同时标注了 formalgeo7k 和 formalgeo-imo 两个数据集，前者含 6,981 道几何题（数据增强后为 133,818 道），后者含 18 道 IMO 水平的几何难题（增强后为 2,627 道并持续增加）。所有标注题目均含详细的形式语言描述与解答，采用后向深度优先搜索方法时问题求解失败率仅为 2.42%，并可结合深度学习技术进一步降低。
zh.significance: 为 IMO 水平几何提供形式化且可验证的推理基础，使 AI 的解题过程可以逐步核查而非凭信任接受，这缓解了将大语言模型用于严格数学问题求解的关键障碍。该框架可扩展的谓词-定理库、FGPS 实现以及带标注的训练与挑战数据集，为研究形式系统、搜索与深度学习如何在奥赛几何中协同工作提供了可复用的基础设施和评测基准。

title: math-PVS: A Large Language Model Framework to Map Scientific Publications to PVS Theories
summary: This work examines how large language models could formalize advanced mathematical concepts and proposes math-PVS, a framework that combines LLMs with the PVS proof assistant to bridge textual descriptions in research papers and formal specifications in PVS. Through data ingestion and conversion mechanisms, the authors envision math-PVS as an automated process for extracting and formalizing mathematical theorems from research papers, supporting critical review and checking of mathematical reasoning.
significance: Automating the mapping from natural-language mathematics to formal PVS specifications could make formalization of research-level mathematics more scalable and enable machine-checked scrutiny of reasoning in published papers. The approach addresses known LLM weaknesses in logic by coupling them with a proof assistant, potentially aiding mathematical discovery and academic review if the envisioned pipeline is realized.

title: MLFMF: Data Sets for Machine Learning for Mathematical Formalization
summary: MLFMF is a collection of benchmark data sets for recommendation systems that support mathematical formalization with proof assistants such as Agda and Lean. Drawing on major libraries including Mathlib, the Agda standard library, Agda-unimath, and TypeTopology, each data set encodes a library both as a heterogeneous network of modular structure and references between entries and as s-expressions of the syntax trees of all entries. The collection covers over 250,000 entries, making it the largest machine-learnable corpus of formalized mathematical knowledge to date, and includes baseline results from graph and word embeddings, tree ensembles, and instance-based learning.
significance: Proof assistants rely on humans to identify reusable theorems, constructions, datatypes, and postulates, and MLFMF supplies standardized data for training and evaluating systems that automate this retrieval step. The extraction methodology generalizes to other libraries and proof assistants, so the data sets can anchor broader research on machine learning approaches to formalized mathematics.

title: TRIGO: Benchmarking Formal Mathematical Proof Reduction for Generative Language Models
summary: TRIGO is an automated theorem proving (ATP) benchmark that requires a generative language model to reduce a trigonometric expression step by step, exercising reasoning about formulas as well as manipulation, grouping, and factoring of numeric terms. The authors collect trigonometric expressions and their reduced forms from the web, manually annotate the simplification process, and translate the annotations into the Lean formal language system, then automatically generate additional examples to expand the dataset. A generator built on Lean-Gym produces splits of varying difficulty and distribution to probe generalization. Experiments show that TRIGO remains challenging for advanced generative language models, including GPT-4 despite its exposure to large amounts of open-source formal theorem-proving language data.
significance: Existing ATP benchmarks emphasize symbolic inference and largely neglect complex number combination reasoning, so TRIGO fills a gap by testing whether generative models can carry out genuine formula manipulation inside a formal system. The annotated Lean dataset, its automatic expansion, and the difficulty-controlled Lean-Gym splits provide a reusable resource for studying how formal and mathematical reasoning abilities develop and generalize.

zh.title: TRIGO：面向生成式语言模型的形式数学证明化简（formal mathematical proof reduction）基准
zh.summary: TRIGO 是一个自动定理证明（automated theorem proving, ATP）基准，要求生成式语言模型对三角表达式进行逐步化简，以检验模型对公式的推理能力，以及对数值项进行操作、分组和因式分解的能力。研究者从网络上收集三角表达式及其化简结果，人工标注化简过程，并将其翻译为 Lean 形式化语言系统，随后通过自动生成额外样本来扩充数据集。团队还基于 Lean-Gym 开发了自动生成器，构造出难度与分布各异的数据划分，以深入分析模型的泛化能力。实验表明，TRIGO 对包括 GPT-4 在内的先进生成式语言模型构成了新的挑战，尽管 GPT-4 在预训练阶段接触过大量开源形式化定理证明语言数据；该基准也为研究生成式语言模型的形式化与数学推理能力提供了新工具。
zh.significance: 现有的自动定理证明基准大多聚焦符号推理，很少涉及复杂的数组合推理，因此 TRIGO 填补了这一空白，检验生成式模型能否在形式化系统中完成真正的公式操作。带标注的 Lean 数据集、自动扩充机制以及难度可控的 Lean-Gym 数据划分构成可复用的研究资源，有助于认识形式化推理与数学推理能力如何发展和泛化。

title: Lyra: Orchestrating Dual Correction in Automated Theorem Proving
summary: Lyra is a framework for automated theorem proving that pairs Large Language Models with two correction mechanisms. Tool Correction (TC) applies predefined prover tools such as Sledgehammer in post-processing to replace incorrect tool calls and mitigate hallucinations; Conjecture Correction (CC) uses prover error messages as feedback to refine proof conjectures through instruction-based generation without collecting paired generation-error-refinement prompts. Lyra reaches state-of-the-art results on miniF2F, raising validation accuracy from 48.0% to 55.3% and test accuracy from 45.5% to 51.2%, and solves 3 IMO problems.
significance: The work addresses two persistent weaknesses of language models in formal theorem proving, hallucinated tool usage and unrefined conjectures, by combining a knowledge-guided post-processing step with environment-driven error feedback. The miniF2F gains and 3 IMO solutions suggest that orchestrating complementary correction mechanisms is a practical route toward stronger automated provers, and the authors position both mechanisms as directions for further research.

zh.title: Lyra：编排自动定理证明中的双重修正
zh.summary: Lyra 是一个用于自动定理证明（automated theorem proving）的框架，将大型语言模型（Large Language Models, LLMs）与两种修正机制结合。工具修正（Tool Correction, TC）在后处理阶段利用预定义的证明器工具（如 Sledgehammer）替换错误的工具调用，从而缓解幻觉；猜想修正（Conjecture Correction, CC）将证明器的错误信息作为反馈，通过基于指令的生成来精炼证明猜想，且无需收集配对的生成-错误-修正提示。Lyra 在 miniF2F 上取得当前最优（SOTA）结果，验证集准确率从 48.0% 提升至 55.3%，测试集从 45.5% 提升至 51.2%，并解决了 3 道 IMO 题目。
zh.significance: 该工作针对语言模型在形式化定理证明中的两个长期难题——幻觉式的工具使用与未经打磨的猜想——提出了结合知识引导的后处理步骤与由环境驱动的错误反馈的方案。miniF2F 上的提升和 3 道 IMO 题目的求解表明，将互补的修正机制协同编排是增强自动证明器的一条可行路径，作者也将这两种机制列为未来研究方向。
zh.aiRoleDescription: Lyra 框架结合工具修正（Tool Correction）与猜想修正（Conjecture Correction）进行自动定理证明，在 miniF2F 验证集（48.0% 提升至 55.3%）和测试集（45.5% 提升至 51.2%）上取得最先进性能，并解决了 3 道 IMO 题目。
zh.humanContribution: 人类设计并构建了 Lyra 框架及其两种修正机制，包括定义 Sledgehammer 等预定义证明工具，以及建立与证明器错误信息的交互流程。

title: FIMO: A Challenge Formal Dataset for Automated Theorem Proving
summary: FIMO is a dataset of 149 formal problem statements drawn from the International Mathematical Olympiad Shortlisted Problems, targeted at advanced automated theorem proving (automated theorem proving) at the IMO level. The statements are formalized in Lean and are paired with informal problem descriptions and corresponding LaTeX-based informal proofs. Initial experiments with GPT-4 reveal significant limitations in current methods, suggesting that satisfactory IMO-level automated theorem proving remains a distant goal.
significance: Benchmark datasets at olympiad difficulty are scarce, and FIMO supplies 149 formalized IMO Shortlisted Problems with aligned informal statements and proofs, giving the theorem proving community a demanding testbed for prover tooling and interaction. Its reported GPT-4 baselines indicate that existing approaches fall well short of IMO-level performance, offering a concrete measure of the remaining gap.

title: Automated theorem proving in first-order logic modulo: on the difference between type theory and set theory
summary: This note examines resolution modulo, a first-order theorem proving method that can be used both with first-order presentations of simple type theory, also called higher-order logic, and with set theory. When applied to certain first-order presentations of type theory, the method reproduces higher-order resolution exactly. The author compares how the method behaves on type theory versus set theory.
significance: The comparison clarifies how a single first-order proving technique interacts with two different foundational frameworks, showing when a first-order tool matches higher-order resolution and where set theory requires different treatment. This informs both the design of automated provers and the choice of foundations for formalized mathematics.

zh.title: 一阶逻辑模等价下的自动定理证明：论类型论与集合论的差异
zh.summary: 本笔记考察模等价归结（resolution modulo），这是一种一阶定理证明（theorem proving）方法，既可应用于简单类型论（simple type theory，又称高阶逻辑（higher-order logic））的一阶表述，也可应用于集合论（set theory）。当它被用于某些类型论的一阶表述时，能精确模拟高阶归结（higher-order resolution）。作者比较了该方法在类型论与集合论上的表现差异。
zh.significance: 这一比较澄清了单一的一阶证明技术如何与两种不同的基础框架相互作用，说明了一阶工具在何种情况下与高阶归结一致，以及集合论在何处需要不同的处理方式。这对自动定理证明器的设计以及形式化数学基础框架的选择均有参考价值。

title: An Ensemble Approach for Automated Theorem Proving Based on Efficient Name Invariant Graph Neural Representations
summary: The paper introduces NIAGRA, an ensemble Name InvAriant Graph RepresentAtion for automated theorem proving. It combines improved Graph Neural Networks that learn formula representations invariant to the names appearing in statements with an efficient ensemble proof search strategy. Experiments across multiple datasets from different domains show state-of-the-art performance, with gains up to 10% over the best learning-based methods, while transfer learning experiments report improvements of up to 28%.
significance: Name dependence has limited the transferability of learning-based theorem proving systems between domains, and representation size and theory scope trade-offs have constrained runtime efficiency. NIAGRA addresses both issues and demonstrates strong cross-domain transfer, suggesting more reusable and efficient neural theorem provers.

title: Solving Math Word Problems by Combining Language Models With Symbolic Solvers
summary: The paper combines a large language model (LLM) that incrementally formalizes math word problems as variables and equations with an external symbolic solver that solves them. The approach matches the original PAL method on the GSM8K benchmark and beats PAL by an absolute 20% on ALGEBRA, a new dataset of harder word problems extracted from Algebra textbooks. The authors argue that declarative, incremental representations are beneficial when interfacing with external tools.
significance: Earlier tool-using methods such as PAL are biased toward simple procedural problems and struggle with declarative reasoning. Showing strong gains on harder algebra word problems points toward more reliable step-by-step solution generation for education, and the released data and prompts support further research.

title: A Multi-Modal Neural Geometric Solver with Textual Clauses Parsed from Diagram
summary: This work introduces PGPSNet, a neural geometric solver that converts diagrams into basic textual clauses to better represent diagram features and fuse multi-modal information. The method combines structural and semantic pre-training, data augmentation, and self-limited decoding to endow the model with knowledge of geometry theorems and geometric representations, improving geometric understanding and reasoning. The authors also build PGPS9K, a large-scale fine-annotated geometry problem solving dataset with fine-grained diagram annotations and interpretable solution programs. Experiments on PGPS9K and Geometry3K show PGPSNet outperforms state-of-the-art neural solvers. Code, dataset, and appendix are released at https://github.com/mingliangzhang2018/PGPS.
significance: The work addresses two persistent weaknesses of neural geometry solvers, namely diagram representation and multi-modal fusion, by translating diagrams into symbolic textual clauses that are more amenable to reasoning. The release of PGPS9K with fine-grained annotations and interpretable solution programs provides a valuable benchmark for evaluating geometric understanding rather than answer accuracy alone, and the reported gains on PGPS9K and Geometry3K indicate the approach generalizes across datasets.

title: EuclidNet: Deep Visual Reasoning for Constructible Problems in Geometry
summary: EuclidNet 是一个针对尺规作图可构造问题（constructible problems in geometry）的深度学习框架，使用 Mask R-CNN 从初始配置与目标配置（含新增的交点）中提取视觉特征，并以递归方式生成构造步骤作为中间数据模型，用于训练过程中的反馈以进一步改进构造步骤序列。该循环持续进行，直至找到解，此时框架回溯路径以输出逐步作图指南，或将问题判定为不可解。研究者在复杂的日本算额（Sangaku）几何题上验证了该框架。
significance: Straightedge-and-compass construction is a longstanding challenge for automated geometry theorem proving, where the search space over construction sequences grows quickly and visual structure is hard to exploit. EuclidNet couples visual feature extraction with recursive refinement and backtracking, and its evaluation on Sangaku problems suggests neural visual reasoning can handle nontrivial construction tasks with interpretable step-by-step outputs.

aiRole.description: EuclidNet, a deep learning framework using Mask R-CNN and recursive backtracking, generates straightedge-and-compass construction sequences for geometric construction problems and is validated on complex Japanese Sangaku problems.

humanContribution: Humans designed and built the EuclidNet framework and its training process, and curated the Sangaku problems used for validation.

title: A Formalization of Doob's Martingale Convergence Theorems in mathlib
summary: This work presents a formalization in mathlib, for the Lean theorem prover, of Doob's martingale convergence theorems, which give conditions under which (sub)martingales converge almost everywhere or in L^1. Supporting developments include a definition of conditional expectation in Banach spaces and a theory of stochastic processes, stopping times, and martingales. As an application, the work also formalizes Lévy's generalized Borel-Cantelli lemma, drawing on mathlib's topology, analysis, and measure theory.
significance: The development supplies reusable formal infrastructure for conditional expectation, stochastic processes, stopping times, and martingales, while establishing one of the first substantial treatments of probability theory in mathlib. Formalizing Doob's convergence theorems and a generalized Borel-Cantelli lemma demonstrates that the library can support central probabilistic arguments and creates foundations for further verified probability theory.

zh.title: mathlib 中 Doob 鞅收敛定理的形式化
zh.summary: 本工作为 Lean 定理证明器的 mathlib 库形式化了 Doob 鞅收敛定理（Doob's martingale convergence theorems），这些定理给出（次）鞅几乎处处或在 L^1 中收敛的条件。为此构建的成果包括巴拿赫空间（Banach spaces）中的条件期望（conditional expectation）定义，以及随机过程（stochastic processes）、停时（stopping times）与鞅（martingales）的理论。作为应用，工作还形式化了 Lévy 广义 Borel-Cantelli 引理（Lévy's generalized Borel-Cantelli lemma），并利用了 mathlib 的拓扑学、分析学与测度论（measure theory）等多个组成部分。
zh.significance: 这一发展为条件期望、随机过程、停时与鞅提供了可复用的形式化基础设施，同时构成了 mathlib 中概率论（probability theory）最早的重要工作之一。对 Doob 鞅收敛定理和广义 Borel-Cantelli 引理的形式化，表明该库能够支持概率论中的核心论证，并为进一步验证概率论奠定基础。

title: UniGeo: Unifying Geometry Logical Reasoning via Reformulating Mathematical Expression
summary: UniGeo is a large-scale unified geometry benchmark containing 4,998 calculation problems and 9,543 proving problems, where each proving problem is annotated with a multi-step proof including reasons and mathematical expressions that can be reformulated into a proving sequence sharing the format of program sequences for calculation problems. The authors propose Geoformer, a unified multi-task Geometric Transformer that solves both tasks via sequence generation, and a Mathematical Expression Pretraining (MEP) method that predicts the mathematical expressions appearing in solutions. On UniGeo, Geoformer achieves state-of-the-art results, exceeding the task-specific model NGS by over 5.6% accuracy on calculation problems and 3.2% on proving problems.
significance: Treating geometry calculation and proving under a single sequence-generation formulation reveals that their shared representations and overlapping mathematical knowledge can improve a deep model's reasoning on both tasks. The benchmark, unified architecture, and expression-based pretraining offer a reusable resource and methodology for multi-modal geometric reasoning research.

aiRole.description: The Geoformer unified multi-task Geometric Transformer achieved state-of-the-art results on the UniGeo benchmark, outperforming task-specific model NGS by over 5.6% and 3.2% accuracy on calculation and proving problems.

humanContribution: Humans constructed and annotated the UniGeo benchmark with multi-step proofs and program sequences, and designed and trained the Geoformer framework and the Mathematical Expression Pretraining method.

zh.title: UniGeo：通过重构数学表达式统一几何逻辑推理
zh.summary: UniGeo 是一个大规模统一几何问题基准，包含 4,998 道计算题和 9,543 道证明题，其中每道证明题均标注了包含理由和数学表达式的多步证明，且该证明可被重构为与计算题标注程序序列格式一致的证明序列。作者提出统一的多任务 Geometric Transformer 框架 Geoformer，以序列生成方式同时求解两类问题，并提出数学表达式预训练（Mathematical Expression Pretraining, MEP）方法，通过预测解答中出现的数学表达式来改进 Geoformer。在 UniGeo 上，Geoformer 取得当前最优性能，在计算题和证明题上的准确率分别超过专用任务模型 NGS 5.6% 和 3.2% 以上。

title: End-to-end Symbolic Regression with Transformers
summary: The paper trains a Transformer to directly predict a complete symbolic expression including its numerical constants, replacing the usual two-step pipeline of predicting an expression skeleton and then fitting constants. The predicted constants can initialize a non-convex optimizer, and ablations show the end-to-end approach improves results, sometimes without refinement. Evaluated on SRBench, the model approaches state-of-the-art genetic programming while running several orders of magnitude faster at inference.
significance: The work shows neural sequence models can compete with genetic programming on symbolic regression, enabling fast equation discovery and combining learned expression prediction with classical constant fitting. This advances equation discovery and automated mathematical discovery.

aiRole.description: The authors present a Transformer that directly predicts full mathematical expressions, constants included, for symbolic regression, with ablations showing better results and SRBench evaluation approaching state-of-the-art genetic programming with much faster inference.

humanContribution: Humans designed, built and trained the Transformer model, ran the ablations and benchmark evaluation, and performed the optional refinement of predicted constants via a non-convex optimizer.

title: A Unified Framework for Deep Symbolic Regression
summary: The paper identifies five solution strategy classes for symbolic regression—recursive problem simplification, neural-guided search, large-scale pre-training, genetic programming, and linear models—and hybridizes them into a single modular, unified framework. Evaluated on SRBench across 252 ground-truth and black-box benchmark problems, both noiseless and at various noise levels, the framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in symbolically recovering analytical expressions, fitting datasets accurately, and balancing accuracy against complexity. Extensive combinatorial ablation studies support practical, use-case-based guidance for constructing hybrid symbolic regression algorithms.
significance: Rather than advancing one strategy family in isolation, the work shows that combining heterogeneous symbolic regression strategies in a modular design leads the field across complementary goals on a shared benchmark. The ablations and use-case guidance give practitioners concrete criteria for choosing and assembling strategy combinations.

title: Towards Autoformalization of Mathematics and Code Correctness: Experiments with Elementary Proofs
summary: The paper presents an autoformalization method built on the Universal Transformer architecture that translates elementary natural-language proofs into Coq formalizations. Experiments on artificial and human-written proofs within a limited domain report good generalization to intermediate proof lengths absent from training and to variations in natural language.

title: Tracing and Manipulating intermediate values in Neural Math Problem Solvers
summary: The paper introduces a method for analyzing how Transformer models process complex inputs by focusing on simple arithmetic problems and their intermediate values. Using principal component analysis (PCA), the authors trace where information about intermediate values is encoded in model activations, then perform a causal intervention by manipulating model weights. The intervention shows that the identified weights are causally related to model predictions rather than merely correlated with intermediate values, revealing that the model exhibits locality to certain intermediate values and thereby improving model interpretability.
significance: The work addresses an open gap in understanding how language models carry out multi-step inference, going beyond correlational probing to establish a causal link between internal representations of intermediate values and model behavior. The tracing-plus-intervention approach offers a concrete tool for making neural math problem solvers more interpretable and for checking whether extracted intermediate information is genuinely used during reasoning.

title: Formalising the Krull Topology in Lean
summary: The authors present a formalisation in the Lean 3 theorem prover of the Krull topology on the Galois group of an infinite Galois extension, along with a proof that this topology is profinite. significance: Making the Krull topology and its profinite structure available in a proof assistant supplies foundational infrastructure for later formal work on infinite Galois theory and Galois representations, and is a step toward mechanising ingredients of the Langlands Program.

title: Constrained Training of Neural Networks via Theorem Proving
summary: The paper presents a theorem proving method for specifying and generating temporal logical constraints used to train neural networks. A deep embedding of linear temporal logic over finite traces (LTL_f) and its evaluation function are formalised in the higher-order logic of Isabelle. A loss function L is then formalised and proved sound and differentiable to a function dL. Using Isabelle's automatic code generation, OCaml versions of LTL_f, L, and dL are produced and connected to PyTorch through OCaml bindings for Python. Applied to an existing deep learning framework for dynamic movement, the approach yields expected results on movement specification patterns such as obstacle avoidance and patrolling, providing a fully rigorous route to constrained training rather than ad hoc implementations of logical components in a language such as Python.
significance: Rigorously verified logical constraints could reduce correctness risks when spec-driven constraints are embedded in neural network training pipelines. The work also demonstrates a practical bridge from formal proofs in Isabelle to executable code usable inside mainstream deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch.

zh.title: 通过定理证明进行神经网络的约束训练

zh.significance: 严格验证的逻辑约束有助于降低将规格驱动的约束嵌入神经网络训练流程时的正确性风险。这项工作还展示了从 Isabelle 中的形式化证明到可执行代码、再接入 PyTorch 等主流深度学习框架的实用路径。

title: Proving Theorems using Incremental Learning and Hindsight Experience Replay
summary: This paper presents a first-order logic automated theorem prover in which all of the smart clause-scoring heuristics of the state-of-the-art E prover are disabled and replaced by a neural clause scorer. The network is trained in an incremental learning setting using hindsight experience replay, a reinforcement learning technique adapted to reuse the intermediate data produced by unsuccessful proof attempts. Clauses are represented as graphs and fed to transformer networks with spectral features. On the MPTP2078, M2k, and Mizar40 benchmarks, the resulting prover surpasses previous machine learning approaches and competes with E in its best configuration, while generating proofs that are almost always significantly shorter.
significance: The work recycles data from failed proof attempts instead of discarding it, addressing the scarcity of proof data and the lack of a smooth difficulty gradient in theorem proving datasets. It also shows that a learned clause scorer can replace the handcrafted heuristics of a leading prover without relying on that prover to bootstrap training, and that the produced proofs are substantially shorter, which is valuable for downstream formalization and verification tasks.

humanContribution: The authors designed the hindsight-based incremental learning approach, disabled E's handcrafted clause-scoring heuristics and replaced them with a transformer-based graph clause-scoring network, and evaluated the resulting prover on the standard benchmarks.

zh.title: 使用增量学习与事后经验回放证明定理

title: Deep symbolic regression for recurrence prediction
summary: This paper trains Transformers to perform symbolic regression, inferring the function or recurrence relation behind sequences of integers or floats, a task common in human IQ tests but rarely studied in the machine learning literature. The integer model, evaluated on a subset of OEIS sequences, outperforms built-in Mathematica functions at recurrence prediction, while the float model produces informative approximations of out-of-vocabulary functions and constants, such as bessel0(x) approximately equal to (sin(x)+cos(x))/sqrt(pi x) and 1.644934 approximately equal to pi^2/6.
significance: Inferring exact recurrences and closed-form expressions from data is central to mathematical discovery, and surpassing specialized computer algebra tools such as Mathematica on OEIS sequences shows that sequence-to-formula prediction is becoming feasible. The float model's ability to approximate unseen functions and recognize constants like pi^2/6 also suggests such systems could support conjecture formation and experimental mathematics beyond their training vocabulary.

aiRole.description: The paper reports that its trained Transformers infer recurrence relations and functions underlying integer and float sequences, outperform built-in Mathematica functions on an OEIS subset and yielding approximations such as bessel0(x) ≈ (sin(x)+cos(x))/√(πx) and 1.644934 ≈ π²/6.

title: From Width-Based Model Checking to Width-Based Automated Theorem Proving
summary: The paper develops a general, modular framework that converts a broad class of width-based model-checking algorithms in parameterized complexity into procedures testing the validity of graph-theoretic conjectures on graph classes of bounded width. The framework applies to several established width measures, including treewidth and cliquewidth. As a quantitative application, the authors show analytically that for several long-standing graph-theoretic conjectures there is an algorithm which, given k, decides in time double-exponential in k^{O(1)} whether the conjecture holds on all graphs of treewidth at most k. These bounds, interpretable as upper bounds on the size of proofs or disproofs on treewidth-k graphs, substantially improve on previous theoretical bounds.
significance: The work builds a bridge from model-checking technology to automated theorem proving, turning algorithmic parameterized complexity into a tool for establishing or refuting conjectures on structured graph classes. The double-exponential bounds in treewidth give the first quantitatively sharper guarantees for the size of counterexamples or certificates on bounded-treewidth graphs, and the modular design suggests the approach can be reused across width measures and conjectures.

zh.title: 从基于宽度的模型检测到基于宽度的自动定理证明

zh.significance: 这项工作在模型检测与自动定理证明（automated theorem proving）之间建立桥梁，把参数化复杂性的算法工具转化为在结构化图类上判定或反驳猜想的手段。树宽下的双指数上界首次给出了有界树宽图上反例或证明规模的更精细定量保证，而模块化设计表明该方法可在不同宽度度量和猜想之间复用推广。

title: Mechanising Gödel-Löb provability logic in HOL Light
summary: The paper presents a HOL Light formalisation of the metatheory of Gödel-Löb provability logic (GL), establishing soundness and completeness with respect to possible world semantics. The modal completeness proof adapts the argument from George Boolos' 1995 monograph to HOL Light, overcoming the technical difficulty that GL is non-compact. Building on this formalisation, the authors implement a prototype theorem prover for GL as a HOL Light tactic mimicking proof search in the labelled sequent calculus G3KGL; it acts as a decision algorithm, producing a HOL Light theorem for valid input formulas and extracting a falsifying model for invalid ones. The paper discusses the formal completeness code and the proof search design, with examples of interactive and automated use.
significance: This work delivers both a rigorous mechanised metatheory for an important provability logic and a certified decision procedure on top of it, so GL theorems can be established inside a trusted proof assistant and refutations can be witnessed by explicit countermodels. The handling of non-compactness in a modal completeness proof offers reusable technique for formalising other non-compact logics, and the tactic-based integration shows how proof search can feed back into interactive theorem proving.

zh.title: 在 HOL Light 中机械化 Gödel-Löb 可证性逻辑

title: Seeking Patterns, Not just Memorizing Procedures: Contrastive Learning for Solving Math Word Problems
summary: Math Word Problem solving requires recovering quantitative relations from natural-language narratives, yet current models often memorize procedures and exploit shallow heuristics. The paper attributes this to a lack of global understanding of MWP patterns and shows that semantic representations already cluster by shared prototype equations, with misaligned representations tending to yield wrong solutions. The authors propose a contrastive learning approach that makes the network perceive divergence between patterns: prototype equations are converted into trees, similar tree structures are collected as contrastive examples, and the solver is trained with an auxiliary objective that pulls together representations of problems sharing similar prototypes. Experiments on the Chinese dataset Math23k and the English dataset MathQA show large gains in both monolingual and multilingual settings.
significance: The work targets a core failure of neural MWP solvers, shallow heuristic generalization instead of structural understanding, and offers a training signal grounded in equation structure rather than surface semantics. Improved cross-lingual results suggest the learned pattern awareness transfers beyond a single dataset or language, making the approach relevant for robust mathematical reasoning in language models.

aiRole.description: The paper presents a contrastive learning approach for neural math word problem solving and reports that the trained model greatly improves performance on the Math23k and MathQA benchmarks in monolingual and multilingual settings.

humanContribution: Humans designed the contrastive learning method, converted prototype equations into trees to collect contrastive examples, trained the solving model with an auxiliary objective, and ran the benchmark experiments.

zh.title: 不只是记忆解题程序，而是寻找模式：面向数学应用题求解的对比学习
zh.summary: 数学应用题（Math Word Problem, MWP）的求解需要从自然语言叙述中发现数量关系，但现有模型往往记忆解题程序并依赖浅层启发式规则。本文将此归因于对题目模式缺乏整体理解，并指出仅凭语义得到的表示已会按共享的原型方程聚拢，而偏离这些原型或贴近其他原型的表示往往导致错误解答。作者提出一种对比学习（contrastive learning）方法，使网络感知模式之间的差异：将原型方程转换为树结构（tree），检索相似的树结构以收集对比样本，并用辅助目标训练求解模型，使具有相似原型的题目表示相互拉近。在中文数据集 Math23k 与英文数据集 MathQA 上的实验显示，该方法在单语和多语设置下均大幅提升性能。
zh.significance: 该工作针对神经网络数学应用题求解器的核心缺陷，即以浅层启发式泛化代替对结构的理解，并提出一种以方程结构而非表面语义为依据的训练信号。跨语言实验中性能的提升表明，所学到的模式感知能力可迁移到单一数据集或语言之外，对语言模型的稳健数学推理具有参考价值。

title: Formalization of a Stochastic Approximation Theorem
summary: This paper gives a formal proof in the Coq proof assistant of a general convergence theorem due to Aryeh Dvoretzky in stochastic approximation. The theorem implies convergence of important classical methods such as the Robbins-Monro and Kiefer-Wolfowitz algorithms. In the process, the authors build a comprehensive Coq library for measure-theoretic probability theory and stochastic processes.
significance: Formalizing a central stochastic approximation theorem in Coq provides machine-checked foundations for convergence arguments used across adaptive signal processing and machine learning, including Stochastic Gradient Descent. The accompanying probability library is reusable for future formal work on stochastic processes and learning algorithms.

title: A Neural Network Solves, Explains, and Generates University Math Problems by Program Synthesis and Few-Shot Learning at Human Level
summary: The work shows that a neural network pre-trained on text and fine-tuned on code can solve, explain, and generate university-level mathematics problems at a human level. Using few-shot learning, Codex automatically synthesizes programs that are executed to solve course problems with 81% automatic accuracy. The authors curate questions from MIT's largest mathematics courses and Columbia University's Computational Linear Algebra, and also solve problems from the MATH dataset. Randomly sampled questions are answered with multiple modalities including numbers, equations, and plots. GPT-3 reaches only 18.8% zero-shot and 30.8% with few-shot chain of thought prompting, while program synthesis with few-shot Codex reaches 81%, lifting previous state-of-the-art accuracy on the benchmark topics from 8.8% to 81.1%. A survey evaluates the quality and difficulty of the generated questions.
significance: The reported 81% accuracy on university course problems, versus 30.8% for the strongest text-only prompting baseline, suggests that program synthesis is a far more effective route to reliable automated mathematical problem solving than direct language model answering. The work also scales explanation and question generation for higher education mathematics, with implications for tutoring, assessment, and curriculum support.

aiRole.description: A neural network system using program synthesis with few-shot learning and OpenAI's Codex generated and executed programs that solved university-level mathematics course problems at 81% automatic accuracy, explained solutions, and generated new questions, improving benchmark accuracy from 8.8% to 81.1%.

humanContribution: Humans curated a new dataset of questions from MIT and Columbia mathematics courses, designed the program synthesis approach and prompting, and conducted a survey to evaluate the quality and difficulty of generated questions.

zh.title: 通过程序合成与少样本学习以人类水平求解、解释并生成大学数学问题的神经网络
zh.summary: 该研究表明，一个在文本上预训练、在代码上微调的神经网络可以达到人类水平，求解、解释并生成大学数学问题。借助少样本学习（few-shot learning），Codex 自动合成程序（program synthesis）并执行这些程序来求解课程问题，自动准确率达到 81%。作者从 MIT 最大的几门数学课程——单变量与多变量微积分（Single Variable and Multivariable Calculus）、微分方程（Differential Equations）、概率与统计导论（Introduction to Probability and Statistics）、线性代数（Linear Algebra）、计算机科学数学（Mathematics for Computer Science）——以及 Columbia University 的计算线性代数（Computational Linear Algebra）中整理出题目，并求解 MATH 数据集中的问题。对随机抽样的题目，作者生成包含数字、方程和图形等多种模态的解答。GPT-3 仅用零样本（zero-shot）求解 18.8%，用少样本学习结合最新的思维链提示（chain of thought prompting）达到 30.8%；而使用少样本学习的 Codex 通过程序合成达到 81%，将基准主题上此前的最优自动求解准确率从 8.8% 提升到 81.1%。作者还通过问卷评估所生成问题的质量与难度。
zh.significance: 在大学课程问题上达到 81% 的准确率，而最强的纯文本提示基线仅为 30.8%，这表明程序合成是通往可靠自动数学解题的更有效途径，远胜于让语言模型直接作答。该工作还大规模实现了高等数学的问题解释与题目生成，对辅导、考核和课程支持具有实际意义。
zh.aiRoleDescription: 一个使用程序合成、少样本学习和 OpenAI 的 Codex 的神经网络系统生成并执行程序，以 81% 的自动准确率解决大学数学课程问题，解释解答并生成新题目，将基准准确率从 8.8% 提升到 81.1%。
zh.humanContribution: 人类整理了来自 MIT 和 Columbia 数学课程的新题目数据集，设计了程序合成方法和提示方式，并开展调查以评估生成题目的质量与难度。

title: A proof system for graph (non)-isomorphism verification
summary: The paper recasts a state-of-art canonical labeling algorithm for graphs, as described by McKay and Piperno, as a formal proof system for use in interactive theorem provers. It provides an implementation that exports a proof certifying that an obtained graph is the canonical form of a given graph, and an independent checker that verifies such proofs and thereby confirms that two graphs are not isomorphic.
significance: Interactive theorem provers cannot trust unverified graph canonicalization or isomorphism-checking code unless its output is independently checkable. By turning canonical labelling into explicit proof objects checked by a separate verifier, this work makes graph (non)-isomorphism claims usable in formal development without requiring the underlying algorithm to be mechanically verified.

zh.title: 图（非）同构验证的证明系统
zh.summary: 本文将McKay和Piperno提出的图规范形标注（canonical labelling）前沿算法重新表述为一个形式证明系统（formal proof system），以便在交互式定理证明器（interactive theorem prover）中使用。作者给出一个实现，可导出证明，以证实所获得的图是指定图的规范形（canonical form）；同时提供一个独立检查器来验证这类证明，从而确认给定的两个图不同构（graph non-isomorphism）。
zh.significance: 交互式定理证明器无法信任未经验证的图规范形标注或同构检查代码，除非其输出可被独立核查。这项工作将规范形标注转化为显式证明对象，交由独立验证器检查，使图（非）同构论断无需对底层算法进行机械验证即可用于形式化开发。

title: Symbolic Regression via Deep Reinforcement Learning Enhanced Genetic Programming Seeding
summary: This work proposes a hybrid approach to symbolic regression and other combinatorial optimization problems, combining a neural-guided reinforcement learning component with genetic programming. The neural-guided component seeds the starting population of a random-restart genetic programming algorithm and gradually learns better initial populations. On common benchmark tasks for recovering underlying expressions from datasets, the method recovers 65% more expressions than a recently published top-performing model under the same experimental setup. Experiments indicate that letting genetic programming run many generations with little dependence on the neural-guided component outperforms more tightly coupled formulations. The paper also introduces 22 new, more difficult symbolic regression benchmark problems and provides source code.
significance: The work shows that loosely coupling reinforcement learning with genetic programming can substantially improve expression recovery in symbolic regression, and the 22 new benchmark problems raise the difficulty standard for evaluating such methods, supporting further progress on discrete optimization tasks widely believed to be NP-hard.

aiRole.description: The authors introduce a hybrid neural-guided deep reinforcement learning and genetic programming method for symbolic regression that seeds random-restart genetic programming populations, and their system recovers 65% more expressions than a recently published top-performing model on common benchmark tasks.

humanContribution: Humans designed, built and trained the neural-guided and genetic programming components, curated the experimental benchmarks, and introduced a new set of 22 harder symbolic regression benchmark problems.

zh.title: 通过深度强化学习增强遗传编程播种的符号回归

zh.significance: 该研究表明，将强化学习与遗传编程松散耦合可显著提升符号回归中的表达式恢复能力，而 22 个新的基准问题提高了评估此类方法的难度标准，有助于推动这类被普遍认为是 NP 困难（NP-hard）的离散优化问题取得进一步进展。

title: Improving Math Word Problems with Pre-trained Knowledge and Hierarchical Reasoning
summary: The paper proposes RPKHS, a network for math word problems combining a pre-trained knowledge encoder that draws on outside knowledge from transformer-based pre-trained models with a hierarchical reasoning encoder that jointly performs word-level and sentence-level reasoning. Experiments show state-of-the-art results on Math23K and MAWPS, raising accuracy from 77.4% to 83.9% on Math23K, from 75.5% to 82.2% on Math23K under 5-fold cross-validation, and from 83.7% to 89.8% on MAWPS, with ablations supporting the method's effectiveness and interpretability.
significance: The work addresses two limitations of existing math word problem solvers, namely the neglect of outside knowledge and reasoning confined to word-level relationships. Its large reported accuracy gains on two widely used benchmarks suggest that injecting pre-trained knowledge and modeling hierarchical structure is a promising direction for improving automatic mathematical reasoning on natural language problems.

aiRole.description: The RPKHS network, combining a pre-trained knowledge encoder with a hierarchical reasoning encoder, reports benchmark accuracies of 83.9% on Math23K, 82.2% on Math23K with 5-fold cross-validation, and 89.8% on MAWPS, outperforming prior approaches.

humanContribution: Humans designed, built and trained the RPKHS model, curated the math word problem datasets, and ran the experiments and ablations that checked its effectiveness and interpretability.

title: Mathematical Word Problem Generation from Commonsense Knowledge Graph and Equations
summary: This work presents an end-to-end neural model for generating diverse mathematical word problems in real-world scenarios from a commonsense knowledge graph and symbolic equations. The model learns representations from edge-enhanced Levi graphs of both the equations and the commonsense knowledge, and a self-planning module automatically fuses the two information sources during generation. Experiments on an educational gold-standard set and a large-scale generated MWP set show the approach outperforming SOTA models on automatic metrics (BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, Self-BLEU) and human judgments of equation relevance, topic relevance, and language coherence. Code and the MWP dataset are released publicly.
significance: Generating word problems requires preserving the underlying mathematical operations while staying on topic, a combination that standard natural question generation does not handle. A model that fuses symbolic equations with commonsense knowledge could scale up the production of varied, contextually grounded assessment items, and the released code and dataset support reproducible follow-up work.

aiRole.description: The authors developed an end-to-end neural model that generates mathematical word problems from commonsense knowledge graphs and equations, outperforming SOTA models on BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, Self-BLEU and human evaluation metrics.

humanContribution: Humans designed, built and trained the neural model and its self-planning module, curated the educational gold-standard and generated MWP datasets, and conducted the automatic and human evaluations.

title: An Edge-Enhanced Hierarchical Graph-to-Tree Network for Math Word Problem Solving
summary: This paper proposes EEH-G2T, a neural model for math word problem solving that represents problems as edge-labeled graphs and encodes them with an edge-enhanced hierarchical graph encoder performing sentence-level and problem-level node aggregation. A tree-structured decoder with a split attention mechanism attends to different parts of the input problem during generation, and experiments on the MAWPS and Math23K datasets show improvements over state-of-the-art methods.
significance: Earlier graph neural network approaches largely ignored edge label information and long-range word relationships across sentences, and their generation process focused on the currently relevant region while neglecting the rest of the problem. EEH-G2T addresses both limitations, offering a stronger encoding of problem structure and broader attention during solution generation for automated math word problem solving.

aiRole.description: The authors propose EEH-G2T, an edge-enhanced hierarchical graph-to-tree neural model whose experiments on the MAWPS and Math23K datasets showed improved math word problem solving performance over state-of-the-art methods.

humanContribution: Humans designed and built the model architecture, including the edge-labeled graph encoder and tree-structured decoder, and evaluated it on curated benchmark datasets.

zh.title: 一种用于数学应用题求解的边增强层次化图到树网络
zh.summary: 本文提出用于数学应用题求解的神经模型 EEH-G2T，将应用题表示为带边标签的图，并采用边增强层次化图编码器，分句子层聚合与问题层聚合两步更新图节点。树结构解码器配合分裂注意力机制，在生成过程中关注输入题目的不同部分。在 MAWPS 和 Math23K 数据集上的实验表明，EEH-G2T 相比当前最优方法能有效提升性能。

zh.aiRoleDescription: 作者提出 EEH-G2T 模型，即一种边增强的层级式图到树神经网络模型，其在 MAWPS 和 Math23K 数据集上的实验表明，该模型在数学应用题求解性能上优于现有最好方法。

title: Generate & Rank: A Multi-task Framework for Math Word Problems
summary: The paper proposes Generate & Rank, a multi-task framework built on a generative pre-trained language model for math word problems (MWP). Alongside the usual generation objective, it introduces a ranking task that lets the model learn from its own mistakes and discriminate correct from incorrect mathematical expressions, supported by tree-based disturbance tailored to MWP and online updates to strengthen the ranker. The method consistently outperforms baselines across all evaluated datasets, improving accuracy on Math23k from 78.4% to 85.4%. Code is available at the huawei-noah/noah-research repository.
significance: Generation-only approaches are vulnerable to small errors in produced mathematical expressions, and this work shows that jointly training a ranker offers an effective corrective signal. The gains across all datasets and the 7-point improvement on the classical Math23k benchmark indicate strong practical value for automated math word problem solving.

aiRole.description: The Generate & Rank multi-task framework, built on a generative pre-trained language model, produces mathematical expressions for math word problems and outperforms baselines on all datasets, reaching 85.4% on Math23k versus 78.4% for the prior state-of-the-art.

humanContribution: Humans devised the ranking task and the Generate & Rank framework, designed tree-based disturbance and online update mechanisms, trained and evaluated the model, and compared it against baselines.

zh.title: Generate & Rank：面向数学应用题的多任务框架
zh.summary: 本文提出 Generate & Rank，一个建立在生成式预训练语言模型之上、面向数学应用题（math word problem, MWP）的多任务框架。除常规的生成目标外，该框架引入排序任务，使模型能从自身错误中学习，并区分正确与错误的数学表达式，同时配合专为 MWP 设计的树状扰动（tree-based disturbance）与在线更新来增强排序器。该方法在所有评测数据集上一致优于基线方法，在 Math23k 上将准确率从 78.4% 提升至 85.4%。代码见 huawei-noah/noah-research 仓库。
zh.significance: 仅采用生成目标的方法容易在产出的数学表达式中出现细小错误，本研究表明联合训练排序器可提供有效的纠错信号。该方法在所有数据集上均有提升，并在经典的 Math23k 基准上取得 7 个百分点的改进，对自动化数学应用题求解具有较强的实用价值。
zh.aiRoleDescription: 基于生成式预训练语言模型的 Generate & Rank 多任务框架可为数学应用题生成数学表达式，并在所有数据集上超越基线方法，在 Math23k 上达到 85.4%，高于此前最优的 78.4%。

title: Voting Theory in the Lean Theorem Prover
summary: The paper reports on a framework for formalizing voting theory in the Lean theorem prover, applied to verify properties of a recently studied voting method. It uses a variable-election setting with dependent types to express axioms about adding or removing candidates and voters, and aims to cover both impossibility theorems and method-specific properties such as Condorcet consistency and independence of clones.
significance: It broadens interactive theorem proving in social choice from impossibility results to verifying concrete voting methods, and the dependent-typed variable-election formalization gives a reusable way to state and check axioms about changes to the candidate and voter sets.

zh.title: Lean定理证明器中的投票理论
zh.summary: 本文报告了一个在Lean定理证明器中形式化投票理论（voting theory）的框架，并将其用于验证一种近期研究的投票方法的性质。该框架采用可变选举设定，借助依赖类型（dependent types）表达关于增加或删除候选人与选民的公理，目标是覆盖不可能性定理（impossibility theorems）以及特定投票方法的性质，例如孔多塞一致性（Condorcet consistency）和克隆独立性（independence of clones）。
zh.significance: 这项工作将交互式定理证明（interactive theorem proving）在社会选择理论（social choice theory）中的应用从不可能性定理扩展到对具体投票方法的验证；其中基于依赖类型（dependent types）的可变选举形式化为表达和检查候选人集合与选民集合变化的公理提供了可复用的基础。

title: Formalizing Geometric Algebra in Lean
summary: This paper reports on a formalization of Geometric (Clifford) algebras in the Lean 3 theorem prover, building on the mathlib library. Multivectors are constructed as a quotient of the tensor algebra by a suitable relation, which yields the ring structure automatically, and the universal property of the Clifford algebra is then established. The authors explain their approach with Lean source code, including a short introduction to Lean for readers new to theorem provers. Unlike existing formalizations of geometric algebra in other theorem provers, this approach does not require choosing a basis. Using the universal property alone, the paper defines involutions, versors, and the Z_2-grading, and recovers an induction principle suited to proving results about these definitions. It also outlines the remaining steps for the wedge product and the N-grading, together with current gaps in mathlib that make this work difficult.
significance: A basis-free, universal-property-based development gives geometric algebra a reusable and mathematically natural foundation inside a mainstream proof assistant, and the recovered induction principle makes the resulting definitions practically usable in proofs. The account of missing mathlib infrastructure also gives a concrete agenda for extending the library's support for graded algebraic structures.

zh.title: 在 Lean 中形式化几何代数
zh.summary: 本文介绍了在 Lean 3 定理证明器中对几何代数（Geometric algebra），即克利福德代数（Clifford algebra），进行形式化的工作，其基础是数学库 mathlib。作者将多重向量（multivector）构造为张量代数（tensor algebra）关于一个适当关系的商，从而自动获得环结构，随后建立了克利福德代数的泛性质（universal property）。论文通过 Lean 源代码阐述思路，并为从未接触过 Lean 或定理证明器的读者提供了简短的 Lean 语言介绍。与既有定理证明器中几何代数的形式化不同，该方法不需要选取基（basis）。作者仅利用泛性质即可定义对合（involution）、versor 以及 $\mathbb{Z}_2$-分次（$\mathbb{Z}_2$-grading），并从泛性质导出一个适用于证明这些定义相关命题的归纳原理（induction principle）。论文还概述了形式化楔积（wedge product）与 $\mathbb{N}$-分次（$\mathbb{N}$-grading）尚需完成的步骤，以及 mathlib 当前存在的、使这项工作具有挑战性的缺口。
zh.significance: 这种不依赖基、以泛性质为核心的发展，为几何代数在主流证明助手中提供了可复用且在数学上自然的基础，而所导出的归纳原理使这些定义在实际证明中切实可用。作者对 mathlib 缺失基础设施的梳理，也为扩展该库对分次代数结构的支持给出了具体工作方向。

title: Neural-Symbolic Solver for Math Word Problems with Auxiliary Tasks
summary: The paper proposes NS-Solver, a neural-symbolic framework for math word problems built from a problem reader, a programmer that generates symbolic equations, and a symbolic executor that produces answers. Beyond target expression supervision, it trains on four auxiliary objectives: self-supervised number prediction covering both quantity and location, commonsense constant prediction (e.g. how many legs a chicken has), a program consistency checker computing semantic loss between predicted and target equations, and a duality task pairing equation generation with part-of-speech generation. The authors also introduce CM17K, a benchmark of over 17K samples spanning arithmetic, one-unknown linear, one-unknown non-linear, and equation set problems. Experiments on Math23K and CM17K show gains over state-of-the-art methods.
significance: Explicitly injecting symbolic constraints through auxiliary tasks addresses the unexplainable and unreasonable predictions of pure encoder-decoder solvers, while the multi-level objectives target number handling, commonsense constants, equation semantics, and linguistic understanding. The CM17K benchmark additionally supplies a broader, more challenging testbed spanning four problem types, supporting work on universal and scalable solvers.

zh.summary: 论文提出 NS-Solver，一个用于数学应用题（math word problem）的神经符号框架，由问题阅读器、生成符号方程的程序员和输出答案的符号执行器组成。除目标表达式监督外，该方法还通过四个辅助目标进行训练：自监督数字预测（涵盖数字数量与数字位置）、常识常数预测（例如鸡有几条腿）、程序一致性检查器（计算预测方程与目标方程之间的语义损失），以及利用方程生成与词性生成之间拟对偶关系的对偶任务。作者还构建了 CM17K 基准，包含超过 17K 个样本，涵盖算术题、一元一次方程题、一元非线性方程题和方程组题四种类型。在 Math23K 和 CM17K 上的实验表明，该方法优于当前最优方法。
zh.significance: 通过辅助任务显式注入符号约束，可以应对纯编码器-解码器求解器产生的不可解释、不合理的预测，而多层次目标分别针对数字处理、常识常数、方程语义与语言理解。CM17K 基准还提供了覆盖四类问题、更具挑战性的测试环境，有助于研究通用且可扩展的求解器。

title: Sequence to General Tree: Knowledge-Guided Geometry Word Problem Solving
summary: The paper introduces sequence-to-general tree (S2G), a neural solver for geometry word problems that generates executable operation trees whose nodes may be mathematical formulas with an arbitrary number of arguments, rather than only binary expression trees built from basic operators. This design lets the model incorporate mathematical domain knowledge explicitly, producing shorter and more interpretable solutions. Experiments report that S2G outperforms strong baselines on problems requiring domain knowledge.
significance: Neural math word problem solvers typically encode a single formula as long chains of binary operators, obscuring meaning and limiting reuse of mathematical knowledge. S2G shows that allowing formula-level nodes yields more interpretable, executable reasoning and measurable gains on knowledge-intensive geometry problems, offering a useful direction for structured mathematical reasoning models.

aiRole.description: The paper introduces S2G, a neural solver that generates interpretable and executable general operation trees incorporating formula nodes, and reports that it outperforms strong baselines on geometry word problems requiring domain knowledge.

humanContribution: The authors designed, built, and trained the S2G model and its knowledge-guided formulation, and ran the experiments comparing it against baselines.

zh.title: 序列到通用树：知识引导的几何应用题求解

zh.significance: 神经网络数学应用题求解器通常用一长串二元运算符来编码单个公式，这既降低了可解释性，也限制了数学知识的复用。S2G 表明，允许公式级节点能带来更具可解释性、可执行的推理，并在知识密集型几何问题上取得可衡量的提升，为结构化数学推理模型提供了有价值的方向。
zh.aiRoleDescription: 论文提出神经求解器 S2G，能够生成包含公式节点、可解释且可执行的一般运算树，并报告其在需要领域知识的几何应用题上优于强基线。
zh.humanContribution: 作者设计、构建并训练了 S2G 模型及其知识引导的公式化方法，并进行了与基线的对比实验。

title: JEFL: Joint Embedding of Formal Proof Libraries
summary: JEFL is an unsupervised embedding method for retrieving similar mathematical concepts across interactive proof assistant libraries built on heterogeneous logical foundations. It builds on the fasttext implementation of Word2Vec and adds a tree traversal module to adapt the algorithm to the output format of the authors' data export pipeline. The paper compares this neural approach with a previously proposed algorithm for matching concepts across libraries along explainability, customizability, and online servability, and argues that the neural embedding approach has greater potential for integration into an interactive proof assistant.
significance: Concepts are developed in parallel across proof libraries grounded in different logical systems, and finding correspondences between them is a recurring obstacle for reuse and for AI-assisted formalization. A retrievable, servable embedding representation of library concepts could support discovery and cross-library search inside interactive provers, and the comparison with an earlier matching algorithm gives evidence about which design is practical to deploy.

aiRole.description: JEFL presents an unsupervised neural embedding approach, built on fasttext Word2Vec with an added tree traversal module, that retrieves similar mathematical concepts across interactive proof assistant libraries and is compared against a previously proposed concept-matching algorithm.

humanContribution: Humans designed the data export pipeline, implemented the tree traversal adaptation of the embedding algorithm, and evaluated and compared the approaches in terms of explainability, customizability, and online-servability.

title: Integrating an Automated Prover for Projective Geometry as a New Tactic in the Coq Proof Assistant
summary: The authors present an automated theorem prover for projective incidence geometry that uses a combinatorial matroid-based approach and proceeds by saturation with matroid rules. Implemented in C as a standalone tool, it takes a geometric configuration as input and emits Coq proof scripts, namely the expected theorem statement, a proof script establishing it, and possibly auxiliary lemmas. The document describes how to embed this external tool as a Coq plugin so that it can be invoked as a simple tactic.
significance: Connecting a specialized external prover to Coq as a tactic turns a standalone C program into an interactive automation step inside a proof assistant, letting formal users discharge projective incidence geometry goals without leaving Coq. This improves proof automation for this geometric field and offers a reusable pattern for wrapping external solvers as native tactics.

aiRole.description: The authors built an automated theorem prover for projective incidence geometry that, given a geometric configuration, outputs Coq proof scripts including the expected theorem statement, a proof of it, and possibly auxiliary lemmas. The paper shows how to embed this external C tool as a Coq tactic.

humanContribution: Humans developed the matroid-based saturation prover in C and integrated it as a plugin and tactic in the Coq proof assistant.

zh.significance: 将面向特定领域的外部证明器以策略形式接入 Coq，使一个独立的 C 程序成为证明助手内部可交互调用的自动化步骤，形式化用户无需离开 Coq 即可处理射影关联几何目标。这增强了该几何领域的证明自动化，也为把外部求解器封装为原生策略提供了可复用的模式。

title: Neural Symbolic Regression that scales
summary: The paper introduces the first symbolic regression method that leverages large-scale pre-training. The approach procedurally generates an unbounded set of equations and simultaneously pre-trains a Transformer to predict the symbolic equation underlying a set of input-output pairs. At test time, the model's output guides the search for the target equation. Experiments show the method re-discovers well-known physical equations and improves as more data and compute are added.
significance: Applying large-scale pre-training to symbolic regression turns equation discovery into a method that improves with experience rather than relying on fixed, hand-designed search strategies, strengthening the automation of recovering scientific laws from data.

aiRole.description: The paper introduces a Transformer-based symbolic regression system that, when queried on new input-output points, can re-discover well-known physical equations and improves with more data and compute.

humanContribution: Humans designed the method, procedurally generated the unbounded set of training equations, built and pre-trained the Transformer, and empirically evaluated its equation discovery results.

zh.title: 可扩展的神经符号回归

zh.significance: 将大规模预训练引入符号回归（symbolic regression），使方程发现方法不再依赖固定的人工设计策略，而是能够随经验积累不断改进，从而增强从数据中自动发现科学规律的能力。

title: Learning to Guide a Saturation-Based Theorem Prover
summary: TRAIL is a deep learning approach that recasts core elements of saturation-based theorem proving inside a neural framework: an effective graph neural network for representing logical formulas, a novel neural state representation built from processed clauses and available actions, and a novel attention-based action policy for inference selection. The authors report that these components let TRAIL significantly outperform previous reinforcement learning-based theorem provers on two standard benchmark datasets, proving up to 36% more theorems, and that it is the first reinforcement learning-based method to surpass a state-of-the-art traditional theorem prover on a standard benchmark, solving up to 17% more problems.
significance: The result indicates that learned guidance can replace manually tuned heuristics in saturation-based theorem proving and can even exceed the best traditional prover on established benchmarks, suggesting that neural inference selection is a practical route to stronger automated provers rather than only a complement to existing systems.

aiRole.description: The paper introduces TRAIL, a deep reinforcement learning approach to saturation-based theorem proving, which significantly outperforms prior RL-based provers on two standard benchmarks (up to 36% more theorems proved) and is reported as the first RL-based method to exceed a state-of-the-art traditional theorem prover…

humanContribution: The authors designed and built TRAIL's neural components, including a graph neural network for formulas and an attention-based action policy, and evaluated it on two standard benchmark datasets.

zh.title: 学习引导饱和式定理证明器

zh.significance: 这一结果表明，在基于饱和的定理证明中，学习得到的引导策略可以取代人工调校的启发式方法，甚至在既有基准上超过最强的传统定理证明器，说明神经化的推理选择是增强自动定理证明器的可行路径，而不只是现有系统的补充。
zh.aiRoleDescription: 论文提出 TRAIL，一种面向饱和式定理证明的深度强化学习方法，在两个标准基准上显著优于此前基于强化学习的证明器（最多多证明 36% 的定理），并被称为首个在标准定理证明基准上超过最先进的传统定理证明器的强化学习方法（最多多解决 17% 的问题）。
zh.humanContribution: 作者设计并构建了 TRAIL 的神经组件，包括用于表示逻辑公式的图神经网络和基于注意力的动作策略，并在两个标准基准数据集上对其进行了评估。

title: NaturalProofs: Mathematical Theorem Proving in Natural Language
summary: NaturalProofs is a multi-domain corpus of mathematical statements and their proofs written in natural mathematical language, unifying broad-coverage, deep-coverage, and low-resource sources to enable both in-distribution and zero-shot evaluation. On top of it the authors benchmark strong neural methods for mathematical reference retrieval and generation tasks that test a system's ability to identify key results appearing in a proof. Large-scale sequence models show promise relative to classical information retrieval methods, but their performance and out-of-domain generalization remain far from solved.
significance: The corpus and its benchmarks give the community a shared testbed for evaluating how well systems retrieve and generate the references that underpin mathematical proofs, spanning both rich and low-resource domains. The results expose clear gaps in generalization beyond the training distribution, pointing to concrete directions for improving machine reasoning over natural mathematical language.

title: Proof Artifact Co-training for Theorem Proving with Language Models
summary: PACT is a general method that extracts abundant self-supervised training data from kernel-level proof terms and co-trains it with the standard tactic prediction objective. Applied to Lean through a neural theorem prover driven by a Transformer language model, PACT improves success on a held-out set of test theorems from 32% to 48%.
significance: The work shows that proof artifacts already present in formal libraries can alleviate labeled-data scarcity for tactic prediction and yield substantial gains in automated theorem proving, offering a scalable data source for stronger formal reasoning systems.

title: A Formal Proof of the Independence of the Continuum Hypothesis
summary: The paper presents a formal proof in Lean of the independence of the continuum hypothesis. It develops forcing arguments through Boolean-valued models, using Cohen forcing to establish the consistency of not-CH and a sigma-closed forcing to establish the consistency of CH.
significance: This work brings one of set theory's central independence theorems into a machine-checked formal development, demonstrating that sophisticated Boolean-valued forcing constructions can be formalized in a general-purpose proof assistant and strengthening foundations for formalized set theory.

zh.title: 连续统假设独立性的形式化证明
zh.summary: 本文给出连续统假设（continuum hypothesis, CH）独立性在 Lean 中的形式化证明。研究者借助布尔值模型构造力迫法（forcing）论证：使用 Cohen forcing 建立非 CH 的相容性，并使用一种 σ-闭力迫建立 CH 的相容性。
zh.significance: 这项工作将集合论的核心独立性定理之一纳入机器检验的形式化发展之中，表明复杂的布尔值力迫构造能够在通用证明助手（proof assistant）中完成形式化，从而为形式化集合论奠定更坚实的基础。

title: A formalization of Dedekind domains and class groups of global fields
summary: This paper describes a formalization in Lean, developed within mathlib, of Dedekind domains and class groups of global fields together with fundamental properties such as number-theoretic finiteness results for class groups. It presents useful development idioms and discusses mathlib's decentralized collaborative processes.
significance: The work provides machine-checked foundations for core commutative algebra and algebraic number theory notions in mathlib, making results on class groups reusable in verified mathematics. Its account of idioms and collaboration can guide future large-scale formalization projects.

zh.title: 整体域的戴德金整环与类群的形式化
zh.summary: 本文介绍了在 mathlib 中使用 Lean 证明器完成的形式化工作，内容包括戴德金整环（Dedekind domains）与整体域（global fields）的类群（class groups），以及类群的数论有限性等基本性质。文章总结了开发中有用的表述方法，并讨论了 mathlib 的去中心化协作流程。
zh.significance: 这项工作为 mathlib 中交换代数（commutative algebra）与代数数论（algebraic number theory）的核心概念提供了机器验证的基础，使类群相关结果可以在经过验证的数学中重复使用。文中对表述方法和协作经验的总结，也可为今后的大规模形式化项目提供参考。

title: An Automated Theorem Proving Framework for Information-Theoretic Results
summary: The paper presents a versatile automated theorem proving framework that, within a single setting, discovers, simplifies, and proves inner and outer bounds in network information theory, deduces properties of information-theoretic quantities such as Wyner and Gács-Körner common information, and discovers non-Shannon-type inequalities. The implementation generated proofs for 32 of the 56 theorems in Chapters 1-14 of Network Information Theory by El Gamal and Kim. The framework is founded on the concept of existential information inequalities, which offers an axiomatic basis for a wide range of problems in information theory.
significance: The work shows that automated theorem proving can deliver machine-generated proofs for central results in network information theory, handling bound derivation, common information, and non-Shannon-type inequality discovery in one pipeline. Successful coverage of a large share of theorems from a standard reference text suggests the approach can scale and support the systematic exploration of information-theoretic inequalities and bounds.

aiRole.description: The authors present an automated theorem proving framework that generated proofs for 32 of 56 theorems from El Gamal and Kim's Network Information Theory, and can discover bounds, deduce properties of information-theoretic quantities, and find non-Shannon-type inequalities.

humanContribution: The researchers built and implemented the framework, designed its axiomatic basis of existential information inequalities, and selected the 56 book theorems used for evaluation.

zh.title: 面向信息论结果的自动定理证明框架
zh.summary: 本文提出了一个通用的自动定理证明框架，可在统一的设定下自动发现、简化并证明网络信息论（network information theory）中的内界与外界，推导信息论量（如 Wyner 与 Gács-Körner 公共信息）的性质，并发现非香农型不等式（non-Shannon-type inequalities）。该实现成功为 El Gamal 与 Kim 所著《Network Information Theory》第1至14章的56个定理中的32个生成了证明。框架建立在存在信息不等式（existential information inequalities）的概念之上，为信息论中的广泛问题提供了公理化基础。
zh.significance: 该工作表明，自动定理证明可以为网络信息论的核心结果生成机器证明，并在统一的流程中处理界推导、公共信息以及非香农型不等式发现等任务。在一部标准参考著作的大量定理上取得较高覆盖率，说明该方法具备可扩展性，有望支持对信息论不等式与界的系统化探索。
zh.aiRoleDescription: 作者提出了一个自动定理证明框架，为 El Gamal 与 Kim 所著 Network Information Theory 中 56 条定理里的 32 条生成了证明，并能发现界、推导信息论量的性质以及发现非 Shannon 型不等式。
zh.humanContribution: 研究者构建并实现了该框架，设计了其基于 existential information inequalities 的公理化基础，并选取了用于评估的 56 条书中定理。

title: A Study of Continuous Vector Representationsfor Theorem Proving
summary: This paper develops a dense vector encoding of mathematical formulas that preserves syntactic and semantic logical properties and is reversible, so the full tree structure with all symbols can be reconstructed from the vector. Reconstruction is achieved with two decoders, one predicting the tree's top symbol and another recovering subtree embedding vectors, with target properties including structural features, natural deduction step applicability, and unifiability. The authors propose training datasets covering these properties and evaluate the encoding on them and on premise selection in the Mizar corpus.
significance: Reversible formula encodings that retain logical structure could let neural models manipulate formulas with greater fidelity, bridging vector representations and symbolic reasoning. Evaluation on premise selection for Mizar indicates practical relevance to theorem proving tools, where relevant-lemma retrieval is a key bottleneck.

aiRole.description: The authors develop a reversible dense vector encoding of mathematical formulas that preserves structural and logical properties such as natural deduction applicability and unifiability, trained via two decoders, and evaluate it on proposed datasets and on premise selection in the Mizar corpus.

humanContribution: Humans designed the encoding and its two decoders, trained the models, proposed the training datasets, and set up the evaluation including Mizar premise selection.

zh.title: 定理证明（theorem proving）中连续向量表示的研究
zh.summary: 本文提出一种数学公式的稠密向量编码，可保留语法与语义逻辑性质，并且可逆，即从向量中可以重建包含全部符号的完整树形结构。该方法训练两个解码器，一个预测树的顶层符号（top symbol），另一个恢复子树的嵌入向量（subtree embedding vectors），所针对的性质包括结构特征、自然演绎（natural deduction）步骤的适用性，以及更复杂的可合一性（unifiability）。作者提出覆盖这些性质的训练数据集，并在这些数据集以及 Mizar 语料库中的前提选择（premise selection）任务上评估了该编码的可行性。
zh.significance: 保留逻辑结构的可逆公式编码能够让神经网络模型更忠实地处理公式，从而连接向量表示与符号推理。在 Mizar 的前提选择任务上的评估表明，该工作与定理证明工具具有实际关联，而相关引理的检索正是其中的关键瓶颈。
zh.aiRoleDescription: 作者开发了一种可逆的公式稠密向量编码，能保留结构与逻辑性质（如自然演绎步骤的适用性和可合一性），通过两个解码器训练，并在自建数据集及 Mizar 语料库的引理选择任务上进行了评估。
zh.humanContribution: 人类设计了该编码及其两个解码器，训练了模型，构建了训练数据集，并搭建了包括 Mizar 引理选择在内的评测流程。

title: Formalizing Hall's Marriage Theorem in Lean
summary: The authors formalize Hall's Marriage Theorem in the Lean theorem prover for inclusion in mathlib, a community-driven unified mathematics library for Lean aimed at covering a complete undergraduate mathematics curriculum. They present the main theorem in three forms: for indexed families of finite sets, for relations on types, and for matchings in bipartite graphs. They also formalize a version of Kőnig's lemma phrased via inverse limits to extend the result to countably infinite index sets, describe the design of the recent mathlib simple graph library, and give a necessary and sufficient condition for a simple graph to carry a function.
significance: The work adds a classic combinatorial result to mathlib in several equivalent formulations, supporting both graph-theoretic and relation-theoretic uses, and pushes the statement from finite to countably infinite index sets. The account of the simple graph library design and the stated necessary and sufficient condition give reusable infrastructure and insights for further formalized discrete mathematics in Lean.

zh.title: 在 Lean 中形式化 Hall 婚姻定理
zh.summary: 作者在 Lean 证明器中形式化了 Hall 婚姻定理（Hall's Marriage Theorem），并计划纳入 mathlib——一个由社区驱动、面向 Lean 的统一数学库，目标是覆盖完整的本科数学教育内容。他们给出主定理的三种表述：有限集的索引族、类型上的关系，以及二分图中的匹配。此外，作者还形式化了一个以逆极限（inverse limits）表述的 Kőnig 引理（Kőnig's lemma）版本，以便将定理推广到可数无穷索引集的情形，并介绍了近期 mathlib 简单图库的设计，还给出了一个简单图承载函数的充要条件。
zh.significance: 该项工作以多种等价表述将经典组合数学结果加入 mathlib，同时支持图论与关系论的使用，并把定理从有限索引集推进到可数无穷索引集。关于简单图库设计的说明与所给充要条件，为在 Lean 中进一步形式化离散数学提供了可复用的基础设施与经验。

title: Formalization of PAL$\cdot$S5 in Proof Assistant
summary: Researchers formalize the model and proof system for multi-agent modal logic S5 with a PAL-style dynamic modality in the Lean theorem prover, as an experiment in applying proof assistants to logic research. They give a formal proof of the reduction axiom for public announcement and of the soundness and completeness of modal logic S5, all typecheckable with Lean 3.19.0. The complete proof is available on Github.
significance: The work demonstrates that a proof assistant can serve as experimental infrastructure for logic research, turning key metatheoretic results — the public announcement reduction axiom and soundness and completeness — into machine-checked proofs. Typechecking with Lean 3.19.0 and a public Github artifact make the verification reproducible and reusable by others working on dynamic and epistemic logics.

zh.title: 在证明助手中形式化 PAL·S5
zh.summary: 研究者作为将证明助手应用于逻辑研究的一次实验，在 Lean 定理证明器中形式化了带 PAL 式动态模态（PAL-style dynamic modality）的多主体模态逻辑 S5（multi-agent modal logic S5）的模型与证明系统。研究者给出了公共公告的归约公理（reduction axiom）以及模态逻辑 S5 的可靠性（soundness）与完全性（completeness）的形式化证明，全部可通过 Lean 3.19.0 类型检查。完整证明已在 Github 上公开。
zh.significance: 这项工作表明，证明助手可以作为逻辑研究的实验基础设施，把公共公告归约公理以及可靠性与完全性等关键元理论结果转化为可机器检验的证明。借助 Lean 3.19.0 的类型检查与公开的 Github 证明材料，验证过程可复现，也可供从事动态逻辑与认知逻辑的研究者复用。

title: A Novice-Friendly Induction Tactic for Lean
summary: This paper presents a new induction tactic implemented in Lean 3 that improves the ergonomics of proof scripts in dependent type theory provers such as Coq and Lean. The tactic reliably supports inductive predicates and relations, generates more useful induction hypotheses, and introduces hypotheses under clearer names. It is aimed at educational use while also being convenient for experts, and its implementation serves as a moderately complex case study of Lean 3's metaprogramming framework, documenting difficulties encountered and suggesting framework improvements.
significance: Induction is ubiquitous in dependent type theory proofs, so improving the reliability and readability of induction tactics benefits both learners and experienced users of Lean and Coq. The work also provides practical feedback on Lean 3 metaprogramming, highlighting pain points that can inform the design of future tactic frameworks.

zh.title: 一种面向新手的 Lean 归纳策略
zh.summary: 本文提出一种在 Lean 3 中实现的新型归纳策略（induction tactic），用于改善依赖类型论（dependent type theory）证明器（如 Coq 与 Lean）中证明脚本的使用体验。该策略可靠地支持归纳谓词与归纳关系，生成更有用的归纳假设（induction hypotheses），并为引入的假设选取更清晰的名称。它既适合教学场景，也为专家提供了更便捷的选择；其实现还构成了对 Lean 3 元编程框架的一项中等复杂度案例研究，作者记录了开发过程中遇到的困难并提出了框架改进建议。
zh.significance: 归纳法（induction）在依赖类型论证明中无处不在，因此提升归纳策略的可靠性与可读性，既能帮助学习者，也能改善 Lean 与 Coq 资深用户的证明工作流。该工作还为 Lean 3 元编程提供了实践反馈，指出了使用中的痛点，可为未来策略框架的设计提供参考。
